chapters.title: Come, Let Us Settle This
chapters.html:
Isaiah 1

1The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

The Rebel Sons

2Hear, heavens, and give ear, earth,
for the LORD has spoken:
"Sons I have raised and brought up,
but they have rebelled against Me.

3The ox knows its owner,
and the donkey its master's manger;
Israel does not know,
My people do not understand."

4Woe, sinful nation,
a people heavy with iniquity,
offspring of evildoers,
sons who deal corruptly!
They have forsaken the LORD,
they have spurned the Holy One of Israel,
they have turned their backs on Him.

5Where will you be struck again,
as you keep on rebelling?
The whole head is sick,
and the whole heart faint.

6From the sole of the foot to the head
there is no soundness in it:
bruises and welts and raw wounds,
not pressed out, not bound up,
not softened with oil.

7Your land is a desolation,
your cities are burned with fire;
your soil — strangers devour it before your eyes,
and it is a desolation, like an overthrow by strangers.

8The daughter of Zion is left
like a shelter in a vineyard,
like a hut in a cucumber field,
like a city under siege.

9Unless the LORD of hosts
had left us a few survivors,
we would have been like Sodom,
we would have resembled Gomorrah.

Your Sacrifices

10Hear the word of the LORD,
you rulers of Sodom!
Give ear to the instruction of our God,
you people of Gomorrah!

11"What are your many sacrifices to Me?"
says the LORD.
"I have had my fill of burnt offerings of rams
and the fat of fattened animals;
I take no delight in the blood of bulls,
of lambs or of goats.

12When you come to appear before My face,
who asked this of you,
this trampling of My courts?

13Bring no more empty offerings;
incense is a detestable thing to Me.
New moon and sabbath, the calling of assemblies —
I cannot bear iniquity with the sacred assembly.

14Your new moons and your appointed feasts
My soul hates;
they have become a burden to Me;
I am weary of bearing them.

15When you spread out your hands,
I will hide My eyes from you;
even when you make many prayers,
I am not listening.
Your hands are full of blood.

16Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean;
remove the evil of your deeds from before My eyes;
stop doing evil.

17Learn to do good;
seek justice;
set the oppressor right;
defend the orphan;
plead for the widow."

Come, Let Us Settle This

18"Come now, let us settle this,"
says the LORD:
"Though your sins are like scarlet,
they shall be white as snow;
though they are red like crimson,
they shall become like wool.

19If you are willing and listen,
you shall eat the good of the land;

20but if you refuse and rebel,
you shall be eaten by the sword";
for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.

The Faithful City

21How the faithful city
has become a prostitute!
She was full of justice;
righteousness lodged in her,
but now murderers.

22Your silver has become dross,
your wine is cut with water.

23Your rulers are rebels
and companions of thieves.
Every one of them loves a bribe
and runs after payoffs.
They do not defend the orphan,
and the widow's case never comes before them.

24Therefore the Lord, the LORD of hosts,
the Mighty One of Israel, declares:
"Ah, I will get relief from My foes,
and avenge Myself on My enemies.

25I will turn My hand against you;
I will smelt away your dross as with lye,
and remove all your alloy.

26I will restore your judges as at the first,
and your counselors as at the beginning.
After this you shall be called
the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City."

27Zion shall be redeemed by justice,
and those in her who return, by righteousness.

28But rebels and sinners shall be broken together,
and those who forsake the LORD shall come to an end.

29For they shall be ashamed of the oaks
that you desired,
and you shall blush for the gardens
that you chose.

30For you shall be like an oak
whose leaf withers,
and like a garden that has no water.

31The strong one shall become tinder,
and his work a spark;
both shall burn together,
with no one to quench them.

Notes

  • v1 "Isaiah son of Amoz" — Yesha'yahu, "the LORD saves," from yasha, "save," the root of Joshua's name. The prophet's name says what the book will say.

  • v2 "Hear, heavens, and give ear, earth" — the two witnesses of the Song of Moses, Give ear, heavens, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth (Deuteronomy 32:1), with the verbs reversed. The chapter is a lawsuit: the witnesses are called (v2), the charge is laid (vv2–9), the plea is rejected (vv10–15), and the LORD offers terms (v18, let us settle this, nivvakhechah, the word for arguing a case).

  • v4 "the Holy One of Israel" — qedosh Yisrael, Isaiah's own name for God: twenty-four times in this book, and only six times in the rest of the Hebrew Bible (three in the Psalms, two in Jeremiah, and 2 Kings 19:22, which is Isaiah speaking).

  • vv5–6 "Where will you be struck again" — al meh tukku od can be "Why will you be struck again?" or "On what will you be struck again?" The next line answers the second: from the sole of the foot to the head there is no soundness. There is no unbruised place left to strike.

  • vv7–10 "like an overthrow by strangers… like Sodom… you rulers of Sodom" — mahpekhah, "overthrow," is used everywhere else of the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah (Deuteronomy 29:23; Isaiah 13:19; Jeremiah 49:18; 50:40; Amos 4:11). In v9 the survivors say they would have been like Sodom; in v10 the prophet calls them Sodom. Paul quotes v9 from the Greek, which has a seed for "survivors" (Romans 9:29).

  • v12 "to appear before My face" — lera'ot panai, as in Exodus 34:24, to appear before the face of the LORD your God three times in the year. The pilgrim feasts God commanded, He now calls trampling of My courts. What He rejects is not the rite but the hands that bring it: Your hands are full of blood (v15).

  • v17 "set the oppressor right" — ashsheru chamots. Chamots is found only here: "the ruthless one," whom the people are to correct, or "the oppressed," whom they are to relieve. The verb means to set straight.

  • v18 "Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be white as snow" — im yihyu chata'eikhem kashshanim kashsheleg yalbinu, "if your sins are like scarlet, as snow they will be white." It can be read as the promise it has always been taken to be, or as the question of a judge: "if your sins are scarlet, are they to pass for white?" Verses 19–20 set the terms either way.

  • vv19–20 "you shall eat… you shall be eaten" — tokhelu… te'ukkelu, the same verb active and passive: eat the land's good, or be eaten by the sword.

  • vv21, 26 "the faithful city" — qiryah ne'emanah opens the lament and closes the promise: what she was, she will be called again. "The oaks… the gardens" (vv29–30): places of other worship, as later in the book, sacrificing in the gardens (65:3) and burning with lust among the oaks (57:5). Eilim, "oaks," is spelled as eilim, "rams," the burnt offerings of v11.

chapters.title: The Mountain of the LORD and the Day of the LORD
chapters.html:
Isaiah 2

1The word that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

The Mountain of the LORD

2And it shall come to pass in the last days
that the mountain of the LORD's house
shall be established as the highest of the mountains,
and shall be lifted up above the hills;
and all the nations shall stream to it.

3Many peoples shall go and say,
"Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD,
to the house of the God of Jacob,
that He may teach us His ways,
and that we may walk in His paths."
For out of Zion shall go forth instruction,
and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

4He shall judge between the nations,
and decide for many peoples;
they shall beat their swords into plowshares,
and their spears into pruning hooks;
nation shall not lift up sword against nation,
nor shall they learn war anymore.

5House of Jacob,
come, let us walk in the light of the LORD.

The Day of the LORD

6For You have forsaken Your people,
the house of Jacob,
because they are full of what comes from the east,
and of fortune-tellers like the Philistines,
and they strike hands with the children of foreigners.

7Their land is filled with silver and gold,
and there is no end to their treasures;
their land is filled with horses,
and there is no end to their chariots.

8Their land is filled with idols;
they bow down to the work of their hands,
to what their own fingers have made.

9So man is humbled,
and each one brought low —
do not forgive them!

10Go into the rock,
and hide in the dust,
from the terror of the LORD
and the splendor of His majesty.

11The haughty eyes of man shall be brought low,
and the pride of men shall be humbled,
and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day.

12For the LORD of hosts has a day
against all that is proud and lofty,
against all that is lifted up — and it shall be brought low;

13against all the cedars of Lebanon,
lofty and lifted up,
and against all the oaks of Bashan;

14against all the lofty mountains,
and against all the hills that are lifted up;

15against every high tower,
and against every fortified wall;

16against all the ships of Tarshish,
and against all the beautiful craft.

17The haughtiness of man shall be humbled,
and the pride of men brought low,
and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day.

18The idols shall utterly pass away.

19Men shall go into the caves of the rocks
and into the holes of the ground,
from the terror of the LORD
and the splendor of His majesty,
when He rises to make the earth tremble.

20In that day man will throw away
his idols of silver and his idols of gold,
which they made for him to bow down to,
to the moles and to the bats,

21to go into the clefts of the rocks
and the crevices of the crags,
from the terror of the LORD
and the splendor of His majesty,
when He rises to make the earth tremble.

22Stop trusting in man,
who has only breath in his nostrils;
for of what account is he?

Notes

  • v1 "The word that Isaiah… saw" — ha-davar asher chazah: a word that is seen, as the book's title calls the whole a vision (1:1).

  • vv2–4 "the mountain of the LORD's house… all the nations shall stream to it" — naharu, "flow like a river": the nations run uphill to a mountain. The same oracle stands, with small differences, in Micah 4:1–3.

  • v3 "that He may teach us… instruction" — yorenu… torah: the verb and the noun are one root, yarah, "to point the way." What goes out from Zion is what the LORD teaches.

  • v4 "He shall judge… and decide" — ve-hokhiach, the verb of 1:18, let us settle this: the case the LORD offered Judah, He will settle for the nations. "Swords into plowshares" — Joel turns the words around for the day of battle: Beat your plowshares into swords (Joel 3:10, Hebrew 4:10).

  • vv7–8 "silver and gold… horses… idols" — the three things the law forbade a king to multiply, he shall not multiply horses… and silver and gold he shall not greatly multiply (Deuteronomy 17:16–17), and the third is the end of it. "Idols" — elilim, "nothings," a mocking twin of elohim, "God."

  • v9 "do not forgive them!" — ve-al tissa lahem, "and do not lift [it] from them": nasa, "lift," is the verb of forgiving, as in lift the offense of your brothers (Genesis 50:17). The prophet's own cry breaks into the oracle.

  • vv10–21 "from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty" — a refrain three times (vv10, 19, 21); and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day twice (vv11, 17). The day of the LORD is a day against everything high: cedars, oaks, mountains, towers, walls, ships.

  • v19 "when He rises to make the earth tremble" — la'arots ha-arets, a play of sounds: to terrify the terrain.

  • v22 "who has only breath in his nostrils" — neshamah be-appo, the breath God blew into the first man's nostrils (Genesis 2:7): what man has is lent.

chapters.title: Judgment on Jerusalem and the Daughters of Zion
chapters.html:
Isaiah 3

1For the Lord, the LORD of hosts,
is about to take away from Jerusalem and from Judah
every prop and support:
all support of bread,
and all support of water;

2the mighty man and the man of war,
the judge and the prophet,
the diviner and the elder,

3the captain of fifty and the man of rank,
the counselor and the skilled craftsman,
and the expert in charms.

4I will make boys their princes,
and whims shall rule over them.

5The people will oppress one another,
each man his fellow and each his neighbor;
the youth will be insolent to the elder,
and the despised to the honored.

6When a man takes hold of his brother
in his father's house:
"You have a cloak; you shall be our ruler,
and this heap of ruins shall be in your charge,"

7in that day he will cry out:
"I will not be a healer;
in my house there is neither bread nor cloak;
you shall not make me ruler of the people."

8For Jerusalem has stumbled,
and Judah has fallen,
because their speech and their deeds are against the LORD,
defying His glorious presence.

9The look on their faces testifies against them;
they declare their sin like Sodom;
they do not hide it.
Woe to them!
For they have brought evil on themselves.

10Tell the righteous that it shall be well with them,
for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds.

11Woe to the wicked! It shall go badly with him,
for what his hands have done shall be done to him.

12My people — their oppressors are children,
and women rule over them.
My people, those who guide you lead you astray,
and have swallowed up the way of your paths.

13The LORD has taken His place to contend;
He stands to judge the peoples.

14The LORD will enter into judgment
with the elders of His people and their princes:
"It is you who have devoured the vineyard;
the plunder of the poor is in your houses.

15What do you mean by crushing My people,
and grinding the faces of the poor?"
declares the Lord GOD of hosts.

16The LORD said:
Because the daughters of Zion are haughty,
and walk with outstretched necks,
glancing with their eyes,
walking with mincing steps,
and jingling with their feet,

17the Lord will strike with scabs
the heads of the daughters of Zion,
and the LORD will lay bare their foreheads.

18In that day the Lord will take away the finery of the anklets, the headbands and the crescents,

19the pendants, the bracelets and the veils,

20the headdresses, the armlets, the sashes, the perfume boxes and the amulets,

21the signet rings and the nose rings,

22the festal robes, the mantles, the cloaks and the purses,

23the mirrors, the linen garments, the turbans and the shawls.

24Instead of perfume there will be rot;
instead of a sash, a rope;
instead of well-set hair, baldness;
instead of a rich robe, a girding of sackcloth;
branding instead of beauty.

25Your men shall fall by the sword,
and your mighty ones in battle.

26Her gates shall lament and mourn;
and emptied, she shall sit on the ground.

Notes

  • v1 "every prop and support" — mash'en u-mash'enah, the same word in its masculine and feminine forms: every kind of support. The list that follows (vv2–3) names what Judah leaned on, and puts the diviner and the expert in charms beside the judge and the prophet.

  • v4 "whims shall rule over them" — ta'alulim, "caprices" or "childishness": the rulers are boys, and what rules is their whim.

  • vv6–7 "I will not be a healer" — chovesh, "one who binds up," the verb of 1:6, not bound up: no one will take on the wounds of the city. He has a cloak, and that is enough to be offered the throne.

  • v9 "they declare their sin like Sodom" — the third time Sodom is named (1:9, 10).

  • v12 "their oppressors are children, and women rule over them" — me'olel… nashim, as the Hebrew is pointed. The same letters can be read me'olel, "gleaning," and noshim, "creditors," and that is how the Greek takes them: your exactors glean you, and the creditors rule over you (hoi apaitountes). The pointing makes the line continue v4, the rule of boys.

  • vv13–14 "The LORD has taken His place to contend… It is you who have devoured the vineyard" — la-riv, the lawsuit of chapter 1 again. Bi'artem, "you have grazed off" or "burned," is the word the vineyard song uses for what will happen to the vineyard (5:5, it shall be grazed bare); the song itself follows two chapters on.

  • v17 "lay bare their foreheads" — pothen ye'areh. Pot is rare and uncertain: "their foreheads" (where the hair is shaved), or "their private parts" (shame by stripping). Both fit the verse; the text here reads the first, after the heads in the line before.

  • vv18–23 "the anklets, the headbands and the crescents…" — twenty-one items of finery. Several words are found only here, and their exact meaning is guessed from the setting and from related words. The crescents are the moon-shaped ornaments Gideon took from the camels of Midian (Judges 8:21).

  • v24 "branding instead of beauty" — ki tachat yofi, where ki is read as a noun, "a burn": the brand of a captive. Every line of the verse is a reversal of vv18–23.

chapters.title: The Branch of the LORD
chapters.html:
Isaiah 4

1In that day seven women will take hold of one man, saying, "We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothing; only let us be called by your name; take away our disgrace."

2In that day the branch of the LORD shall be beautiful and glorious,
and the fruit of the land shall be the pride and splendor
of the survivors of Israel.

3Whoever is left in Zion
and remains in Jerusalem will be called holy,
everyone who is recorded for life in Jerusalem,

4when the Lord has washed away
the filth of the daughters of Zion,
and rinsed the bloodstains of Jerusalem from within her
by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

5Then the LORD will create
over the whole site of Mount Zion and over her assemblies
a cloud by day, and smoke,
and the shining of a flaming fire by night;
for over all the glory there will be a canopy.

6There will be a shelter for shade from the heat by day,
and a refuge and a hiding place from storm and rain.

Notes

  • v1 "seven women will take hold of one man" — the aftermath of 3:25, your men shall fall by the sword. To be called by your name is to be married; the disgrace is to be left unmarried and childless.

  • v2 "the branch of the LORD" — tsemach YHWH, "what the LORD makes sprout." Set beside the fruit of the land, it reads as the growth God gives to the land after the judgment. Elsewhere tsemach becomes a title for the promised king: I will raise up for David a righteous Branch (Jeremiah 23:5), My servant the Branch (Zechariah 3:8). Here it stands lowercase, in step with the fruit of the land.

  • v3 "everyone who is recorded for life" — ha-katuv la-chayyim, "written for life": the book of Exodus 32:32, blot me out, please, from Your book that You have written, and Psalm 69:28, the book of the living.

  • v4 "a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning" — ruach, also "wind": the cleansing is by judgment and by fire, as metal is refined (1:25).

  • v5 "the LORD will create… a cloud by day… a flaming fire by night" — bara, the verb of Genesis 1:1, used only with God as subject; and the pillar of the exodus, by day in a pillar of cloud… and by night in a pillar of fire (Exodus 13:21), now resting over all of Mount Zion.

  • v5 "over all the glory there will be a canopy" — chuppah, the bride's canopy; Psalm 19:5 uses the word for the bridegroom's chamber.

  • v6 "There will be a shelter" — sukkah: in 1:8 the daughter of Zion was left like a shelter in a vineyard, a flimsy booth; here the LORD's shelter covers the whole city.

speech.text: Isaiah 4
In that day seven women will take hold of one man, saying, "We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothing; only let us be called by your name; take away our disgrace."
In that day the branch of the LORD shall be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land shall be the pride and splendor of the survivors of Israel.
Whoever is left in Zion and remains in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone who is recorded for life in Jerusalem,
when the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and rinsed the bloodstains of Jerusalem from within her by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

Then the LORD will create over the whole site of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day, and smoke, and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory there will be a canopy.
There will be a shelter for shade from the heat by day, and a refuge and a hiding place from storm and rain.

chapters.title: The Song of the Vineyard
chapters.html:
Isaiah 5

The Song of the Vineyard

1Let me sing for my beloved
my love song about his vineyard:
My beloved had a vineyard
on a very fertile hill.

2He dug it and cleared it of stones,
and planted it with choice vines;
he built a watchtower in the middle of it,
and also hewed out a winepress in it;
and he looked for it to yield grapes,
but it yielded rotten grapes.

3So now, inhabitants of Jerusalem
and men of Judah,
judge between me and my vineyard.

4What more was there to do for my vineyard
that I have not done in it?
Why, when I looked for it to yield grapes,
did it yield rotten grapes?

5And now, let me tell you
what I am about to do to my vineyard:
I will remove its hedge,
and it shall be grazed bare;
I will break down its wall,
and it shall be trampled.

6I will make it a waste;
it shall not be pruned or hoed,
and briers and thorns shall come up;
I will also command the clouds
to send no rain upon it.

7For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts
is the house of Israel,
and the men of Judah
are the planting He delighted in;
He looked for justice,
but there was bloodshed;
for righteousness,
but there was a cry.

Six Woes

8Woe to those who join house to house,
who add field to field,
until there is no room left,
and you are made to dwell alone in the middle of the land!

9In my hearing the LORD of hosts has sworn:
Surely many houses shall be desolate,
large and fine ones, without inhabitant.

10For ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath,
and a homer of seed shall yield an ephah.

11Woe to those who rise early in the morning
to chase strong drink,
who stay late into the evening
as wine inflames them!

12They have lyre and harp,
tambourine and flute and wine at their feasts,
but they do not regard the deeds of the LORD,
or see the work of His hands.

13Therefore My people go into exile
for lack of knowledge;
their honored men are starving,
and their multitude is parched with thirst.

14Therefore Sheol has opened wide its throat,
and opened its mouth beyond measure;
and down go her splendor and her multitude,
her din, and whoever exults in her.

15So man is humbled,
and each one brought low,
and the eyes of the haughty are brought low.

16But the LORD of hosts is exalted in justice,
and the holy God is shown holy in righteousness.

17Lambs shall graze as in their pasture,
and guests shall eat among the ruins of the fat ones.

18Woe to those who drag iniquity with cords of falsehood,
and sin as with cart ropes,

19who say, "Let Him hurry,
let Him speed His work, so that we may see it;
let the plan of the Holy One of Israel
draw near and come, so that we may know it!"

20Woe to those who call evil good
and good evil,
who put darkness for light
and light for darkness,
who put bitter for sweet
and sweet for bitter!

21Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes,
and clever in their own sight!

22Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine,
and valiant men at mixing strong drink,

23who acquit the guilty for a bribe,
and take from the righteous what is right!

24Therefore, as the tongue of fire devours the stubble,
and dry grass sinks down in the flame,
so their root will be like rot,
and their blossom will go up like dust;
for they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of hosts,
and spurned the word of the Holy One of Israel.

25Therefore the anger of the LORD burned against His people,
and He stretched out His hand against them and struck them;
the mountains quaked,
and their corpses were like refuse in the middle of the streets.
For all this His anger has not turned away,
and His hand is still stretched out.

The Nation from Afar

26He will raise a signal for nations far away,
and whistle for them from the end of the earth;
swiftly, speedily they come!

27None of them is weary, none stumbles;
none slumbers or sleeps;
not a waistband is loosened,
not a sandal strap broken.

28Their arrows are sharp,
all their bows are bent;
their horses' hooves are counted as flint,
and their wheels as the whirlwind.

29Their roar is like a lioness;
they roar like young lions;
they growl and seize the prey,
and carry it off, and no one can rescue.

30They will growl over it in that day
like the growling of the sea;
and if one looks to the land:
darkness and distress,
and the light darkened by its clouds.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "my beloved… my love song… on a very fertile hill" — yedidi… shirat dodi, the language of the Song of Songs; the prophet sings as the friend of the bridegroom. The hill is qeren ben shamen, "a horn, son of oil": a hilltop of rich soil.

  • vv2, 4 "rotten grapes" — be'ushim, from ba'ash, "to stink": not wild grapes but grapes gone bad on the vine, after every care.

  • vv3–6 "judge between me and my vineyard" — the hearers are made the judges of a case they do not yet know is their own, as Nathan made David judge in the story of the ewe lamb, You are the man! (2 Samuel 12:7). The owner is still a man in the song; only in v6, I will command the clouds to send no rain, does the speaker show who He is, and v7 names Him.

  • v5 "it shall be grazed bare… it shall be trampled" — le-va'er… le-mirmas: the verb of 3:14, you have devoured the vineyard, and the noun of 1:12, this trampling of My courts.

  • v7 "He looked for justice, but there was bloodshed; for righteousness, but there was a cry" — mishpat… mispach; tsedaqah… tse'aqah: each pair differs by a sound or a letter. What the LORD looked for and what He found sound almost alike.

  • vv8–23 "Woe" — six woes (vv8, 11, 18, 20, 21, 22), on land-grabbing, drunkenness, mocking God, calling evil good, self-made wisdom, and justice for sale (who acquit the guilty for a bribe; compare Exodus 23:8, a bribe blinds the clear-sighted).

  • v14 "Sheol has opened wide its throat" — hirchivah… nafshah: nefesh here is the throat, the appetite, as in Leviticus 17:11; the grave swallows the city's noise and pride.

  • v16 "the holy God is shown holy in righteousness" — niqdash, as the LORD said at the death of Nadab and Abihu, Through those near Me I will be shown holy (Leviticus 10:3).

  • v25 "For all this His anger has not turned away, and His hand is still stretched out" — a refrain that returns four times (9:12, 17, 21; 10:4).

  • v27 "none slumbers or sleeps" — lo yanum ve-lo yishan, the words Psalm 121:4 says of the LORD, He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep: the army He summons has His tirelessness.

chapters.title: Holy, Holy, Holy
chapters.html:
Isaiah 6

1In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and the hem of His robe filled the temple.

2Seraphim stood above Him; each had six wings: with two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.

3One called to another and said:

"Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts;
the whole earth is full of His glory."

4The posts of the thresholds shook at the voice of the one who called, and the house was filled with smoke.

5I said: "Woe is me! For I am ruined, because I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts."

6Then one of the seraphim flew to me, with a burning coal in his hand that he had taken with tongs from the altar.

7He touched my mouth with it and said: "This has touched your lips; your iniquity is taken away, and your sin is atoned for."

8Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying: "Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?" I said: "Here I am; send me."

9He said: "Go, and say to this people:

'Keep on listening, but do not understand;
keep on looking, but do not perceive.'

10Make the heart of this people fat,
make their ears heavy,
and shut their eyes;
otherwise they might see with their eyes,
and hear with their ears,
and understand with their heart,
and turn and be healed."

11Then I said, "How long, Lord?" He said:

"Until cities lie waste without inhabitant,
and houses without people,
and the land is left a desolate waste,

12and the LORD has sent the people far away,
and the forsaken places are many in the middle of the land.

13Even if a tenth remains in it,
it will be burned again,
like a terebinth or an oak
whose stump remains when it is felled.
The holy seed is its stump."

Notes

  • v1 "In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord" — Adonai, "the Lord." The king of Judah dies, and Isaiah sees the King (v5). John says of this vision, Isaiah said these things because he saw His glory and spoke about Him (John 12:41, eiden tēn doxan autou).

  • v2 "Seraphim" — serafim, from saraf, "to burn": the "burning ones." The same word names the fiery serpents of the wilderness (Numbers 21:6) and the bronze serpent made in their likeness.

  • v3 "Holy, holy, holy" — qadosh qadosh qadosh: Hebrew repeats a word to make a superlative, and nowhere else in the Hebrew Bible is holy said three times; the living creatures of Revelation say it again (hagios hagios hagios, Revelation 4:8). It is the source of the title Isaiah gives God throughout the book, the Holy One of Israel (1:4).

  • v5 "For I am ruined" — nidmeiti, from a root meaning both "be silenced" and "be cut off." The man whose lips are unclean is struck silent before the King.

  • v7 "your sin is atoned for" — tekhuppar, the verb of the altar's atonement (kipper), and the coal comes from the altar. The lips that made him ruined are where he is cleansed.

  • v8 "who will go for us?" — the plural, as in Let us make humankind in our image (Genesis 1:26); and the answer is Abraham's, Here I am (hinneni, Genesis 22:1).

  • vv9–10 "Keep on listening, but do not understand" — shim'u shamoa… re'u ra'o, each verb doubled. Jesus quotes these lines of His hearers (Matthew 13:14–15), and John and Paul quote them again (John 12:40; Acts 28:26–27). "Otherwise they might… turn and be healed" — pen, the word usually given as "lest."

  • v13 "The holy seed is its stump" — zera qodesh matsavtah: what is left after the felling is a stump, and the stump is a seed. The Greek of Isaiah ends the verse without this line.

chapters.title: The Sign of Immanuel
chapters.html:
Isaiah 7

1And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to wage war against it, but could not prevail against it.

2When it was told to the house of David, "Aram has settled in Ephraim," his heart and the heart of his people shook as the trees of the forest shake before the wind.

3The LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out now to meet Ahaz, you and Shear-jashub your son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer's Field,

4and say to him: Take care and be calm; do not fear, and do not let your heart lose courage because of these two smoldering stubs of firebrands, because of the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.

5Because Aram has plotted evil against you, with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, saying,

6'Let us go up against Judah and terrify it, and break it open for ourselves, and set up the son of Tabeel as king in it,'

7thus says the Lord GOD:

It shall not stand,
and it shall not come to pass.

8For the head of Aram is Damascus,
and the head of Damascus is Rezin;
within sixty-five years
Ephraim will be shattered and no longer be a people.

9The head of Ephraim is Samaria,
and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah.
If you will not stand firm in faith,
you will not stand firm at all."

10Again the LORD spoke to Ahaz, saying,

11"Ask a sign for yourself from the LORD your God; make it as deep as Sheol or as high as the heights above."

12Ahaz said, "I will not ask, and I will not test the LORD."

13Then Isaiah said, "Hear now, house of David! Is it too little for you to weary men, that you weary my God also?

14Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign:
the virgin will conceive and bear a son,
and she will call his name Immanuel.

15He will eat curds and honey
by the time he knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good.

16For before the boy knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land whose two kings you dread will be deserted.

17The LORD will bring upon you, upon your people and upon your father's house days such as have not come since the day Ephraim broke away from Judah: the king of Assyria."

18And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD will whistle for the fly that is at the far end of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.

19They will all come and settle in the steep ravines and in the clefts of the rocks, on all the thornbushes and on all the watering places.

20In that day the Lord will shave with a razor hired beyond the River — with the king of Assyria — the head and the hair of the feet, and it will sweep away the beard too.

21And it shall come to pass in that day, that a man will keep alive a young cow and two sheep;

22and because of the abundance of milk they give, he will eat curds; for everyone who is left in the land will eat curds and honey.

23And it shall come to pass in that day, that every place where there used to be a thousand vines, worth a thousand pieces of silver, will become briers and thorns.

24With arrows and bow one will go there, for all the land will be briers and thorns.

25As for all the hills that used to be hoed with a hoe, you will not go there for fear of briers and thorns; they will become a place where cattle are let loose and sheep tread.

Notes

  • v3 "Shear-jashub your son" — She'ar yashuv, "a remnant will return." The boy is a living message at his father's side, and the name returns as a promise in 10:21, A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God.

  • v9 "If you will not stand firm in faith, you will not stand firm at all" — im lo ta'aminu ki lo te'amenu, the same verb twice, aman, "to be firm," the root of amen: to believe is to stand on what holds.

  • v11 "as deep as Sheol" — ha'meq she'alah, which can be read she'alah, "ask it deep," or she'olah, "deep to Sheol"; the line plays on both.

  • v12 "I will not test the LORD" — the words of the law, You shall not test the LORD your God (Deuteronomy 6:16), used by a king who will not ask because he has already chosen Assyria (2 Kings 16:7).

  • v13 "that you weary my God also" — in v11 the prophet said the LORD your God; now, after Ahaz's refusal, my God.

  • v14 "the virgin will conceive and bear a son" — the Hebrew has hinneh ha-almah harah ve-yoledet ben, "the young woman is with child and is about to bear a son." Almah is a young woman of marriageable age; the word does not by itself say "virgin," for which the Hebrew has betulah. Both words are used of Rebekah before her marriage: a virgin (betulah, Genesis 24:16) and the young woman (ha-almah, 24:43). The Greek of Isaiah has idou hē parthenos en gastri lēmpsetai, "the virgin will conceive," and Matthew quotes the Greek of the birth of Jesus (Matthew 1:23). This line follows the Greek, which Matthew confirms; the Hebrew's she will call his name is kept (the Greek has you will call).

  • v14 "Immanuel" — immanu el, "with us is God." The name returns as the owner of the land (8:8) and as a battle cry (8:10, for God is with us).

  • vv15–16 "before the boy knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good" — the sign has a clock: before the child is old enough to choose, Damascus and Samaria will be deserted. The same clock runs for the prophet's next son (8:4).

  • v20 "the hair of the feet" — a polite phrase for the body's hair below the waist; the shaving is the shame of captives, as Hanun shamed David's men by shaving half of each one's beard (2 Samuel 10:4).

  • v23 "a thousand vines, worth a thousand pieces of silver" — the price of Solomon's vineyard (Song of Songs 8:11–12): the best land of Judah gone to briers and thorns, the pair of 5:6.

chapters.title: God Is with Us
chapters.html:
Isaiah 8

1The LORD said to me, "Take a large tablet and write on it in ordinary letters: For Maher-shalal-hash-baz."

2I called reliable witnesses to attest it for me, Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.

3Then I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. The LORD said to me, "Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz;

4for before the boy knows how to cry 'My father' and 'My mother,' the wealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be carried off before the king of Assyria."

5The LORD spoke to me again:

6"Because this people has refused
the waters of Shiloah that flow gently,
and rejoices with Rezin and the son of Remaliah,

7therefore the Lord is about to bring up against them
the waters of the River, mighty and many —
the king of Assyria and all his glory;
it will rise over all its channels
and go over all its banks;

8it will sweep on into Judah,
overflowing and passing through;
it will reach up to the neck;
and its outspread wings will fill
the breadth of your land, Immanuel."

9Be broken, you peoples, and be shattered;
give ear, all you distant parts of the earth;
put on your armor, and be shattered;
put on your armor, and be shattered.

10Make a plan, and it will come to nothing;
speak a word, and it will not stand;
for God is with us.

11For the LORD spoke thus to me, while His hand was strong upon me, and warned me not to walk in the way of this people, saying:

12"Do not call conspiracy
all that this people calls conspiracy,
and do not fear what they fear,
or be in dread.

13The LORD of hosts — Him you shall regard as holy;
let Him be your fear,
and let Him be your dread.

14He will become a sanctuary,
and a stone to strike against and a rock to stumble over
for both houses of Israel,
a trap and a snare
for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

15Many shall stumble over them;
they shall fall and be broken;
they shall be snared and taken."

16Bind up the testimony;
seal the instruction among my disciples.

17I will wait for the LORD,
who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob,
and I will hope in Him.

18Here am I and the children the LORD has given me, as signs and portents in Israel from the LORD of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.

19When they say to you, "Consult the ghosts and the spirits that chirp and mutter," should not a people consult their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?

20To the instruction and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, it is because there is no dawn for them.

21They will pass through the land, hard-pressed and hungry. And it shall come to pass, when they are hungry, that they will be enraged and curse their king and their God, and turn their faces upward;

22they will look to the earth: distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish; and they will be driven into deep darkness.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "Maher-shalal-hash-baz" — "Swift is the spoil, speedy the plunder": the name is written on a public tablet before the child is conceived, with two witnesses, so that no one can say afterward the prophecy was made up. One of them, Uriah the priest, is the priest who built King Ahaz an altar on the pattern of the one at Damascus (2 Kings 16:10).

  • v4 "before the boy knows how to cry 'My father'" — the clock of 7:16, now shorter: before the child can talk, Damascus and Samaria will be plundered.

  • vv6–8 "the waters of Shiloah that flow gently… the waters of the River" — the small stream that fed Jerusalem against the Euphrates in flood: the people who would not trust the quiet water will get the flood. "Your land, Immanuel" — the land belongs to the child of 7:14.

  • vv9–10 "for God is with us" — ki immanu el: the name of 7:14 becomes the answer to every plan the nations make.

  • v11 "while His hand was strong upon me" — ke-chezqat ha-yad, "with the strength of the hand": the prophet speaks under compulsion.

  • vv12–13 "do not fear what they fear… The LORD of hosts — Him you shall regard as holy" — Peter applies the Greek of these lines to Christ: do not fear what they fear… but in your hearts regard Christ the Lord as holy (1 Peter 3:14–15, ton de phobon autōn mē phobēthēte… kyrion de ton Christon hagiasate).

  • v14 "a stone to strike against and a rock to stumble over" — Paul and Peter join this verse to 28:16 and apply both to Christ: a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense (Romans 9:33; 1 Peter 2:8, lithos proskommatos kai petra skandalou). The same LORD is a sanctuary to some and a stumbling stone to others.

  • vv16–18 "seal the instruction among my disciples… Here am I and the children the LORD has given me" — the prophet, his disciples and his sons (Shear-jashub, Maher-shalal-hash-baz) are themselves signs and portents. Hebrews puts vv17–18 in the mouth of Christ: I will put my trust in Him… Here am I and the children God has given me (Hebrews 2:13).

  • v19 "the ghosts and the spirits that chirp and mutter" — ovot… yidde'onim, the pair of 2 Kings 23:24, the ghosts and the spirits, which Josiah would later put away.

  • v20 "there is no dawn for them" — ein lo shachar: those who will not speak by the instruction walk into the darkness of vv21–22, and 9:2 answers it, The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.

they will look to the earth: distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish; and they will be driven into deep darkness.

chapters.title: For to Us a Child Is Born
chapters.html:
Isaiah 9

1But there will be no gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time He brought contempt on the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the latter time He has made glorious the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.

2The people who walked in darkness
have seen a great light;
those who lived in the land of the shadow of death,
light has shone on them.

3You have multiplied the nation;
You have increased its joy;
they rejoice before You as with joy at the harvest,
as men rejoice when they divide the spoil.

4For the yoke of his burden,
and the staff on his shoulder,
the rod of his oppressor,
You have broken as on the day of Midian.

5For every boot of the tramping warrior in the tumult,
and every garment rolled in blood,
will be for burning, fuel for the fire.

6For to us a child is born,
to us a son is given;
and the government shall be on his shoulder;
and his name shall be called
Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God,
Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

7Of the increase of his government and of peace
there will be no end,
on the throne of David and over his kingdom,
to establish it and to uphold it
with justice and with righteousness
from this time forth and forever.
The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this.

His Hand Is Still Stretched Out

8The Lord has sent a word against Jacob,
and it has fallen on Israel;

9all the people will know it,
Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria,
who say in pride and arrogance of heart:

10"The bricks have fallen,
but we will build with dressed stone;
the sycamores have been cut down,
but we will put cedars in their place."

11So the LORD raised up the adversaries of Rezin against him,
and stirred up his enemies:

12the Arameans on the east and the Philistines on the west,
and they devoured Israel with open mouth.
For all this His anger has not turned away,
and His hand is still stretched out.

13But the people did not turn to Him who struck them,
nor did they seek the LORD of hosts.

14So the LORD cut off from Israel head and tail,
palm branch and reed, in one day —

15the elder and the man of rank, he is the head;
and the prophet who teaches lies, he is the tail;

16for those who guide this people lead them astray,
and those who are guided by them are swallowed up.

17Therefore the Lord does not rejoice over their young men,
and has no compassion on their orphans and widows;
for every one is godless and an evildoer,
and every mouth speaks folly.
For all this His anger has not turned away,
and His hand is still stretched out.

18For wickedness burns like fire;
it devours briers and thorns;
it kindles the thickets of the forest,
and they roll upward in a column of smoke.

19Through the fury of the LORD of hosts the land is scorched,
and the people are like fuel for the fire;
no one spares his brother.

20They slice on the right, and are still hungry;
they devour on the left, and are not satisfied;
each devours the flesh of his own arm,

21Manasseh Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh,
and together they are against Judah.
For all this His anger has not turned away,
and His hand is still stretched out.

Notes

  • v1 — Hebrew 8:23; the Hebrew numbers the rest of the chapter one lower (English 9:2 = Hebrew 9:1). The English numbering is followed. Zebulun and Naphtali, the northern tribes first taken by Assyria, are the first promised glory: Matthew quotes vv1–2 of Jesus making His home in Capernaum, Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations (Matthew 4:15–16).

  • v2 "the land of the shadow of death" — tsalmavet, the word of Psalm 23:4, the valley of the shadow of death; the darkness of 8:22 is answered.

  • v3 "You have increased its joy" — the read form, lo spelled with vav, "to it"; the written form is lo spelled with aleph, "not," which would make the line You have not increased the joy. The two differ in meaning, and the read form fits the rejoicing that follows.

  • v4 "as on the day of Midian" — when Gideon's three hundred broke a vast army without a fight, the LORD set every man's sword against his fellow (Judges 7:22).

  • vv4, 6 "the staff on his shoulder… the government shall be on his shoulder" — shikhmo both times: the oppressor's rod is broken off the people's shoulder, and the rule is laid on the child's.

  • v6 "Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace" — pele yo'ets, el gibbor, avi-ad, sar-shalom. El gibbor, "Mighty God," is used of the LORD Himself in the next chapter: A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God (10:21).

  • v7 "The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this" — qin'at YHWH tseva'ot: what the people cannot bring about, the LORD's own ardor will.

  • vv12, 17, 21 "For all this His anger has not turned away, and His hand is still stretched out" — the refrain of 5:25, three times here, and once more at 10:4. Each stanza ends where the last one did: the blow has fallen and the people have not turned.

  • v14 "head and tail, palm branch and reed" — v15 explains the first pair; the second is the high and the low of the marsh: everyone, from top to bottom.

chapters.title: Assyria, the Rod of My Anger
chapters.html:
Isaiah 10

1Woe to those who make unjust laws,
and those who keep putting oppression in writing,

2to turn the poor away from justice
and to rob the afflicted of My people of their right,
so that widows become their spoil,
and they plunder the orphans.

3What will you do on the day of punishment,
in the ruin that will come from far away?
To whom will you flee for help,
and where will you leave your wealth?

4Nothing is left but to crouch among the prisoners
or to fall among the slain.
For all this His anger has not turned away,
and His hand is still stretched out.

Assyria, the Rod of My Anger

5Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger;
the staff in their hand is My fury!

6Against a godless nation I send him,
and against the people of My wrath I command him,
to take spoil and seize plunder,
and to trample them down like the mud of the streets.

7But this is not what he intends,
and this is not what his heart plans;
it is in his heart to destroy,
and to cut off nations, not a few.

8For he says:
"Are not my commanders all kings?

9Is not Calno like Carchemish?
Is not Hamath like Arpad?
Is not Samaria like Damascus?

10As my hand has reached the kingdoms of the idols,
whose carved images outnumbered those of Jerusalem and Samaria,

11shall I not do to Jerusalem and her images
as I have done to Samaria and her idols?"

12And it shall come to pass, when the Lord has finished all His work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, that I will punish the fruit of the king of Assyria's arrogant heart and the pride of his haughty eyes.

13For he says:
"By the strength of my hand I have done it,
and by my wisdom, for I have understanding.
I have removed the borders of peoples
and plundered their treasures;
like a mighty one I have brought down the inhabitants.

14My hand has found the wealth of the peoples like a nest,
and as one gathers eggs that have been left,
so I have gathered all the earth;
and there was none that fluttered a wing,
or opened its beak, or chirped."

15Shall the axe boast over him who hews with it,
or the saw make itself great over him who wields it?
As if a rod should wield those who lift it,
as if a staff should lift him who is not wood!

16Therefore the Lord, the LORD of hosts,
will send leanness among his fat ones,
and under his glory a blaze will be kindled,
burning like fire.

17The light of Israel will become a fire,
and his Holy One a flame;
it will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day.

18The glory of his forest and of his fruitful land
He will consume, both soul and body,
and it will be as when a sick man wastes away.

19The remnant of the trees of his forest will be so few
that a child could write them down.

A Remnant Will Return

20And it shall come to pass in that day, that the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no longer lean on him who struck them, but will lean on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.

21A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God.

22For though your people Israel be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them will return. Destruction is decreed, overflowing with righteousness.

23For the Lord GOD of hosts will carry out the full end that is decreed, throughout the whole earth.

24Therefore thus says the Lord GOD of hosts: "My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of Assyria, when he strikes you with the rod and lifts his staff against you, as in Egypt.

25For in a very little while the fury will be spent, and My anger will turn to their destruction."

26The LORD of hosts will wield a whip against him, as in the striking of Midian at the rock of Oreb; His staff will be over the sea, and He will lift it, as in Egypt.

27And it shall come to pass in that day, that his burden will depart from your shoulder, and his yoke from your neck, and the yoke will be broken because of fatness.

The March on Jerusalem

28He has come to Aiath;
he has passed through Migron;
at Michmash he leaves his baggage.

29They have crossed the pass;
"At Geba we will spend the night."
Ramah trembles;
Gibeah of Saul has fled.

30Cry aloud, daughter of Gallim!
Listen, Laishah!
Poor Anathoth!

31Madmenah is in flight;
the inhabitants of Gebim take cover.

32This very day he will halt at Nob;
he shakes his fist
at the mount of the daughter of Zion,
the hill of Jerusalem.

33The Lord, the LORD of hosts,
is about to lop the boughs with a terrifying crash;
the tall in stature will be hewn down,
and the lofty will be brought low.

34The thickets of the forest will be cut down with iron,
and Lebanon will fall by the Majestic One.

Notes

  • vv2, 6 "widows become their spoil, and they plunder the orphans… to take spoil and seize plunder" — shalal and bazaz, the two words of the child's name in 8:1, Maher-shalal-hash-baz, "swift is the spoil, speedy the plunder." The lawmakers make spoil of the widow and plunder of the orphan; in v6 the LORD sends Assyria lishlol shalal ve-lavoz baz, to do the same to them.

  • v4 "For all this His anger has not turned away" — the refrain's last appearance (5:25; 9:12, 17, 21). It is answered in 12:1 with the same two words, shuv, "turn," and af, "anger": Your anger has turned away, and You have comforted me.

  • vv5, 15, 24, 26 "the rod… the staff" — shevet and matteh, a pair that runs through the chapter. Assyria is the LORD's rod (v5); the rod boasts as if it lifted the hand that holds it (v15); Assyria lifts his staff against Zion as in Egypt (v24), and the LORD lifts His staff over the sea as in Egypt (v26), as Moses was told to lift his over the Red Sea (Exodus 14:16). Be-derekh Mitsrayim, "as in Egypt," is the same phrase both times: the oppressor's staff and the deliverer's.

  • vv9–11 "Is not Samaria like Damascus?… shall I not do to Jerusalem" — the king counts Jerusalem among the kingdoms of the idols, and the LORD among the idols. His officer makes the same speech outside Jerusalem's walls: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad?… Have they delivered Samaria out of my hand? (36:19).

  • v13 "like a mighty one" — ka-abbir. The consonants are those of God's title in 1:24, the Mighty One of Israel (avir); the reading tradition voices them one way for God and another for a strong man or a bull. Spelled out, the king's boast and God's title are the same word.

  • vv16, 27 "leanness among his fat ones… because of fatness" — mishmannav and shamen, one root. Assyria's fat ones waste away, and the yoke on Israel's neck breaks mipnei shamen, literally "from before fat." Shemen is oil, and also the fat of a body (my flesh has grown lean, with no fat, mi-shamen, Psalm 109:24). The phrase is uncertain: the picture may be a neck grown too thick for the yoke, or the oil of anointing. The Greek has neither: the yoke will be destroyed from your shoulders. "His burden… from your shoulder" — subbolo… shikhmekha, the words of 9:4.

  • vv19–22 "remnant" — she'ar, five times. Assyria's remnant is a handful of trees a child can count (v19); Israel's is the she'ar that will return, the name of Isaiah's son Shear-jashub (7:3), and it returns to the Mighty God, el gibbor, the name given the child in 9:6.

  • vv22–23 "though your people Israel be like the sand of the sea" — the promise to Abraham, as the sand that is on the lip of the sea (Genesis 22:17), is turned: as many as the sand, and still only a remnant comes back. The Greek has will be saved for will return, and Paul quotes it: the remnant will be saved, for the Lord will carry out His word on the earth, completing it and cutting it short (Romans 9:27–28).

  • vv28–32 "Aiath… Nob" — the enemy comes town by town, each nearer, until Jerusalem is in sight. Michmash, Geba and Gibeah of Saul are the ground of Saul's war with the Philistines (the pass of Michmash, 1 Samuel 13:23); Anathoth is a town of priests, Jeremiah's home (Jeremiah 1:1); Nob is the city of the priests, put to the sword at Saul's order (1 Samuel 22:17–19). "Poor Anathoth" — aniyyah Anatot, two words that chime.

  • v34 "by the Majestic One" — be-addir. Addir is used of the LORD in this book, there the LORD in majesty will be for us (33:21), and of great trees elsewhere, the majestic ones are ruined (Zechariah 11:2). Read the first way, the line matches with iron above it, the hand that fells the forest. The Greek reads it the second way: Lebanon will fall with its lofty ones.

chapters.title: The Shoot from the Stump of Jesse
chapters.html:
Isaiah 11

1A shoot will come out from the stump of Jesse,
and a branch from his roots will bear fruit.

2The Spirit of the LORD will rest on him,
the Spirit of wisdom and understanding,
the Spirit of counsel and might,
the Spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD.

3The fear of the LORD will be his delight;
he will not judge by what his eyes see,
or decide by what his ears hear,

4but with righteousness he will judge the poor,
and decide with fairness for the humble of the earth;
he will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth,
and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.

5Righteousness will be the belt around his waist,
and faithfulness the belt around his loins.

6The wolf shall live as a guest with the lamb,
and the leopard shall lie down with the young goat;
the calf and the young lion and the fatling together,
and a little child shall lead them.

7The cow and the bear shall graze;
their young shall lie down together;
and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.

8The nursing child shall play over the hole of the cobra,
and the weaned child shall put his hand on the adder's den.

9They shall not harm or destroy
in all My holy mountain;
for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD
as the waters cover the sea.

The Second Exodus

10And it shall come to pass in that day, that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a signal for the peoples, and his resting place will be glorious.

11And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord will extend His hand a second time to recover the remnant of His people, those who are left, from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the coastlands of the sea.

12He will raise a signal for the nations,
and gather the banished of Israel,
and bring together the scattered of Judah
from the four corners of the earth.

13The jealousy of Ephraim shall depart,
and those who harass Judah shall be cut off;
Ephraim shall not be jealous of Judah,
and Judah shall not harass Ephraim.

14They shall swoop down on the slopes of the Philistines to the west;
together they shall plunder the sons of the east;
Edom and Moab shall be in their grasp,
and the sons of Ammon shall obey them.

15The LORD will devote to destruction
the tongue of the sea of Egypt,
and wave His hand over the River
with His scorching wind,
and strike it into seven streams,
and lead people across in sandals.

16There will be a highway for the remnant of His people
who are left from Assyria,
as there was for Israel
on the day they came up from the land of Egypt.

Notes

  • v1 "a shoot will come out from the stump of Jesse" — choter and geza. The chapter before ends with a forest felled, its tall trees hewn down and Lebanon fallen (10:33–34). This one opens on a stump that sprouts. The line is named for Jesse, David's father, not for David: the tree has been cut back to its stump. "Will bear fruit" — yifreh; the Greek has a flower will come up from the root.

  • v2 "the Spirit of the LORD will rest on him" — ve-nachah, "settle, rest," the verb of Numbers 11:25, when the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied; in v10 the same root gives his resting place. Then three pairs: wisdom and understanding, counsel and might, knowledge and the fear of the LORD. The Greek makes the last knowledge and godliness, and gives the fear of God to v3, so that it names seven where the Hebrew names six.

  • v3 "the fear of the LORD will be his delight" — va-hariho, literally "his smelling." It is the verb of the LORD smelled the soothing aroma (Genesis 8:21), and of I will not smell your solemn assemblies (Amos 5:21), where to smell is to take pleasure. The judge who will not go by what his eyes see or his ears hear is given a third sense.

  • v4 "the rod of his mouth… the breath of his lips" — shevet, the word of 10:5, where Assyria is the rod of My anger. This king's rod is his word. Paul applies the line to the Lord Jesus: whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of His mouth (2 Thessalonians 2:8).

  • v6 "The wolf shall live as a guest with the lamb" — gar, from gur, the verb of the guest who lives on land that is another's, A guest and a resident I am among you (Genesis 23:4). The wolf is the lamb's guest. Isaiah returns to vv6–9 at the book's end: The wolf and the lamb shall graze together… They shall not harm or destroy in all My holy mountain, says the LORD (65:25).

  • v9 "the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea" — Habakkuk has the same line with one word more: the knowledge of the glory of the LORD (Habakkuk 2:14).

  • vv10, 12 "a signal for the peoples… He will raise a signal for the nations" — nes, the signal of 5:26, where the LORD raises it to call the enemy from the end of the earth. Here it is raised to gather His own scattered people from its four corners. Paul quotes v10 from the Greek, which reads differently: the root of Jesse, the one who rises to rule the nations; in Him the nations will hope (Romans 15:12).

  • vv11, 15–16 "a second time to recover… as there was for Israel on the day they came up from the land of Egypt" — liqnot, "to acquire, make one's own," the verb of the Song of the Sea, the people You made Your own (Exodus 15:16). The return is told as the first exodus told again: a sea struck, a crossing on foot, a highway.

  • v13 "The jealousy of Ephraim shall depart" — Ephraim, the northern kingdom, had joined Aram against Judah (7:1–2), and together they are against Judah (9:21). The split ends.

  • v15 "devote to destruction" — hecherim, the verb of the ban, used of the cities of Canaan (They devoted to destruction all that was in the city, Joshua 6:21). Here it is laid on a sea. The Greek has will lay waste. "His scorching wind" — ba'yam, a word found only here; "scorching" is the sense the context gives, and the Greek has a violent wind.

but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with fairness for the humble of the earth; he will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.

chapters.title: The Springs of Deliverance
chapters.html:
Isaiah 12

1In that day you will say:
"I will give thanks to You, LORD,
for though You were angry with me,
Your anger has turned away,
and You have comforted me.

2God is my deliverance;
I will trust, and will not be afraid;
for my strength and my song is Yah, the LORD,
and He has become my deliverance."

3With joy you will draw water
from the springs of deliverance.

4In that day you will say:
"Give thanks to the LORD; call on His name;
make His deeds known among the peoples;
proclaim that His name is exalted.

5Sing praise to the LORD, for He has done gloriously;
let this be known in all the earth.

6Cry out and shout for joy, you who live in Zion,
for great among you is the Holy One of Israel."

Notes

  • v1 "Your anger has turned away" — yashov appekha. The refrain of the chapters before was His anger has not turned away (5:25; 9:12, 17, 21; 10:4), lo shav appo: the same verb and the same noun. The song begins where the refrain ended. "You will say" is singular here and plural in v4: one voice first, then all of them.

  • v2 "my strength and my song is Yah… and He has become my deliverance" — word for word the Song of the Sea (Exodus 15:2), sung again in Psalm 118:14. Isaiah adds the name of the LORD to Yah: Yah YHWH. The chapter before ended on the sea struck and a people crossing it (11:15–16); the song that follows is the song Israel sang on the far shore.

  • vv2–3 "deliverance" — yeshu'ah, three times in two verses: God is my deliverance, He has become my deliverance, the springs of deliverance. It is the root of the prophet's own name, Yesha'yahu (1:1), "the LORD delivers."

  • v6 "you who live in Zion… great among you is the Holy One of Israel" — yoshevet Tsiyyon, feminine and singular: the city's people spoken to as one woman, as in the daughter of Zion (1:8; 10:32). The One the seraphim called holy, holy, holy (6:3) is among you, be-qirbekh.

chapters.title: The Oracle Against Babylon
chapters.html:
Isaiah 13

1The oracle concerning Babylon, which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.

2On a bare hill raise a signal;
lift up your voice to them;
wave the hand
for them to enter the gates of the nobles.

3I Myself have commanded My consecrated ones;
I have called My mighty men for My anger,
those who exult in My majesty.

4The sound of a tumult on the mountains,
like that of a great people!
The sound of an uproar of kingdoms,
of nations gathered together!
The LORD of hosts is mustering
a host for battle.

5They come from a distant land,
from the end of the heavens,
the LORD and the weapons of His fury,
to destroy the whole earth.

6Wail, for the day of the LORD is near;
it will come like destruction from the Almighty.

7Therefore all hands will go limp,
and every human heart will melt.

8They will be terrified;
pangs and agony will seize them;
they will writhe like a woman in labor.
They will look at one another aghast;
their faces will be aflame.

9The day of the LORD is coming,
cruel, with fury and burning anger,
to make the earth a desolation
and to destroy its sinners from it.

10For the stars of the heavens and their constellations
will not flash their light;
the sun will be dark at its rising,
and the moon will not shine its light.

11I will punish the world for its evil,
and the wicked for their iniquity;
I will put an end to the pride of the arrogant,
and lay low the haughtiness of the ruthless.

12I will make man rarer than fine gold,
and mankind than the gold of Ophir.

13Therefore I will make the heavens tremble,
and the earth will be shaken out of its place,
at the fury of the LORD of hosts
on the day of His burning anger.

14Like a hunted gazelle,
like sheep that no one gathers,
each will turn to his own people,
and each will flee to his own land.

15Whoever is found will be thrust through,
and whoever is caught will fall by the sword.

16Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes;
their houses will be plundered,
and their wives raped.

17I am about to stir up the Medes against them,
who have no regard for silver
and take no delight in gold.

18Their bows will dash the young men to pieces;
they will have no mercy on the fruit of the womb;
their eyes will not spare children.

19Babylon, the glory of kingdoms,
the splendor and pride of the Chaldeans,
will be like Sodom and Gomorrah
when God overthrew them.

20It will never be inhabited
or lived in for all generations;
no Arab will pitch his tent there;
no shepherds will rest their flocks there.

21But wild beasts will lie down there,
and their houses will be full of howling creatures;
there ostriches will live,
and there goat-spirits will dance.

22Hyenas will cry in its strongholds,
and jackals in its palaces of pleasure;
its time is close at hand,
and its days will not be prolonged.

Notes

  • v1 "The oracle concerning Babylon" — massa, from nasa, "to lift": a thing lifted up, a burden, and so a solemn pronouncement. The word heads each of the oracles on the nations that follow: Moab (15:1), Damascus (17:1), Egypt (19:1), and on through 23:1. Babylon heads the list, though the power in Isaiah's own chapters so far is Assyria (7:17; 10:5).

  • v3 "My consecrated ones" — mequddashai, "those made holy": soldiers set apart for the LORD's war. The verb is the one of consecrate war against her, that is, prepare for battle (Jeremiah 6:4). The army that takes Babylon is named in v17: the Medes.

  • v6 "like destruction from the Almighty" — ke-shod mi-Shaddai, a play of sounds: shod, "destruction," from Shaddai, the old name of God rendered the Almighty, the only time the name appears in Isaiah. Joel has the same line (Joel 1:15).

  • v10 "their constellations" — u-khsileihem, the plural of kesil, Orion (Amos 5:8; Job 9:9; 38:31): one constellation's name used for them all. Jesus takes up the verse: Immediately after the affliction of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light (Matthew 24:29).

  • vv14, 19 "Like a hunted gazelle… the glory of kingdoms" — tsevi both times. The word means a gazelle and also beauty, glory. In v14 it is the frightened animal running; in v19 it is Babylon's pride, the tsevi of kingdoms. The same word names the city's glory and the hunted thing it becomes.

  • v17 "the Medes" — named here as the power that will take Babylon. Belshazzar's last night in Babylon ends with the same people: your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians, and Darius the Mede received the kingdom (Daniel 5:28, 31). They have no regard for silver: they cannot be bought off.

  • v19 "like Sodom and Gomorrah when God overthrew them" — ke-mahpekhat Elohim, "like God's overthrow," the word used of Sodom and Gomorrah in Deuteronomy 29:23 and in Isaiah 1:7–9.

  • v21 "goat-spirits" — se'irim, "hairy ones," the word of Leviticus 17:7 for what Israel had been sacrificing to. It is also the ordinary word for he-goats, so the line may mean wild goats leaping in the ruins. The Greek has daimonia, demons, and Isaiah pairs se'ir with Lilith in another ruined land (34:14). "Howling creatures" — ochim, a word found only here; what creature it names is not known.

  • v22 "in its strongholds" — be-almenotav, spelled as the word for "its widows." The same spelling stands beside cities laid waste at Ezekiel 19:7. The sense "strongholds" reads it as armenot (23:13; 32:14), l for r, and the next line's palaces calls for a building. Read as spelled, the hyenas howl among Babylon's widows.

chapters.title: How You Have Fallen from Heaven
chapters.html:
Isaiah 14

1For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob, and will again choose Israel, and will settle them in their own land; and the guest will join them and attach himself to the house of Jacob.

2Peoples will take them and bring them to their place, and the house of Israel will possess them in the LORD's land as male and female servants. They will take captive those who took them captive, and rule over their slave drivers.

3And it shall come to pass, in the day the LORD gives you rest from your pain and your turmoil and the hard service you were made to serve,

4that you will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon, and say:

"How the slave driver has ceased,
the taskmaster has ceased!

5The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked,
the rod of rulers,

6that struck the peoples in fury
with blows that never let up,
that ruled the nations in anger
with persecution no one held back.

7The whole earth is at rest and quiet;
they break out into singing.

8Even the cypresses rejoice over you,
the cedars of Lebanon:
'Since you were laid low,
no woodcutter comes up against us.'

9Sheol beneath is stirred up for you,
to meet you when you come;
it rouses the shades for you,
all the leaders of the earth;
it raises from their thrones
all the kings of the nations.

10All of them will answer
and say to you:
'You too have become as weak as we are;
you have become like us.'

11Your pomp is brought down to Sheol,
with the sound of your harps;
maggots are the bed spread beneath you,
and worms are your covering.

12How you have fallen from heaven,
Day Star, son of the dawn!
How you are cut down to the ground,
you who laid the nations low!

13You said in your heart:
'I will ascend to heaven;
above the stars of God
I will set my throne on high;
I will sit on the mount of assembly
in the far reaches of the north;

14I will ascend above the heights of the clouds;
I will make myself like the Most High.'

15But you are brought down to Sheol,
to the far reaches of the pit.

16Those who see you will stare at you
and look you over:
'Is this the man who made the earth tremble,
who shook kingdoms,

17who made the world like a wilderness
and tore down its cities,
who never let his prisoners go home?'

18All the kings of the nations, every one of them,
lie in honor, each in his own tomb;

19but you are cast out, away from your grave,
like a detestable branch,
clothed with the slain, those pierced by the sword,
who go down to the stones of the pit,
like a corpse trampled underfoot.

20You will not be joined with them in burial,
because you have destroyed your land;
you have slain your people.
The seed of evildoers
will never be named again.

21Prepare a slaughtering place for his sons
for the iniquity of their fathers,
so that they do not rise and possess the earth
and fill the world with cities."

22"I will rise up against them,"
declares the LORD of hosts,
"and cut off from Babylon name and remnant,
offspring and posterity,"
declares the LORD.

23"I will make it a possession for the hedgehog,
and pools of water,
and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction,"
declares the LORD of hosts.

The LORD's Plan for Assyria

24The LORD of hosts has sworn:
"As I have planned,
so it will be;
as I have purposed,
so it will stand:

25to break Assyria in My land,
and trample him on My mountains;
his yoke will depart from them,
and his burden will depart from their shoulder."

26This is the plan made for the whole earth,
and this is the hand stretched out
over all the nations.

27For the LORD of hosts has planned,
and who will annul it?
His hand is stretched out,
and who will turn it back?

The Oracle Against Philistia

28In the year that King Ahaz died this oracle came:

29Do not rejoice, Philistia, all of you,
that the rod that struck you is broken;
for from the serpent's root will come an adder,
and its fruit will be a flying fiery serpent.

30The poorest of the poor will graze,
and the needy will lie down in safety;
but I will kill your root with famine,
and it will slay your remnant.

31Wail, gate! Cry out, city!
Melt in fear, Philistia, all of you!
For smoke comes out of the north,
and there is no straggler in its ranks.

32What will one answer the messengers of the nation?
"The LORD has founded Zion,
and in her the afflicted of His people will find refuge."

Notes

  • vv2–4 "slave drivers… the hard service you were made to serve… How the slave driver has ceased" — nogesim, the word for Pharaoh's slave drivers (Exodus 3:7; 5:6), and ha-avodah ha-qashah, the hard service of Exodus 1:14. The fall of Babylon is told in the words of the release from Egypt, as the return was in 11:15–16 and the song in 12:2.

  • v4 "the taskmaster" — madhevah, a word found only here, whose meaning is not known. The Greek has epispoudastēs, "one who hurries others on," from the verb the Greek of Exodus uses for the slave drivers who pressed Israel (katespeudon, Exodus 5:13); the rendering follows it. Taken from the Aramaic dehav, "gold" (Daniel 2:32), it would be "the golden city." "This taunt" — mashal, a proverb, a saying that likens one thing to another; the Greek calls it a thrēnos, a lament.

  • vv4, 5, 10 "taunt… rulers… you have become like us" — the same three letters, m-sh-l, three times: the mashal, "taunt," is taken up against the moshlim, "rulers," and the dead greet the king with nimshalta, "you have been made like" us.

  • vv8, 13–15 "the cedars of Lebanon… the far reaches of the north… the far reaches of the pit" — felling Lebanon's cedars is a conqueror's boast: I have gone up… to the far reaches of Lebanon; I cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest cypresses, says the king of Assyria (37:24). Here the trees are glad the king is gone. Yarkhetei, "far reaches," twice: he aims at the far reaches of the north, which Psalm 48:2 gives to Mount Zion (Mount Zion, the heights of the north, the city of the great King), and is sent to the far reaches of the pit.

  • v11 "maggots are the bed spread beneath you" — yutsa, the verb for spreading a bed, as in if I make my bed in Sheol (Psalm 139:8).

  • v12 "Day Star, son of the dawn" — helel ben shachar. Helel is from halal, "to shine" (when His lamp shone on my head, Job 29:3); the Greek has heōsphoros, "dawn-bringer," the morning star. The taunt is spoken against the king of Babylon (v4), and when he lands, the dead ask, Is this the man? (v16). "Cut down to the ground" — nigda'ta, the verb used of the tall trees hewn down in 10:33. Jesus uses the same picture for Satan: I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven (Luke 10:18).

  • v14 "I will make myself like the Most High" — eddammeh, from damah, "to be like." The LORD answers it in the book's second half: To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal? (40:25). In v24 He swears by the same verb, ka'asher dimmiti, "as I have planned."

  • v19 "like a detestable branch" — ke-netser nit'av. Netser is the branch from the roots of Jesse (11:1); nit'av is the verb of to'evah, "detestable." One branch bears fruit; the other is thrown out.

  • vv25–27 "his yoke will depart from them… the hand stretched out… who will turn it back?" — the words of 10:27 again, his burden will depart from your shoulder, and his yoke from your neck. Ha-yad ha-netuyah, "the hand stretched out," and shuv, "turn back," are the words of the refrain, His anger has not turned away, and His hand is still stretched out (5:25 to 10:4). The hand that was stretched out against Israel is now stretched out over all the nations.

  • vv28–29 "In the year that King Ahaz died… a flying fiery serpent" — dated like the vision of 6:1, In the year that King Uzziah died. Saraf me'ofef: the seraphim who flew above the throne (6:2, ye'ofef, the same verb) and the fiery serpents of the wilderness (Numbers 21:6) share the name. "From the serpent's root" — mi-shoresh nachash, a root as in 11:1 and 11:10, the root of Jesse.
