Prepare a slaughtering place for his sons for the iniquity of their fathers, so that they do not rise and possess the earth and fill the world with cities."
"I will rise up against them," declares the LORD of hosts, "and cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and posterity," declares the LORD.
"I will make it a possession for the hedgehog, and pools of water, and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction," declares the LORD of hosts.
The LORD's Plan for Assyria
The LORD of hosts has sworn: "As I have planned, so it will be; as I have purposed, so it will stand:
to break Assyria in My land, and trample him on My mountains; his yoke will depart from them, and his burden will depart from their shoulder."
This is the plan made for the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
For the LORD of hosts has planned, and who will annul it? His hand is stretched out, and who will turn it back?
The Oracle Against Philistia
In the year that King Ahaz died this oracle came:
Do not rejoice, Philistia, all of you, that the rod that struck you is broken; for from the serpent's root will come an adder, and its fruit will be a flying fiery serpent.
The poorest of the poor will graze, and the needy will lie down in safety; but I will kill your root with famine, and it will slay your remnant.
Wail, gate! Cry out, city! Melt in fear, Philistia, all of you! For smoke comes out of the north, and there is no straggler in its ranks.
What will one answer the messengers of the nation? "The LORD has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of His people will find refuge."

chapters.title: The Oracle Against Moab
chapters.html:
Isaiah 15

1The oracle concerning Moab.

Ar of Moab is laid waste in a night;
it is ruined.
Kir of Moab is laid waste in a night;
it is ruined.

2They have gone up to the temple, and Dibon to the high places, to weep;
over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails.
Every head is shaved bald;
every beard is cut off.

3In its streets they put on sackcloth;
on its roofs and in its squares
everyone wails, running with tears.

4Heshbon and Elealeh cry out;
their voice is heard as far as Jahaz.
So the armed men of Moab cry aloud;
his soul trembles within him.

5My heart cries out for Moab;
her fugitives flee as far as Zoar,
to Eglath-shelishiyah.
Up the ascent of Luhith
they go weeping;
on the road to Horonaim
they raise a cry of ruin.

6The waters of Nimrim are desolate;
the grass is withered, the new growth is gone;
there is nothing green.

7So the wealth they have gained
and what they have stored up
they carry away over the Brook of the Willows.

8The cry has gone around the borders of Moab;
her wailing reaches Eglaim;
her wailing reaches Beer-elim.

9The waters of Dimon are full of blood;
yet I will bring still more on Dimon:
a lion for those of Moab who escape,
and for the remnant of the land.

Notes

  • v1 "The oracle concerning Moab" — Moab was Lot's son by his elder daughter (Genesis 19:37). Jeremiah's oracle on Moab takes up much of this one and the next, often word for word (Jeremiah 48:5, 29–38). "Ruined" — nidmah, the verb of Isaiah's own cry in the temple, I am ruined (6:5).

  • v2 "Every head is shaved bald; every beard is cut off" — the signs of mourning, with the sackcloth of v3. Isaiah calls Jerusalem to the same in 22:12, to weeping and mourning, to baldness and to putting on sackcloth.

  • v5 "My heart cries out for Moab" — the prophet grieves for the enemy he condemns, and he says it again: I weep… I drench you with my tears (16:9); my inner parts moan for Moab like a harp (16:11). Jeremiah takes up the line: my heart moans for Moab like flutes (Jeremiah 48:36).

  • v5 "Eglath-shelishiyah" — literally "the third Eglath," or "a heifer three years old," as the Greek reads it (damalis trietēs). Jeremiah 48:34 has it in a list of towns, from Zoar to Horonaim, and it is rendered here as a place.

  • vv2, 9 "Dibon… the waters of Dimon are full of blood" — the town is Dibon in v2; in v9 it is spelled Dimon, twice, beside dam, "blood." The spelling makes the town's name sound like what fills its waters.

  • v9 "a lion for those of Moab who escape, and for the remnant" — peletah, "those who escape," and she'erit, "remnant": the words of hope for Israel in 10:20 (peletah, and she'ar from the same root as she'erit). Moab's survivors meet a lion.

chapters.title: Shelter for the Outcasts of Moab
chapters.html:
Isaiah 16

1Send the lamb to the ruler of the land,
from Sela, across the wilderness,
to the mount of the daughter of Zion.

2Like fluttering birds,
like a nest scattered,
so are the daughters of Moab
at the fords of the Arnon.

3"Give counsel;
grant a ruling;
make your shade like night
at the height of noon;
hide the outcasts;
do not betray the fugitive.

4Let the outcasts of Moab live as guests among you;
be a shelter to them from the destroyer."

When the oppressor is no more,
and destruction has ceased,
and the one who tramples has vanished from the land,

5then a throne will be established in loyal love,
and on it will sit in faithfulness,
in the tent of David,
one who judges and seeks justice
and is swift to do righteousness.

6We have heard of the pride of Moab —
how very proud he is! —
of his arrogance, his pride, and his fury;
his boasting is empty.

7So Moab wails for Moab;
all of them wail.
For the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth you will moan,
utterly stricken.

8For the fields of Heshbon languish,
and the vine of Sibmah;
the lords of the nations have struck down its choice branches,
which reached as far as Jazer
and strayed into the wilderness;
its shoots spread out
and crossed over the sea.

9So I weep with the weeping of Jazer
for the vine of Sibmah;
I drench you with my tears,
Heshbon and Elealeh;
for on your summer fruit and on your harvest
the shout has fallen.

10Joy and gladness are taken away from the fruitful field;
in the vineyards no one sings,
no one shouts for joy;
no one treads out wine in the presses;
I have put an end to the shout.

11So my inner parts moan for Moab like a harp,
and my inmost being for Kir-heres.

12And it shall come to pass, when Moab presents himself, when he wears himself out on the high place and comes to his sanctuary to pray, that he will not prevail.

13This is the word that the LORD spoke concerning Moab long ago.

14But now the LORD has spoken, saying: "Within three years, like the years of a hired man, the glory of Moab will be brought into contempt, with all his great multitude, and the remnant will be very small and feeble."

Notes

  • v1 "Send the lamb to the ruler of the land" — kar, the tribute Moab once paid in lambs: Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he used to pay the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs (2 Kings 3:4, karim). Moab's refugees are told to send it again, now to Zion.

  • vv3–4 "Let the outcasts of Moab live as guests among you" — nidchei Mo'av, as the Greek reads it: the fugitives of Moab will live as guests with you. The Hebrew vowels read the same letters nidachai, "my outcasts," with Moab as the one spoken to: Let my outcasts live as guests among you; Moab, be a shelter to them. Read that way, Israel's outcasts ask Moab for shelter. Read the Greek's way, Moab's refugees (v2) ask the daughter of Zion (v1): most of the commands in v3 and the you of v4 are feminine, and the answer in v5 is a throne in Zion; only be in v4 is masculine. "Live as guests" — yaguru, from gur. Moab once sheltered David's family: Please let my father and my mother come and stay with you (1 Samuel 22:3).

  • v5 "a throne will be established in loyal love… in the tent of David" — chesed and emet, loyal love and faithfulness, the throne of 9:7, on the throne of David… with justice and with righteousness. The answer to the refugees is a king in Zion who judges rightly.

  • v6 "the pride of Moab… his arrogance, his pride" — ge'on, ge, ga'avato, ge'ono: four words from one root, ga'ah, "to rise up." Jeremiah 48:29 has the same line and adds more: his loftiness, his pride, his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart.

  • v7 "the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth" — ashishei, pressed cakes of raisins. Jeremiah's version of the line has the men of Kir-heres (Jeremiah 48:31), and v11 here has the shorter name too. In v11 qirbi, "my inmost being," chimes with Qir.

  • v8 "the lords of the nations have struck down its choice branches" — ba'alei goyim halemu seruqqeha. The words can also be read the other way round: its choice vines struck down the lords of the nations, that is, its wine laid them low, as halumei yayin, "those struck down by wine," says of Ephraim's drunkards (28:1). The Greek reads it as rendered: the nations trample its vines.

  • vv9–10 "the shout has fallen… I have put an end to the shout" — heidad, the shout of the men treading grapes (a shout like those who tread grapes, Jeremiah 25:30). In v10 the harvest shout is silenced; in v9 a shout falls on the harvest, the enemy's.

  • v14 "like the years of a hired man" — counted to the day, no more and no less: in the law a sold man's time shall be counted like the days of a hired man (Leviticus 25:50). The same measure is set for Kedar in 21:16.

chapters.title: The Oracle Against Damascus
chapters.html:
Isaiah 17

1The oracle concerning Damascus.

Damascus is about to cease to be a city;
it will become a heap of ruins.

2The cities of Aroer are deserted;
they will be for flocks,
which will lie down with no one to make them afraid.

3The fortress will vanish from Ephraim,
and the kingdom from Damascus;
and the remnant of Aram will be
like the glory of the sons of Israel,
declares the LORD of hosts.

4And it shall come to pass in that day,
that the glory of Jacob will be brought low,
and the fat of his flesh will grow lean.

5It will be as when the reaper gathers the standing grain,
and his arm harvests the ears,
and as when one gleans the ears of grain
in the Valley of Rephaim.

6Gleanings will be left in it,
as when an olive tree is beaten:
two or three berries
at the top of the highest bough,
four or five
on the branches of a fruitful tree,
declares the LORD, the God of Israel.

7In that day man will look to his Maker,
and his eyes will look to the Holy One of Israel.

8He will not look to the altars,
the work of his hands,
and he will not look at what his fingers have made,
the Asherim and the incense altars.

9In that day his strong cities will be
like the deserted places of the woods and the hilltops,
which they deserted before the sons of Israel;
and there will be desolation.

10For you have forgotten the God of your deliverance,
and have not remembered the Rock of your stronghold;
so you plant pleasant plants,
and set them out with a stranger's vine-slips.

11On the day you plant them, you make them grow,
and in the morning you make your seed blossom;
yet the harvest will be a heap
on the day of possession,
and the pain past cure.

12Woe! The uproar of many peoples —
they roar like the roaring seas;
the thunder of nations —
they thunder like mighty waters!

13The nations thunder like the thunder of many waters,
but He rebukes them, and they flee far away,
chased like chaff on the mountains before the wind,
like whirling dust before the storm.

14At evening, sudden terror;
before morning, they are gone.
This is the portion of those who plunder us,
the lot of those who rob us.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "Damascus… Ephraim" — the two kingdoms that marched on Jerusalem together in 7:1–9, Aram with its capital Damascus and Ephraim, the northern kingdom of Israel. They fall together. "The remnant of Aram will be like the glory of the sons of Israel": like a glory that is fading (v4).

  • v4 "the fat of his flesh will grow lean" — mishman… yerazeh, the two words of 10:16, where the LORD sends leanness among his fat ones, Assyria's. Now the same wasting comes on Jacob.

  • v5 "the Valley of Rephaim" — near Jerusalem, where the Philistines came up against David (2 Samuel 5:18, 22). Its name is the word for the shades of the dead in 14:9, repha'im.

  • v6 "Gleanings will be left in it, as when an olive tree is beaten" — olelot, what the law left on the tree and the vine for the poor: When you beat your olive trees, you shall not go over the branches after you. It shall be for the guest, the orphan and the widow (Deuteronomy 24:20–21). Israel's remnant is the few olives left at the top. The picture returns in 24:13.

  • vv7–8 "his Maker… what his fingers have made" — osehu and asu, the same verb, asah, "to make." Man will look to the One who made him, not to what he made.

  • v9 "the deserted places of the woods and the hilltops, which they deserted before the sons of Israel" — the Greek reads different words: as the Amorites and the Hivites deserted them before the sons of Israel, naming the peoples of the land who left their cities when Israel came in. The Hebrew's amir, "hilltop," is the word for the top of the highest bough in v6, where the last olives hang.

  • vv9–10 "his strong cities… the Rock of your stronghold" — ma'uzzo and ma'uzzekh, the same word. Her strongholds are deserted because she forgot the Rock who was her stronghold. "The God of your deliverance" — yish'ekh, from the root of yeshu'ah in 12:2–3.

  • v11 "the harvest will be a heap on the day of possession" — ned qatsir be-yom nachalah. Ned is a heap, a standing mass, the word for the waters that stood like a wall at the sea (Exodus 15:8). Nachalah is "possession, inheritance," as the Greek also reads it; with other vowels the line reads the harvest flees in a day of sickness. The line is uncertain; either way, the plants that grew in a day bring their planter pain past cure.

  • vv12–14 "before morning, they are gone" — the nations roar like the sea, and one rebuke scatters them overnight. Isaiah tells the night it happened to Assyria's army: The messenger of the LORD went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians. When people rose early in the morning, they were all dead bodies (37:36). "Like whirling dust… like chaff" — the prayer of Psalm 83:13, make them like whirling dust, like chaff before the wind.

chapters.title: A Gift from Beyond the Rivers of Cush
chapters.html:
Isaiah 18

1Woe to the land of whirring wings
beyond the rivers of Cush,

2which sends envoys by the sea,
in vessels of papyrus on the waters!
Go, swift messengers,
to a nation tall and smooth,
to a people feared near and far,
a nation of line upon line, that tramples down,
whose land the rivers divide.

3All you who live in the world,
you who dwell on the earth,
when a signal is raised on the mountains, you will see it;
when the ram's horn is blown, you will hear it.

4For thus the LORD said to me:
"I will be still and look on from My dwelling place,
like shimmering heat in the sunlight,
like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."

5For before the harvest, when the blossom is over
and the flower becomes a ripening grape,
He will cut off the shoots with pruning hooks,
and the spreading branches He will lop off and clear away.

6They will all be left to the birds of prey of the mountains
and to the beasts of the earth;
the birds of prey will summer on them,
and all the beasts of the earth will winter on them.

7At that time a gift will be brought to the LORD of hosts — a people tall and smooth — and from a people feared near and far, a nation of line upon line, that tramples down, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of the LORD of hosts, Mount Zion.

Notes

  • v1 "beyond the rivers of Cush" — Cush is the land the Greek calls Aithiopia, Ethiopia, here and in every verse of Isaiah that names it (Tirhakah king of Cush, 37:9). Its river is the Gihon of Eden, the one winding through all the land of Cush (Genesis 2:13). "Whirring wings" — tsiltsal, a word for whirring or buzzing, the cricket of Deuteronomy 28:42; the Greek reads the wings of ships, their sails.

  • v2 "vessels of papyrus" — kelei gome, the reed of the basket of papyrus in which Moses was set on the Nile (Exodus 2:3).

  • vv2, 7 "a nation of line upon line" — goy qav-qav, the doubled word for a measuring line. It comes again in 28:10, 13, qav la-qav, "line upon line," of a speech Israel will hear with stammering lips and another tongue (28:11). What it says of this nation is not known: one that measures out lands, one strong beyond measure, or one whose speech sounds to Israel like a babble. "Whose land the rivers divide" — bazu, a word found only here and in v7.

  • vv3–6 "I will be still and look on" — the LORD waits like the summer heat and the dew that ripen the crop, and then, before the harvest, cuts the shoots. Mazmerot, "pruning hooks," are what the spears are beaten into in 2:4.

  • v7 "a gift will be brought to the LORD of hosts — a people tall and smooth" — the Hebrew has no from before the first people, only before the second (and from a people feared); as written, the people themselves are the gift. The Greek has from a people both times, and most English supplies it. Isaiah ends with the nations bringing Israel's scattered brothers as an offering to the LORD… to My holy mountain Jerusalem (66:20). Kings will bring You gifts, shai, the word here (Psalm 68:29); Cush will run to stretch out its hands to God (68:31). In Acts an Ethiopian, an official of the queen of the Ethiopians, had come to Jerusalem to worship (Acts 8:27).

chapters.title: The Oracle Against Egypt
chapters.html:
Isaiah 19

1The oracle concerning Egypt.

The LORD is riding on a swift cloud
and is coming to Egypt;
the idols of Egypt tremble before Him,
and the heart of Egypt melts within it.

2"I will stir up Egyptians against Egyptians,
and they will fight, each against his brother
and each against his neighbor,
city against city, kingdom against kingdom.

3The spirit of Egypt will be emptied out within it,
and I will swallow up its counsel;
they will consult the idols and the whisperers,
the ghosts and the spirits.

4I will hand Egypt over
to a hard master,
and a fierce king will rule over them,"
declares the Lord, the LORD of hosts.

5The waters of the sea will dry up,
and the river will be parched and dry;

6the canals will stink;
the streams of Egypt will dwindle and dry up;
reed and rush will wither.

7The bare places by the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile,
and everything sown by the Nile
will dry up, be driven away, and be gone.

8The fishermen will mourn and lament,
all who cast a hook into the Nile;
those who spread nets on the water will languish.

9Those who work combed flax will be ashamed,
and the weavers of white cloth.

10Its foundations will be crushed,
and all who work for wages will be grieved in soul.

11The princes of Zoan are nothing but fools;
the wisest of Pharaoh's counselors give senseless counsel.
How can you say to Pharaoh,
"I am a son of the wise,
a son of ancient kings"?

12Where then are your wise men?
Let them tell you
and make known what the LORD of hosts
has planned against Egypt.

13The princes of Zoan have become fools;
the princes of Memphis are deceived;
those who are the cornerstone of its tribes
have led Egypt astray.

14The LORD has mixed within her
a spirit of confusion,
and they have led Egypt astray in all it does,
as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.

15There will be nothing Egypt can do,
head or tail, palm branch or reed.

Egypt, My People

16In that day Egypt will be like women, and will tremble with fear before the hand that the LORD of hosts shakes over it.

17The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt; everyone to whom it is mentioned will be afraid, because of what the LORD of hosts has planned against it.

18In that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of hosts. One of them will be called the City of Destruction.

19In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a standing stone to the LORD at its border.

20It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of those who crush them, He will send them a deliverer and a defender, and he will rescue them.

21The LORD will make Himself known to Egypt, and Egypt will know the LORD in that day; they will worship with sacrifice and offering, and make vows to the LORD and keep them.

22The LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing; they will return to the LORD, and He will hear their pleas and heal them.

23In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria; Assyria will go into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyria, and Egypt will worship with Assyria.

24In that day Israel will be the third with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the middle of the earth,

25whom the LORD of hosts has blessed, saying: "Blessed be Egypt My people, and Assyria the work of My hands, and Israel My inheritance."

Notes

  • v1 "The LORD is riding on a swift cloud" — the LORD comes to Egypt Himself, and the land's gods and its heart give way. "The heart of Egypt melts" — yimmas, the verb used of Canaan's heart when Israel came (our hearts melted, Joshua 2:11).

  • v4 "a hard master" — adonim qasheh. Qasheh, "hard," is the word of the hard service Egypt laid on Israel (Exodus 1:14). Now Egypt is handed to a hard master.

  • v15 "head or tail, palm branch or reed" — the words of 9:14, where the LORD cut them off from Israel. Here Egypt has no one, high or low, who can do anything.

  • v18 "the City of Destruction" — ir ha-heres. Heres is "tearing down," the verb of the command to Israel about the gods of Canaan: You shall utterly tear them down and utterly break their standing stones (Exodus 23:24); read so, it is the city where the idols are torn down. The Greek has polis asedek, "the City of Righteousness," the name given Jerusalem in 1:26.

  • v19 "a standing stone to the LORD" — matsevah, what the law forbade in Israel: You shall not set up for yourself a standing stone, which the LORD your God hates (Deuteronomy 16:22). In Egypt one stands at the border, for the LORD.

  • vv20–22 "because of those who crush them… Egypt will know the LORD… striking and healing" — the exodus told in reverse. Israel cried out because of the crushing with which Egypt is crushing them (Exodus 3:9, lachats); now Egypt cries out because of lochatsim, "those who crush," and the LORD sends a deliverer, as He did for Israel in Judges (the LORD raised up a deliverer, Judges 3:9). Egypt will know that I am the LORD (Exodus 7:5) was said of the plagues; here it is said of worship. Nagaf, "strike," is the verb of the last plague (the LORD will pass through to strike Egypt, Exodus 12:23), and here the stroke is followed by healing, as I am the LORD your healer was promised Israel (Exodus 15:26).

  • vv24–25 "Blessed be Egypt My people, and Assyria the work of My hands, and Israel My inheritance" — ammi, "My people," the name the LORD gave Israel when He sent Moses to Pharaoh (Exodus 3:7), is given to Egypt, and Israel is the third, a blessing in the middle of the earth, as Abraham was told, In you all the families of the ground shall be blessed (Genesis 12:3). The Greek softens it: Blessed be My people who are in Egypt and who are among the Assyrians.

speech.text: Isaiah 19
The oracle concerning Egypt. The LORD is riding on a swift cloud and is coming to Egypt; the idols of Egypt tremble before Him, and the heart of Egypt melts within it.
"I will stir up Egyptians against Egyptians, and they will fight, each against his brother and each against his neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of Egypt will be emptied out within it, and I will swallow up its counsel; they will consult the idols and the whisperers, the ghosts and the spirits.
I will hand Egypt over to a hard master, and a fierce king will rule over them," declares the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
The waters of the sea will dry up, and the river will be parched and dry;
the canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will dwindle and dry up; reed and rush will wither.
The bare places by the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile, and everything sown by the Nile will dry up, be driven away, and be gone.
The fishermen will mourn and lament, all who cast a hook into the Nile; those who spread nets on the water will languish.
Those who work combed flax will be ashamed, and the weavers of white cloth.
Its foundations will be crushed, and all who work for wages will be grieved in soul.
The princes of Zoan are nothing but fools; the wisest of Pharaoh's counselors give senseless counsel. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of the wise, a son of ancient kings"?
Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you and make known what the LORD of hosts has planned against Egypt.
The princes of Zoan have become fools; the princes of Memphis are deceived; those who are the cornerstone of its tribes have led Egypt astray.
The LORD has mixed within her a spirit of confusion, and they have led Egypt astray in all it does, as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.
There will be nothing Egypt can do, head or tail, palm branch or reed.
Egypt, My People
In that day Egypt will be like women, and will tremble with fear before the hand that the LORD of hosts shakes over it.
The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt; everyone to whom it is mentioned will be afraid, because of what the LORD of hosts has planned against it.
In that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of hosts. One of them will be called the City of Destruction.
In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a standing stone to the LORD at its border.

It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of those who crush them, He will send them a deliverer and a defender, and he will rescue them.
The LORD will make Himself known to Egypt, and Egypt will know the LORD in that day; they will worship with sacrifice and offering, and make vows to the LORD and keep them.
The LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing; they will return to the LORD, and He will hear their pleas and heal them.
In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria; Assyria will go into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyria, and Egypt will worship with Assyria.
In that day Israel will be the third with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the middle of the earth,
whom the LORD of hosts has blessed, saying: "Blessed be Egypt My people, and Assyria the work of My hands, and Israel My inheritance."

chapters.title: Naked and Barefoot
chapters.html:
Isaiah 20

1In the year that the commander in chief came to Ashdod, when Sargon king of Assyria sent him, and he fought against Ashdod and took it,

2at that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, "Go, loosen the sackcloth from your waist and take your sandals off your feet." He did so, walking naked and barefoot.

3The LORD said, "As My servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot three years as a sign and a portent against Egypt and Cush,

4so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, with buttocks uncovered, the nakedness of Egypt.

5They will be dismayed and ashamed because of Cush, whom they looked to, and Egypt, their boast.

6In that day the inhabitants of this coastland will say, 'This is what has become of the one we looked to, to whom we fled for help, to be rescued from the king of Assyria! How then will we escape?'"

Notes

  • v1 "the commander in chief… Sargon king of Assyria" — tartan, the title of an Assyrian officer, the one sent with others to Jerusalem in 2 Kings 18:17. Sargon is named nowhere else in the Bible. The Greek has neither name right (Tanathan… Arna).

  • v2 "spoke through Isaiah" — be-yad, literally "by the hand of": the message is the act. Isaiah says nothing in this chapter; for three years he walks, and the walking is the word.

  • v3 "a sign and a portent" — ot u-mofet, the words of 8:18, Here am I and the children the LORD has given me, as signs and portents in Israel. Isaiah himself is now one.

  • vv5–6 "Cush, whom they looked to… the one we looked to" — mabbat, "what one looks to," twice: the people of the coast had looked to Egypt and Cush, the powers of the Nile, against Assyria, and they watch them led away naked. Isaiah 18 and 19 have just spoken of those two lands; here the hope placed in them is ended.

chapters.title: Fallen, Fallen Is Babylon
chapters.html:
Isaiah 21

1The oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea.

Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negev,
it comes from the wilderness,
from a terrible land.

2A hard vision has been told to me:
the traitor betrays,
and the destroyer destroys.
Go up, Elam!
Lay siege, Media!
All the sighing she caused
I bring to an end.

3So my loins are filled with anguish;
pangs have seized me,
like the pangs of a woman in labor;
I am bent double at what I hear;
I am terrified at what I see.

4My heart staggers;
horror has overwhelmed me;
the twilight I longed for
has been turned to trembling for me.

5They set the table,
they spread the rugs,
they eat, they drink.
Rise up, commanders;
anoint the shield!

6For thus the Lord said to me:
"Go, post a watchman;
let him report what he sees.

7When he sees riders,
horsemen in pairs,
riders on donkeys,
riders on camels,
let him listen closely,
very closely."

8Then he cried out like a lion:
"On the watchtower, Lord,
I stand continually by day,
and at my post I am stationed
every night.

9Here comes a man in a chariot,
with horsemen in pairs!"
Then he answered:
"Fallen, fallen is Babylon,
and all the carved images of her gods
He has shattered to the ground."

10My threshed one, the grain of my threshing floor,
what I have heard from the LORD of hosts,
the God of Israel,
I have told you.

Dumah

11The oracle concerning Dumah.

One calls to me from Seir:
"Watchman, what of the night?
Watchman, what of the night?"

12The watchman says:
"Morning comes, and also the night.
If you would ask, ask;
come back again."

Arabia

13The oracle concerning Arabia.

In the thickets of Arabia you will spend the night,
you caravans of Dedanites.

14To the thirsty bring water,
you who live in the land of Tema;
meet the fugitive with bread.

15For they have fled from the swords,
from the drawn sword,
from the bent bow,
and from the weight of battle.

16For thus the Lord said to me: "Within a year, like the years of a hired man, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end;

17and the remnant of the archers, the mighty men of the sons of Kedar, will be few; for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken."

Notes

  • v1 "the wilderness of the sea" — a riddling name; v9 says what it is: Babylon. "Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media!" (v2): the Medes, named in 13:17 as the power that takes Babylon, with Elam beside them.

  • v5 "They set the table… they eat, they drink. Rise up, commanders" — a feast broken by a call to arms. Daniel tells Babylon's last night in the same way: Belshazzar's feast, and that very night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed (Daniel 5:1, 30). "Spread the rugs" — tsafoh ha-tsafit; tsafit is found only here. The verb tsafah is also "to watch," the root of watchman (v6) and watchtower (v8), and read so the line is keep the watch. The Greek has only Prepare the table, eat, drink. "Anoint the shield" — mishchu, the verb of anointing: leather shields were rubbed with oil, and Saul's was no longer anointed with oil (2 Samuel 1:21).

  • v8 "he cried out like a lion" — va-yiqra aryeh, literally "he cried, a lion." Who cries, and why a lion, is not clear: the watchman shouting with a lion's voice is the plain reading. The Greek reads different words, call Uriah to the watchtower.

  • v9 "Fallen, fallen is Babylon" — nafelah nafelah Bavel. Revelation takes up the cry twice, Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great (Revelation 14:8; 18:2).

  • v10 "My threshed one, the grain of my threshing floor" — medushati u-ven gorni, literally "my threshed one and son of my threshing floor": the prophet's own people, beaten on the floor like grain, are the ones he tells.

  • vv11–12 "Dumah… Seir" — Seir is Edom's mountain (Genesis 36:8), and dumah is "silence" (my soul would soon have dwelt in silence, Psalm 94:17). The watchman's answer is in words close to Aramaic, tiv'ayun… be'ayu… eteyu, "ask… come": morning comes, but night as well; they may come back and ask again.

  • vv16–17 "like the years of a hired man" — the measure set for Moab in 16:14: counted exactly, no more. Kedar is one of Ishmael's sons (Genesis 25:13).

chapters.title: The Key of the House of David
chapters.html:
Isaiah 22

1The oracle concerning the Valley of Vision.

What is the matter with you,
that you have all gone up to the housetops,

2you who are full of shouting,
a tumultuous city, an exultant town?
Your slain were not slain by the sword,
nor did they die in battle.

3All your rulers fled together;
without a bow they were captured.
All of you who were found were captured together,
though they had fled far away.

4So I said: "Look away from me;
let me weep bitterly;
do not try to comfort me
over the destruction of the daughter of my people."

5For the Lord GOD of hosts has a day
of tumult and trampling and confusion
in the Valley of Vision,
a battering down of walls
and a crying out to the mountain.

6Elam took up the quiver,
with chariots of men and horsemen,
and Kir bared the shield.

7Your choicest valleys were full of chariots,
and the horsemen took their stand at the gate.

8He stripped away the covering of Judah.

In that day you looked to the weapons of the House of the Forest,

9and you saw that the breaches in the City of David were many. You collected the waters of the lower pool,

10and you counted the houses of Jerusalem, and tore down the houses to fortify the wall.

11You made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you did not look to Him who did it, or see Him who planned it long ago.

12In that day the Lord GOD of hosts called
for weeping and mourning,
for baldness and putting on sackcloth;

13but instead there was joy and gladness,
killing oxen and slaughtering sheep,
eating meat and drinking wine:
"Let us eat and drink,
for tomorrow we die."

14The LORD of hosts has revealed Himself in my hearing: "Surely this iniquity will not be atoned for you until you die," says the Lord GOD of hosts.

Shebna and Eliakim

15Thus says the Lord GOD of hosts: "Go, come to this steward, to Shebna, who is over the household, and say:

16'What have you here, and whom have you here, that you have cut out a tomb for yourself here — cutting out his tomb on the height, carving a dwelling for himself in the rock?

17The LORD is about to hurl you away, hurl you, you strong man, and grip you hard;

18He will wind you round and round and throw you like a ball into a wide land. There you will die, and there will be your splendid chariots, you disgrace to your master's house.

19I will thrust you from your office, and from your post he will pull you down.

20And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call My servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah,

21and I will clothe him with your robe, and bind your sash on him, and put your authority in his hand; and he will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.

22I will set the key of the house of David on his shoulder; he will open, and no one will shut; he will shut, and no one will open.

23I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will become a throne of honor for his father's house.

24They will hang on him the whole weight of his father's house, the offspring and the offshoots, every small vessel, from the bowls to all the jars.

25In that day, declares the LORD of hosts, the peg that was driven into a firm place will give way; it will be cut down and fall, and the load that was on it will be cut off, for the LORD has spoken.'"

Notes

  • v1 "the Valley of Vision" — the oracles on the nations come home: this one is against Jerusalem itself (vv9–10), the place of Isaiah's visions. The city is on its rooftops, celebrating, while the prophet weeps (v4).

  • vv5–6 "a battering down of walls… and Kir bared the shield" — meqarqar qir, "a tearing down of walls," and then Qir, the land of Kir: the same sound, the wall and the people who come to break it.

  • vv8–11 "you looked to the weapons… you did not look to Him who did it" — va-tabbet and lo hibbattem, the same verb, nabat, "look to." They looked to the armory of the House of the Forest (Solomon's House of the Forest of Lebanon, where he put his gold shields, 1 Kings 7:2; 10:17), counted houses, collected water, built up the wall, the work Hezekiah did against Assyria (to stop the water of the springs… built up all the wall that was broken down, 2 Chronicles 32:3–5). What they did not look to was the One who made it all, as in 17:7, man will look to his Maker.

  • v13 "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die" — Paul quotes it in the Greek, of those who deny the resurrection: if the dead are not raised, Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die (1 Corinthians 15:32).

  • v14 "Surely this iniquity will not be atoned for you" — yekhuppar, the word spoken over Isaiah's own lips, your sin is atoned for (6:7). The coal was given to him; to the feasting city the same word is refused.

  • vv15, 20 "Shebna, who is over the household… My servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah" — al ha-bayit, the title of the king's chief steward (1 Kings 4:6). When Assyria comes to Jerusalem's walls, it is Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, who goes out, and Shebna the secretary with him (36:3): the office has passed as this chapter says.

  • v22 "the key of the house of David on his shoulder; he will open, and no one will shut" — al shikhmo, the words of 9:6, the government shall be on his shoulder. Revelation gives the line to Christ: the Holy One, the True One, who has the key of David, who opens and no one will shut (Revelation 3:7).

  • vv23–25 "a throne of honor… the whole weight of his father's house… the load" — kavod, "honor," is also "weight": the peg is made a seat of honor, and the family hangs its whole weight on it until it gives way. Ha-massa, "the load," is the word the chapter opened with, the oracle; the burden laid on the peg falls with it.

chapters.title: The Oracle Against Tyre
chapters.html:
Isaiah 23

1The oracle concerning Tyre.

Wail, ships of Tarshish,
for it is laid waste, without house or harbor!
From the land of Kittim it is revealed to them.

2Be silent, inhabitants of the coast,
merchants of Sidon,
whose envoys crossed the sea
and filled you;

3on many waters
the grain of Shihor,
the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue,
and she was the marketplace of the nations.

4Be ashamed, Sidon,
for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea:
"I have not been in labor or given birth;
I have not raised young men
or brought up young women."

5When the report comes to Egypt,
they will be in anguish at the report about Tyre.

6Cross over to Tarshish;
wail, inhabitants of the coast!

7Is this your exultant city,
whose origin is from days of old,
whose feet carried her
to live as a guest far away?

8Who has planned this against Tyre,
the giver of crowns,
whose merchants were princes,
whose traders were the honored of the earth?

9The LORD of hosts has planned it,
to defile the pride of all glory,
to bring into contempt all the honored of the earth.

10Overflow your land like the Nile,
daughter of Tarshish;
there is no restraint anymore.

11He has stretched out His hand over the sea;
He has shaken kingdoms;
the LORD has given command concerning Canaan
to destroy its strongholds.

12He said: "You will exult no more,
you oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon.
Arise, cross over to Kittim;
even there you will have no rest."

13Look at the land of the Chaldeans!
This is the people that was not;
Assyria founded it for desert creatures.
They set up their siege towers;
they stripped her palaces bare;
they made her a ruin.

14Wail, ships of Tarshish,
for your stronghold is laid waste!

15And it shall come to pass in that day, that Tyre will be forgotten seventy years, like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years it will be with Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:

16"Take a harp,
go around the city,
forgotten prostitute!
Play well, sing many songs,
that you may be remembered."

17And it shall come to pass at the end of seventy years, that the LORD will visit Tyre, and she will return to her wages and play the prostitute with all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth.

18Her merchandise and her wages will be holy to the LORD; they will not be stored up or hoarded, for her merchandise will go to those who dwell before the LORD, for food to eat their fill and for fine clothing.

Notes

  • v1 "ships of Tarshish… the land of Kittim" — the far western sea route. Tarshish and Kittim are sons of Javan in the table of nations (Genesis 10:4); the ships of Tarshish were among the proud things brought low on the day of the LORD (2:16).

  • v7 "to live as a guest far away" — la-gur, the verb of the guest: Tyre's colonists went out to live in other men's lands.

  • v8 "whose traders were the honored of the earth" — kin'aneha, literally "her Canaanites," set beside her merchants: the name of the people had become a word for a trader. In v11 the LORD gives command concerning Canaan, the merchant coast itself.

  • v11 "He has stretched out His hand over the sea" — yado natah al ha-yam, the act of Moses at the Red Sea (Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, Exodus 14:21), and the words of the refrain, His hand is still stretched out (5:25 to 10:4). Here the hand is over the sea Tyre ruled.

  • v13 "Look at the land of the Chaldeans! This is the people that was not" — the verse is hard. As it stands, Babylon's land is held up to Tyre as a warning: a people that was nothing, given by Assyria to the desert creatures, its towers and palaces ruined. The Greek reads a shorter line: and to the land of the Chaldeans, and this has been laid waste by the Assyrians; its wall has fallen. The read form bachunav, "its siege towers," is followed.

  • vv15–18 "the song of the prostitute… her wages will be holy to the LORD" — etnan, the prostitute's wage, which the law forbade to be brought to the LORD: You shall not bring the wages of a prostitute… into the house of the LORD your God (Deuteronomy 23:18). Tyre's trade is pictured as selling herself to every kingdom, and at the end her wages are turned over to the LORD's people. Seventy years is the length of Babylon's rule over the nations in Jeremiah 25:11.

Overflow your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish; there is no restraint anymore.

He said: "You will exult no more, you oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon. Arise, cross over to Kittim; even there you will have no rest."
Look at the land of the Chaldeans! This is the people that was not; Assyria founded it for desert creatures. They set up their siege towers; they stripped her palaces bare; they made her a ruin.
Wail, ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is laid waste!
And it shall come to pass in that day, that Tyre will be forgotten seventy years, like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years it will be with Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:
"Take a harp, go around the city, forgotten prostitute! Play well, sing many songs, that you may be remembered."

And it shall come to pass at the end of seventy years, that the LORD will visit Tyre, and she will return to her wages and play the prostitute with all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth.

Her merchandise and her wages will be holy to the LORD; they will not be stored up or hoarded, for her merchandise will go to those who dwell before the LORD, for food to eat their fill and for fine clothing.

chapters.title: The Earth Laid Waste
chapters.html:
Isaiah 24

1The LORD is about to empty the earth and lay it waste;
He will twist its surface
and scatter its inhabitants.

2It will be the same for the people as for the priest,
for the servant as for his master,
for the maid as for her mistress,
for the buyer as for the seller,
for the lender as for the borrower,
for the creditor as for the debtor.

3The earth will be utterly emptied
and utterly plundered,
for the LORD has spoken this word.

4The earth mourns and withers;
the world languishes and withers;
the high ones of the people of the earth languish.

5The earth is defiled under its inhabitants,
for they have transgressed the instructions,
violated the statute,
broken the everlasting covenant.

6Therefore a curse devours the earth,
and those who live on it bear their guilt;
therefore the inhabitants of the earth are burned,
and few men are left.

7The new wine mourns;
the vine languishes;
all the merry-hearted sigh.

8The joy of the tambourines has ceased;
the noise of the revelers has ended;
the joy of the harp has ceased.

9They no longer drink wine with singing;
strong drink is bitter to those who drink it.

10The city of chaos is broken down;
every house is shut, so that no one can enter.

11There is an outcry in the streets for lack of wine;
all joy has grown dark;
the gladness of the earth is banished.

12Desolation is left in the city;
the gate is battered into ruins.

13For so it will be in the middle of the earth,
among the peoples,
as when an olive tree is beaten,
as at the gleaning when the grape harvest is done.

14They lift up their voices; they sing for joy;
over the majesty of the LORD they shout from the west.

15Therefore in the east give glory to the LORD;
in the coastlands of the sea,
to the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

16From the ends of the earth we hear songs:
"Glory to the Righteous One!"
But I say, "I waste away, I waste away!
Woe is me!
The traitors betray;
with betrayal the traitors betray."

17Terror and the pit and the snare
are upon you, inhabitant of the earth!

18Whoever flees at the sound of the terror
will fall into the pit,
and whoever climbs out of the pit
will be caught in the snare.
For the lattices on high are opened,
and the foundations of the earth shake.

19The earth is utterly broken;
the earth is split apart;
the earth is violently shaken.

20The earth staggers like a drunkard;
it sways like a hut;
its transgression lies heavy on it,
and it falls, and will not rise again.

21And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD will punish
the host of heaven in heaven,
and the kings of the earth on the earth.

22They will be gathered together
as prisoners in a pit;
they will be shut up in a prison,
and after many days they will be punished.

23Then the moon will be confounded
and the sun ashamed,
for the LORD of hosts reigns
on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem,
and before His elders, glory.

Notes

  • v1 "to empty the earth and lay it waste" — boqeq ha-arets u-voleqah, two verbs that sound alike, as v3 doubles each: hibboq tibboq… hibboz tibboz, "utterly emptied… utterly plundered." Baz, "plunder," is the last word of the child's name in 8:1.

  • v2 "the same for the people as for the priest" — ka-am ka-kohen, the words of Hosea 4:9. Every rank and trade is named in pairs, and none escapes.

  • vv5, 18 "broken the everlasting covenant… the lattices on high are opened" — berit olam, the covenant God made with every living soul after the flood (to remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living soul, Genesis 9:16). And the earth is undone as it was then: arubbot, the lattices of the heavens that were opened for the flood (Genesis 7:11).

  • v10 "The city of chaos" — qiryat tohu, the tohu of Genesis 1:2, the earth formless before the first word. The city is unmade.

  • v13 "as when an olive tree is beaten, as at the gleaning" — the picture of 17:6, now for the whole earth: a few left at the top of the tree.

  • v16 "I waste away, I waste away" — razi li, razi li, a word found only here. Razah is "to grow lean" (10:16, razon, leanness); in Aramaic raz is "a secret" (Daniel 2:18), and read so the line is My secret is mine. "The traitors betray; with betrayal the traitors betray" — the root bagad five times in two lines, as in 21:2.

  • v17 "Terror and the pit and the snare" — pachad va-fachat va-fach, three words that sound alike. Jeremiah uses the line of Moab (Jeremiah 48:43).

  • v20 "it sways like a hut" — ka-melunah, the watchman's hut in a cucumber field of 1:8, where Zion was left alone.

  • vv21–22 "the host of heaven in heaven… shut up in a prison, and after many days they will be punished" — the powers above are judged with the kings below. 1 Enoch tells of the same: a prison for the stars of heaven and for the host of heaven (1 Enoch 18:14), and the watchers bound for seventy generations… until the day of their judgment (10:12).

  • v23 "before His elders, glory" — as at Sinai: Moses went up, and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel. They saw the God of Israel (Exodus 24:9–10). "The moon… the sun" — ha-levanah, "the white one," and ha-chammah, "the hot one," the poetic names.

chapters.title: He Will Swallow Up Death Forever
chapters.html:
Isaiah 25

1LORD, You are my God;
I will exalt You; I will praise Your name;
for You have done wonders,
plans formed long ago,
faithful and sure.

2For You have made the city a heap,
the fortified town a ruin;
the strangers' palace is a city no more;
it will never be rebuilt.

3Therefore a strong people will glorify You;
the city of ruthless nations will fear You.

4For You have been a stronghold to the poor,
a stronghold to the needy in his distress,
a shelter from the storm, a shade from the heat;
for the breath of the ruthless is like a storm against a wall,

5like heat in a dry land.
You subdue the uproar of strangers;
as heat is cooled by the shade of a cloud,
the song of the ruthless is brought low.

6On this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples
a feast of rich food, a feast of aged wine,
of rich food full of marrow,
of aged wine well refined.

7On this mountain He will swallow up
the covering that is cast over all peoples,
the veil that is spread over all nations.

8He will swallow up death forever;
the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from all faces,
and the reproach of His people He will take away from all the earth,
for the LORD has spoken.

9It will be said in that day:
"This is our God;
we have waited for Him, and He will save us.
This is the LORD; we have waited for Him;
let us be glad and rejoice in His deliverance."

10For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain,
and Moab will be trampled down where he stands,
as straw is trampled down in a dung pit.

11He will spread out his hands in it,
as a swimmer spreads his hands to swim,
but his pride will be brought low
with every stroke of his hands.

12The high fortifications of your walls
He will bring down, lay low,
cast to the ground, to the dust.

Notes

  • v1 "You have done wonders, plans formed long ago" — pele, "wonder," and etsot, "plans, counsels": the two words of the child's first name in 9:6, Wonderful Counselor, pele yo'ets. "Faithful and sure" — emunah omen, two forms of the root of amen.

  • vv6–8 "a feast… for all peoples… He will swallow up death forever" — the meal is set on Zion for every nation. Jesus speaks of it: many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 8:11).

  • vv7–8 "He will swallow up the covering… He will swallow up death" — bila, the same verb twice. Death is the great swallower, let us swallow them alive like Sheol (Proverbs 1:12); here it is swallowed. "Forever" — la-netsach; netsach can also mean "victory," as in the glory, the victory and the majesty (1 Chronicles 29:11), and Paul's Greek reads it so: Death is swallowed up in victory (1 Corinthians 15:54). The Greek of Isaiah reads the line the other way, Death, having prevailed, swallowed.

  • v8 "the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from all faces" — Revelation takes up the line: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more (Revelation 21:4).

  • v9 "His deliverance" — yeshu'ato, the word of 12:2–3, God is my deliverance.

  • v10 "a dung pit" — madmenah, the dung pit, and also the name of a town in 10:31, Madmenah is in flight.

  • v11 "with every stroke of his hands" — im arbot yadav, a word found only here; it is taken as the swimmer's strokes, and the range runs to "the cunning of his hands."

chapters.title: Your Dead Will Live
chapters.html:
Isaiah 26

1In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah:

"We have a strong city;
He sets deliverance
as its walls and rampart.

2Open the gates,
that the righteous nation may enter,
the nation that keeps faith.

3The mind that leans on You
You keep in peace, peace,
because it trusts in You.

4Trust in the LORD forever,
for in Yah, the LORD,
is an everlasting Rock.

5For He has brought low
those who live on the height, the lofty city;
He lays it low, lays it low to the ground,
casts it to the dust.

6The foot tramples it,
the feet of the poor,
the steps of the needy."

7The path of the righteous is level;
You make smooth the way of the righteous.

8In the path of Your judgments, LORD,
we wait for You;
Your name and Your remembrance
are the desire of our soul.

9My soul longs for You in the night;
my spirit within me seeks You at dawn;
for when Your judgments are on the earth,
the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.

10If favor is shown to the wicked,
he does not learn righteousness;
in the land of uprightness he deals wrongly
and does not see the majesty of the LORD.

11LORD, Your hand is lifted up,
but they do not see it.
Let them see Your zeal for the people, and be ashamed;
let the fire for Your adversaries consume them.

12LORD, You will establish peace for us,
for all that we have done
You have done for us.

13LORD our God,
other masters besides You have ruled over us,
but Your name alone we call to mind.

14The dead do not live;
the shades do not rise;
so You have punished and destroyed them,
and wiped out all memory of them.

15You have increased the nation, LORD;
You have increased the nation; You are glorified;
You have extended all the borders of the land.

16LORD, in distress they sought You;
they poured out a whispered prayer
when Your discipline was on them.

17Like a woman with child
who writhes and cries out in her pangs
when she is near to giving birth,
so were we before You, LORD.

18We were with child; we writhed;
we gave birth, as it were, to wind.
We have brought no deliverance to the earth,
and no inhabitants of the world have been born.

19Your dead will live;
my dead ones will rise.
Awake and sing for joy,
you who dwell in the dust!
For your dew is a dew of lights,
and the earth will give birth to the shades.

20Come, my people, enter your rooms,
and shut your door behind you;
hide yourselves for a little while,
until the fury has passed by.

21For the LORD is about to come out from His place
to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity;
the earth will uncover the blood shed on it,
and will no longer cover its slain.

Notes

  • vv1, 18 "He sets deliverance as its walls… We have brought no deliverance to the earth" — yeshu'ah (12:2–3, 25:9). The city's walls are the LORD's deliverance; the people, for all their labor, could bring none.

  • v3 "You keep in peace, peace" — shalom shalom, the word twice, for peace complete. "The mind that leans on You" — yetser samukh, the yetser of the shaping of the human heart (Genesis 8:21), here steadied; yetser and titsor, "You keep," sound alike.

  • v4 "an everlasting Rock" — tsur olamim, "a rock of ages," with Yah, the LORD as in 12:2.

  • v8 "Your name and Your remembrance" — the pair of Exodus 3:15, This is My name forever, and this is My remembrance for all generations.

  • v13 "other masters… have ruled over us" — be'alunu, from ba'al, "master, owner," the word that is also the god Baal's name.

  • vv14, 19 "The dead do not live; the shades do not rise… Your dead will live; my dead ones will rise" — the same words, metim, repha'im, qum, said first of the oppressors (v14) and then turned for the LORD's own: the earth will give birth to the shades. "Awake" — heqitsu, the verb of Daniel 12:2, many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake. "My dead ones" — nevelati, "my corpse," a singular with a plural verb, read as the speaker's own dead together; the Greek has those in the tombs will be raised.

  • vv17–19 "we gave birth, as it were, to wind… the earth will give birth to the shades" — naphal, "fall," is used for being born: in v18 no inhabitants fell, were born; in v19 the earth makes fall, gives birth to, the dead. Israel's labor brought forth nothing; the LORD's dew brings forth the dead.

  • v20 "enter your rooms, and shut your door… until the fury has passed by" — as on the night of the first Passover: None of you shall go out from the doorway of his house until morning. The LORD will pass through to strike Egypt (Exodus 12:22–23); ya'avor, "pass by," is the same verb.

  • v21 "the earth will uncover the blood shed on it" — dameha, "its bloods," the plural of The voice of your brother's bloods is crying out to Me from the ground (Genesis 4:10). The ground that took Abel's blood gives up all it has hidden.

chapters.title: Leviathan and the Vineyard
chapters.html:
Isaiah 27

1In that day the LORD will punish,
with His hard and great and strong sword,
Leviathan the fleeing serpent,
Leviathan the twisting serpent,
and He will kill the dragon that is in the sea.

The Song of the Vineyard Again

2In that day:
"A pleasant vineyard, sing of it!

3I, the LORD, am its keeper;
every moment I water it;
so that no one may harm it,
I keep it night and day.

4I have no wrath.
If only I had briers and thorns to battle!
I would march against them;
I would burn them up together.

5Or let them take hold of My stronghold;
let them make peace with Me;
let them make peace with Me."

6In days to come Jacob will take root;
Israel will blossom and put out shoots,
and fill the face of the world with fruit.

7Has He struck him
as He struck those who struck him?
Or has he been slain
as his slayers were slain?

8By driving her out, by sending her away, You contended with her;
He removed her with His fierce wind
in the day of the east wind.

9Therefore by this the iniquity of Jacob will be atoned for,
and this will be the full fruit of the removal of his sin:
when he makes all the stones of the altar
like chalk stones crushed to pieces,
no Asherim or incense altars will remain standing.

10For the fortified city is alone,
a home deserted and forsaken like the wilderness;
there the calf grazes,
there it lies down and strips its branches.

11When its boughs are dry, they are broken off;
women come and make fires of them.
For this is a people without understanding;
therefore He who made them will not have compassion on them;
He who formed them will show them no favor.

12And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD will thresh out the grain from the flowing Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt, and you will be gathered one by one, sons of Israel.

13And it shall come to pass in that day, that a great ram's horn will be blown, and those who were lost in the land of Assyria and those who were driven out to the land of Egypt will come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain at Jerusalem.

Notes

  • v1 "Leviathan the fleeing serpent… the dragon that is in the sea" — livyatan nachash bariach, the creature of Job 26:13, His hand pierced the fleeing serpent, and of Psalm 74:14, You crushed the heads of Leviathan. Tannin, "dragon," is the word of the great sea-monsters of Genesis 1:21. The Greek renders drakonta ophin, "dragon, serpent," and Revelation joins the same two words for the devil: the great dragon, the ancient serpent (Revelation 12:9).

  • vv2–5 "A pleasant vineyard, sing of it!… If only I had briers and thorns" — the song of the vineyard in 5:1–7 sung again with the ending reversed. There the LORD let the vineyard go to briers and thorns (shamir va-shayit, 5:6) and forbade the clouds to rain on it; here He waters it every moment, and the briers and thorns are what He would fight for it.

  • v5 "let them make peace with Me; let them make peace with Me" — ya'aseh shalom li, shalom ya'aseh li, the same words twice with the order turned round.

  • v9 "the iniquity of Jacob will be atoned for" — yekhuppar, the word refused to Jerusalem in 22:14, Surely this iniquity will not be atoned for you until you die. Here it is given, when the altars of other gods are ground to chalk.

  • v11 "He who made them… He who formed them" — osehu… yotsro, the LORD as Maker and as potter (yatsar, the verb of Genesis 2:7, The LORD God shaped the human of dust).

  • v12 "the flowing Euphrates" — shibbolet ha-nahar. Shibbolet is an ear of grain, and also a stream in flood (the flood sweeps over me, Psalm 69:2); it is the password of Judges 12:6, Shibboleth. Here both senses meet: the LORD threshes from the river's flood, and gathers Israel one by one like gleaned ears. The span is the land promised to Abram, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates (Genesis 15:18).

  • v13 "a great ram's horn will be blown" — shofar gadol. Jesus speaks of the gathering in the same way: He will send out His angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather His chosen from the four winds (Matthew 24:31).

chapters.title: A Cornerstone in Zion
chapters.html:
Isaiah 28

1Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim,
and to the fading flower of its glorious beauty,
which is on the head of the rich valley,
of those struck down by wine!

2The Lord has one who is mighty and strong:
like a storm of hail, a destroying tempest,
like a storm of mighty waters overflowing,
he casts it down to the earth with his hand.

3The proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim
will be trampled underfoot;

4and the fading flower of its glorious beauty,
which is on the head of the rich valley,
will be like a first-ripe fig before the summer:
whoever sees it
swallows it as soon as it is in his hand.

5In that day the LORD of hosts will be
a crown of glory
and a diadem of beauty
to the remnant of His people,

6and a spirit of justice
to him who sits in judgment,
and strength to those
who turn back the battle at the gate.

7These also reel with wine
and stagger with strong drink;
priest and prophet reel with strong drink;
they are swallowed up by wine;
they stagger with strong drink;
they reel in vision;
they stumble in giving judgment.

8For all the tables are full of vomit and filth,
with no place left.

9"Whom will he teach knowledge,
and to whom will he explain the message?
Those weaned from milk,
those taken from the breast?

10For it is rule upon rule, rule upon rule,
line upon line, line upon line,
a little here, a little there."

11Indeed, with stammering lips
and another tongue
He will speak to this people,

12to whom He said,
"This is rest; give rest to the weary;
this is repose";
yet they would not listen.

13So the word of the LORD will be to them
rule upon rule, rule upon rule,
line upon line, line upon line,
a little here, a little there,
so that they will go, and fall backward,
and be broken, and snared, and taken.

A Covenant with Death

14Therefore hear the word of the LORD, you scoffers,
who rule this people in Jerusalem!

15Because you have said,
"We have made a covenant with death,
and with Sheol we have an agreement;
when the overwhelming scourge passes through,
it will not come to us;
for we have made lies our refuge,
and in falsehood we have taken shelter";

16therefore thus says the Lord GOD:
"I am laying in Zion a stone,
a tested stone,
a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation:
whoever believes will not be in haste.

17I will make justice the line,
and righteousness the plumb line;
hail will sweep away the refuge of lies,
and waters will overflow the hiding place."

18Then your covenant with death will be wiped out,
and your agreement with Sheol will not stand;
when the overwhelming scourge passes through,
you will be trampled down by it.

19As often as it passes through it will take you;
for morning by morning it will pass through,
by day and by night;
and it will be sheer terror
to understand the message.

20For the bed is too short to stretch out on,
and the blanket too narrow to wrap oneself in.

21For the LORD will rise up as at Mount Perazim;
as in the Valley of Gibeon He will be stirred up,
to do His deed — strange is His deed! —
and to work His work — alien is His work!

22So now, do not scoff,
or your bonds will be made stronger;
for I have heard a full destruction decreed
by the Lord GOD of hosts
on the whole earth.

The Farmer

23Give ear, and hear my voice;
listen, and hear my speech.

24Does the plowman plow all day for sowing?
Does he keep breaking up and harrowing his ground?

25When he has leveled its surface,
does he not scatter dill and sow cumin,
and put in wheat in rows
and barley in its plot,
and spelt as its border?

26His God instructs him in the right way;
He teaches him.

27Dill is not threshed with a threshing sledge,
nor is a cart wheel rolled over cumin;
dill is beaten out with a stick,
and cumin with a rod.

28Grain for bread is crushed,
but one does not thresh it forever;
when he drives his cart wheel and his horses over it,
he does not crush it.

29This also comes from the LORD of hosts;
He is wonderful in counsel
and great in wisdom.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim… on the head of the rich valley" — Samaria, Ephraim's capital, a city built on a hill (He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer, 1 Kings 16:24): the crown on the valley's head. Halumei yayin, "struck down by wine," is the phrase the note on 16:8 cites.

  • vv1, 5 "the proud crown… a crown of glory" — ateret, twice: the crown of Ephraim's drunken pride fades, and the LORD Himself will be the crown of His remnant.

  • vv9–13 "rule upon rule, line upon line" — tsav la-tsav… qav la-qav. Qav is a measuring line (v17; 18:2), and tsav is from the root of command; but the syllables are short and doubled, and v9 sets them beside infants just weaned, so the mockers may be imitating a child's babble or a teacher's drill. The LORD answers in kind: since they will not hear plain words, He will speak with stammering lips and another tongue, the speech of a foreign army. Paul quotes v11 of speaking in tongues (1 Corinthians 14:21). The Greek has affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope.

  • v13 "fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken" — the verbs of 8:15, they shall fall and be broken; they shall be snared and taken, of those who stumble over the LORD.

  • v15 "a covenant with death… an agreement with Sheol" — chozeh, literally "a seer, a vision," here a pact; v18 has chazut, from the same root. The rulers have bought safety with lies.

  • v16 "I am laying in Zion a stone… whoever believes will not be in haste" — ha-ma'amin lo yachish, "will not hurry, will not flee in panic." The Greek has will not be put to shame, and Peter and Paul quote that: whoever believes in Him will not be put to shame (1 Peter 2:6; Romans 9:33). Paul joins it to a stone of stumbling from 8:14.

  • vv17–18 "justice the line… your covenant with death will be wiped out" — qav, the word the mockers babbled in v10, is now the builder's line the LORD lays. Kuppar, "wiped out," is the verb of atonement (6:7; 22:14; 27:9): the same covering that takes away sin cancels their pact.

  • v21 "as at Mount Perazim… the Valley of Gibeon… strange is His deed" — the places where the LORD fought for Israel: The LORD has broken through my enemies before me (2 Samuel 5:20), and at Gibeon, where He threw the Amorites into panic before Israel (Joshua 10:10). Now He rises the same way against His own people: zar, "strange," and nokhriyyah, "foreign," the words for strangers and foreigners.

  • v22 "a full destruction decreed… on the whole earth" — kalah ve-necheratsah, the words of 10:23.

  • vv26, 29 "His God instructs him… He is wonderful in counsel" — hifli etsah, pele and etsah, the two words of 9:6, Wonderful Counselor, as in 25:1. The farmer's sense of when to plow and how to thresh each crop is called teaching from God (yorennu, the root of torah).

chapters.title: Woe to Ariel
chapters.html:
Isaiah 29

1Woe, Ariel, Ariel,
the city where David camped!
Add year to year;
let the feasts run their round.

2Yet I will distress Ariel,
and there will be moaning and lamentation,
and she will be to Me like an Ariel.

3I will camp against you all around;
I will besiege you with towers
and raise siege works against you.

4Brought low, you will speak from the earth,
and your words will come low from the dust;
your voice will be like a ghost's from the earth,
and your words will chirp from the dust.

5But the multitude of your foes will be like fine dust,
and the multitude of the ruthless like chaff blowing away;
and in an instant, suddenly,

6you will be visited by the LORD of hosts
with thunder and earthquake and a great noise,
with whirlwind and tempest
and the flame of a devouring fire.

7The multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel,
all that fight against her and her stronghold and distress her,
will be like a dream, a vision of the night.

8As when a hungry man dreams he is eating,
and wakes with his hunger unsatisfied,
or a thirsty man dreams he is drinking,
and wakes faint, with his thirst unquenched,
so will the multitude of all the nations be
that fight against Mount Zion.

9Be astonished and astounded;
blind yourselves and be blind!
Be drunk, but not with wine;
stagger, but not with strong drink!

10For the LORD has poured out on you
a spirit of deep sleep,
and has shut your eyes, the prophets,
and covered your heads, the seers.

11All this vision has become to you like the words of a sealed book. When they give it to one who can read, saying, "Read this," he says, "I cannot, for it is sealed."

12When the book is given to one who cannot read, saying, "Read this," he says, "I cannot read."

13The Lord said:
"Because this people draw near with their mouth
and honor Me with their lips,
while their heart is far from Me,
and their fear of Me
is a commandment of men learned by rote,

14therefore I will again do wonders with this people,
wonder upon wonder;
the wisdom of their wise men will perish,
and the understanding of their discerning men will be hidden."

15Woe to those who hide their plans deep from the LORD,
whose deeds are in the dark,
and who say, "Who sees us? Who knows us?"

16You turn things upside down!
Shall the potter be regarded as the clay,
that the thing made should say of its maker,
"He did not make me,"
or the thing formed say of him who formed it,
"He has no understanding"?

17Is it not yet a very little while
until Lebanon is turned into a fruitful field,
and the fruitful field is regarded as a forest?

18In that day the deaf will hear the words of a book,
and out of gloom and darkness
the eyes of the blind will see.

19The humble will increase their joy in the LORD,
and the poorest of mankind will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

20For the ruthless will come to nothing,
and the scoffer will cease,
and all who watch to do evil will be cut off,

21who make a man a sinner by a word,
and lay a snare for the one who reproves at the gate,
and turn aside the righteous with empty arguments.

22Therefore thus says the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob:
"Jacob will no longer be ashamed;
his face will no longer grow pale.

23For when he sees his children,
the work of My hands, in his midst,
they will sanctify My name;
they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob,
and will stand in awe of the God of Israel.

24Those who go astray in spirit will come to understanding,
and those who grumble will accept instruction."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Ariel… she will be to Me like an Ariel" — a name for Jerusalem, the city where David camped (chanah, the verb of v3, I will camp against you). Ariel reads as "lion of God," and the same word names the altar hearth in Ezekiel's temple (ha-ari'el, Ezekiel 43:15). The second sense makes v2 a threat: the city will become a hearth where fire burns.

  • v4 "your voice will be like a ghost's… your words will chirp from the dust" — ov and tsiftsef, the words of 8:19, Consult the ghosts and the spirits that chirp and mutter. The city that consulted the dead will speak like them.

  • v10 "a spirit of deep sleep" — tardemah, the sleep the LORD God made fall upon the human (Genesis 2:21). Paul quotes the line, joined to Deuteronomy 29:4: God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that would not see and ears that would not hear (Romans 11:8).

  • v13 "a commandment of men learned by rote" — Jesus quotes the verse from the Greek: This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me; in vain do they worship Me, teaching as teachings the commandments of men (Matthew 15:8–9). In vain, matēn, is the Greek's; the Hebrew has learned by rote.

  • v14 "wonder upon wonder; the wisdom of their wise men will perish" — hafle va-fele, the pele of 9:6 and 25:1, here a wonder of judgment. Paul quotes the second line: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise (1 Corinthians 1:19).

  • v16 "Shall the potter be regarded as the clay" — yotser, the potter, the word for the LORD who formed (27:11). Paul uses the picture: Will what is formed say to the one who formed it, "Why did you make me like this?" (Romans 9:20).

  • vv11–12, 18 "a sealed book… the deaf will hear the words of a book" — the book no one could read, sealed and unlettered alike, is heard in that day; the eyes shut in v10 see. Jesus answers John's disciples with these signs: the blind see again… and the deaf hear (Matthew 11:5).

  • v24 "those who grumble will accept instruction" — rogenim, the verb of Israel in the wilderness, You grumbled in your tents (Deuteronomy 1:27).
