chapters.title: Besides Me There Is No God
chapters.html:
Isaiah 44

1But now hear, Jacob My servant,
Israel whom I have chosen.

2Thus says the LORD who made you,
who formed you from the womb and will help you:
"Do not fear, Jacob My servant,
Jeshurun whom I have chosen.

3For I will pour water on the thirsty land,
and streams on the dry ground;
I will pour My Spirit on your seed,
and My blessing on your descendants.

4They will spring up among the grass
like willows by flowing streams.

5One will say, 'I am the LORD's';
another will call himself by the name of Jacob;
another will write on his hand, 'The LORD's,'
and take the name of Israel as a title."

6Thus says the LORD, the King of Israel,
and his Redeemer, the LORD of hosts:
"I am the first and I am the last;
besides Me there is no god.

7Who is like Me? Let him proclaim it;
let him declare it and set it in order before Me,
since I appointed an ancient people.
Let them declare what is to come,
and what will happen.

8Do not tremble, and do not be afraid.
Have I not told you from of old and declared it?
You are My witnesses!
Is there a God besides Me?
There is no Rock; I know of none."

The Idol Maker

9All who form idols are emptiness,
and the things they delight in do not profit;
their witnesses neither see nor know,
so that they will be put to shame.

10Who forms a god or casts an idol
that profits nothing?

11All his companions will be put to shame,
and the craftsmen are only human.
Let them all assemble, let them stand up;
they will be terrified; they will be put to shame together.

12The ironsmith takes a cutting tool
and works it over the coals;
he forms it with hammers
and works it with his strong arm;
he becomes hungry, and his strength fails;
he drinks no water and grows faint.

13The carpenter stretches a line;
he marks it out with a stylus;
he shapes it with planes
and marks it with a compass;
he shapes it into the figure of a man,
with the beauty of a human,
to dwell in a house.

14He cuts down cedars for himself,
or takes a cypress or an oak
and lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest;
he plants a pine, and the rain makes it grow.

15Then it becomes fuel for a man;
he takes part of it and warms himself;
he kindles a fire and bakes bread;
he also makes a god and worships it;
he makes it an idol and bows down to it.

16Half of it he burns in the fire;
over that half he eats meat;
he roasts a roast and is satisfied;
he also warms himself and says,
"Aha, I am warm; I see the fire!"

17The rest of it he makes into a god, his idol;
he bows down to it and worships;
he prays to it and says,
"Deliver me, for you are my god!"

18They do not know, nor do they understand;
for their eyes are smeared over so that they cannot see,
and their hearts so that they cannot understand.

19No one stops to think,
nor is there knowledge or understanding to say,
"Half of it I burned in the fire;
I also baked bread on its coals;
I roasted meat and have eaten.
Shall I make the rest of it a detestable thing?
Shall I bow down to a block of wood?"

20He feeds on ashes;
a deluded heart has led him astray,
and he cannot deliver himself or say,
"Is there not a lie in my right hand?"

I Have Redeemed You

21Remember these things, Jacob,
and Israel, for you are My servant;
I formed you; you are My servant;
Israel, you will not be forgotten by Me.

22I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud,
and your sins like mist;
return to Me, for I have redeemed you.

23Sing, you heavens, for the LORD has done it;
shout, you depths of the earth;
break out into singing, you mountains,
you forest, and every tree in it!
For the LORD has redeemed Jacob,
and will be glorified in Israel.

24Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer,
who formed you from the womb:
"I am the LORD, who made all things,
who alone stretched out the heavens,
who spread out the earth by Myself;

25who frustrates the signs of the babblers,
and makes fools of diviners;
who turns wise men back,
and makes their knowledge foolish;

26who confirms the word of His servant,
and fulfills the counsel of His messengers;
who says of Jerusalem, 'She shall be inhabited,'
and of the cities of Judah, 'They shall be built,
and I will raise up their ruins';

27who says to the deep, 'Be dry;
I will dry up your rivers';

28who says of Cyrus, 'He is My shepherd,
and he shall carry out all My purpose,'
saying of Jerusalem, 'She shall be built,'
and of the temple, 'Your foundation shall be laid.'"

Notes

  • v2 "Jeshurun whom I have chosen" — Yeshurun, from yashar, "upright," a name for Israel in the Song and Blessing of Moses: Jeshurun grew fat and kicked (Deuteronomy 32:15); There is none like God, Jeshurun (33:26). The Greek has the beloved Israel.

  • v3 "I will pour My Spirit on your seed" — the promise of 32:15, until the Spirit is poured out on us from on high, here poured on the children.

  • v6 "I am the first and I am the last" — as in 41:4 and 48:12; Revelation 1:17 gives the words to the risen Christ.

  • v8 "There is no Rock; I know of none" — tsur, the name the Song of Moses gives the LORD: The Rock — His work is whole (Deuteronomy 32:4).

  • vv9–10 "All who form idols… Who forms a god" — yotsrei, yatsar, the verb the LORD uses of forming Israel (vv2, 21, 24). In v9 the printed Hebrew has dots set over the word hemmah, "they" (their witnesses, they neither see), a mark of the scribes; the text gives no reason for it.

  • v12 "he grows faint" — va-yi'af, the word of 40:28–31: the LORD does not grow faint or weary; the man who makes a god does.

  • v13 "the figure of a man, with the beauty of a human" — tavnit ish, tif'eret adam: man was made in the likeness of God (Genesis 1:26), and the carpenter makes his god in the likeness of a man.

  • vv15–19 "Half of it he burns… the rest of it he makes into a god" — one log does for the oven, the dinner and the god. "A detestable thing" — to'evah.

  • vv22–24 "blotted out… I have redeemed you… your Redeemer" — machiti, as in 43:25; ge'altikha, go'alekha: the kinsman who buys back (41:14). "By Myself" (v24) — the read form me-itti, "from with Me," is followed; the written form is mi itti, "who was with Me?"

  • v28 "who says of Cyrus, 'He is My shepherd'" — the conqueror of 41:2, 25, named at last. Chronicles and Ezra close and open with his decree: A message from Cyrus king of Persia: The LORD, the God of heaven… has appointed me to build Him a house in Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 36:23; Ezra 1:2).

The carpenter stretches a line; he marks it out with a stylus; he shapes it with planes and marks it with a compass; he shapes it into the figure of a man, with the beauty of a human, to dwell in a house.
He cuts down cedars for himself, or takes a cypress or an oak and lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest; he plants a pine, and the rain makes it grow.
Then it becomes fuel for a man; he takes part of it and warms himself; he kindles a fire and bakes bread; he also makes a god and worships it; he makes it an idol and bows down to it.
Half of it he burns in the fire; over that half he eats meat; he roasts a roast and is satisfied; he also warms himself and says, "Aha, I am warm; I see the fire!"
The rest of it he makes into a god, his idol; he bows down to it and worships; he prays to it and says, "Deliver me, for you are my god!"
They do not know, nor do they understand; for their eyes are smeared over so that they cannot see, and their hearts so that they cannot understand.

No one stops to think, nor is there knowledge or understanding to say, "Half of it I burned in the fire; I also baked bread on its coals; I roasted meat and have eaten. Shall I make the rest of it a detestable thing? Shall I bow down to a block of wood?"
He feeds on ashes; a deluded heart has led him astray, and he cannot deliver himself or say, "Is there not a lie in my right hand?"
I Have Redeemed You
Remember these things, Jacob, and Israel, for you are My servant; I formed you; you are My servant; Israel, you will not be forgotten by Me.
I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like mist; return to Me, for I have redeemed you.

Sing, you heavens, for the LORD has done it; shout, you depths of the earth; break out into singing, you mountains, you forest, and every tree in it! For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and will be glorified in Israel.
Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, who formed you from the womb: "I am the LORD, who made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who spread out the earth by Myself;
who frustrates the signs of the babblers, and makes fools of diviners; who turns wise men back, and makes their knowledge foolish;

who confirms the word of His servant, and fulfills the counsel of His messengers; who says of Jerusalem, 'She shall be inhabited,' and of the cities of Judah, 'They shall be built, and I will raise up their ruins';
who says to the deep, 'Be dry; I will dry up your rivers';
who says of Cyrus, 'He is My shepherd, and he shall carry out all My purpose,' saying of Jerusalem, 'She shall be built,' and of the temple, 'Your foundation shall be laid.'"

chapters.title: To Cyrus, His Anointed
chapters.html:
Isaiah 45

1Thus says the LORD to His anointed,
to Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped,
to subdue nations before him
and to loosen the belts of kings,
to open doors before him,
so that gates will not be shut:

2"I will go before you
and level the swelling hills;
I will break in pieces the doors of bronze
and cut through the bars of iron;

3I will give you the treasures of darkness
and the hoards in secret places,
so that you may know that it is I, the LORD,
the God of Israel, who call you by name.

4For the sake of Jacob My servant,
and Israel My chosen,
I call you by your name;
I give you a title of honor,
though you do not know Me.

5I am the LORD, and there is no other;
besides Me there is no God.
I gird you,
though you do not know Me,

6so that they may know,
from the rising of the sun and from the west,
that there is none besides Me;
I am the LORD, and there is no other.

7I form light and create darkness;
I make peace and create disaster;
I am the LORD, who does all these things.

8Drip down, you heavens, from above,
and let the skies rain down righteousness;
let the earth open, that deliverance may bear fruit,
and let it make righteousness sprout up with it;
I, the LORD, have created it.

9Woe to him who strives with the One who formed him,
a potsherd among the potsherds of the earth!
Does the clay say to the one who forms it, 'What are you making?'
or your work say, 'He has no hands'?

10Woe to him who says to a father, 'What are you begetting?'
or to a woman, 'With what are you in labor?'"

11Thus says the LORD,
the Holy One of Israel, and the One who formed him:
"Ask Me about the things to come;
will you command Me concerning My children
and the work of My hands?

12I made the earth
and created man on it;
My hands stretched out the heavens,
and I commanded all their host.

13I have stirred him up in righteousness,
and I will make all his ways level;
he will build My city
and set My exiles free,
not for price or reward,"
says the LORD of hosts.

14Thus says the LORD:
"The labor of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush,
and the Sabeans, men of stature,
will come over to you and be yours;
they will follow you;
they will come over in chains
and bow down to you;
they will plead with you, saying:
'Surely God is in you, and there is no other;
there is no god besides Him.'"

15Truly, You are a God who hides Himself,
the God of Israel, the Savior.

16They are put to shame and disgraced, all of them;
the makers of idols go away together in disgrace.

17But Israel is delivered by the LORD
with an everlasting deliverance;
you will not be put to shame or disgraced
to all eternity.

18For thus says the LORD,
who created the heavens
(He is God!),
who formed the earth and made it
(He established it;
He did not create it to be empty;
He formed it to be inhabited):
"I am the LORD, and there is no other.

19I did not speak in secret,
in a land of darkness;
I did not say to the offspring of Jacob,
'Seek Me in emptiness.'
I, the LORD, speak what is right;
I declare what is upright.

20Assemble yourselves and come;
draw near together, you survivors of the nations!
They have no knowledge,
who carry about their wooden idols
and keep praying to a god that cannot save.

21Declare it and present your case;
let them take counsel together!
Who told this long ago?
Who declared it of old?
Was it not I, the LORD?
There is no other god besides Me,
a righteous God and a Savior;
there is none besides Me.

22Turn to Me and be saved,
all the ends of the earth!
For I am God, and there is no other.

23By Myself I have sworn;
from My mouth has gone out in righteousness
a word that will not return:
'To Me every knee shall bow,
every tongue shall swear.'

24'Only in the LORD,' it shall be said of Me,
'are righteousness and strength.'
To Him shall come and be ashamed
all who were incensed against Him.

25In the LORD all the offspring of Israel
shall be justified and shall glory."

Notes

  • v1 "to His anointed, to Cyrus" — limshicho, mashiach, the title of Israel's kings, the LORD's anointed (1 Samuel 24:6), given here to a king of another nation who does not know the LORD (vv4, 5). The Greek has to My christ Cyrus. "Whose right hand I have grasped" — hechezaqti, the verb of 41:9, 13, used of Israel.

  • vv1, 5 "to loosen the belts of kings… I gird you" — mothnei melakhim afatteach and a'azzerkha: the LORD ungirds the kings Cyrus defeats, and girds Cyrus.

  • v7 "I make peace and create disaster" — ra, the word for evil and for harm, set here against shalom, "peace, welfare." Amos asks the same: If disaster comes to a city, has not the LORD done it? (Amos 3:6, ra'ah).

  • v9 "Woe to him who strives with the One who formed him" — yotsro, the potter, as in 29:16, and the word for the LORD who formed Israel (43:1; 44:2). Paul uses the picture: Will what is formed say to the one who formed it, "Why did you make me like this?" (Romans 9:20).

  • v14 "the merchandise of Cush, and the Sabeans, men of stature" — the land the Greek calls Ethiopia (18:1 note), and Seba (43:3), its people tall, as the nation tall and smooth of 18:2. They come to Zion and say, Surely God is in you.

  • v15 "Truly, You are a God who hides Himself" — El mistatter, as Isaiah waited for the LORD, who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob (8:17). The God who is hidden is the God who saves.

  • vv18–19 "He did not create it to be empty… Seek Me in emptiness" — tohu, the word rendered wild in Genesis 1:2, the earth was wild and waste. The LORD did not make the earth to stay so, and He did not send Jacob to look for Him there.

  • v23 "To Me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear" — Paul quotes it of God's judgment (every tongue shall confess to God, Romans 14:11), and of Jesus: at the name of Jesus every knee should bow… and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord (Philippians 2:10–11).

  • v25 "shall be justified" — yitsdequ, "be declared righteous," from the root of righteousness in vv8, 13, 19, 21, 23, 24.

chapters.title: Bel Bows Down
chapters.html:
Isaiah 46

1Bel bows down; Nebo stoops;
their idols are on beasts and cattle;
the things you carry are loaded
as a burden on weary beasts.

2They stoop, they bow down together;
they cannot save the burden,
but they themselves go into captivity.

3Listen to Me, house of Jacob,
and all the remnant of the house of Israel,
you who have been loaded on Me from birth,
carried from the womb;

4even to your old age I am He,
and to gray hairs I will bear you.
I have made, and I will carry;
I will bear, and I will save.

5To whom will you liken Me and make Me equal,
and compare Me, that we may be alike?

6Those who lavish gold from the purse,
and weigh out silver on the scale,
hire a goldsmith, and he makes it into a god;
then they fall down and worship!

7They lift it on their shoulders, they bear it;
they set it in its place, and it stands there;
from its place it does not move.
If one cries to it, it does not answer,
or save him from his trouble.

8Remember this and stand firm;
take it to heart, you transgressors.

9Remember the former things of old;
for I am God, and there is no other;
I am God, and there is none like Me,

10declaring the end from the beginning,
and from ancient times things not yet done,
saying, "My counsel shall stand,
and I will do all My purpose,"

11calling a bird of prey from the east,
the man of My counsel from a far country.
I have spoken, and I will bring it to pass;
I have planned it, and I will do it.

12Listen to Me, you stubborn of heart,
you who are far from righteousness:

13I bring near My righteousness; it is not far off,
and My deliverance will not delay;
I will put deliverance in Zion,
for Israel My glory.

Notes

  • v1 "Bel bows down; Nebo stoops" — gods of Babylon. Jeremiah's oracle on Babylon names Bel too: Babylon is taken, Bel is put to shame, Merodach is dismayed (Jeremiah 50:2).

  • vv1–4, 7 "the things you carry are loaded… you who have been loaded on Me… I will carry… they bear it" — nasa, "carry," amas, "load," and saval, "bear," each said twice: once of the idols, which have to be loaded on animals and borne on men's shoulders, and once of the LORD, who has carried Israel from the womb and will bear them to old age. The idols are a burden; the LORD bears His people. Saval is the verb of the servant who will bear the people's pains and iniquities (53:4, 11).

  • v5 "To whom will you liken Me and make Me equal" — tedammeyuni and tashvu, the two verbs of 40:25, To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal? "And compare Me" — tamshiluni, from mashal, added here.

  • v10 "declaring the end from the beginning" — me-reshit acharit; reshit is the word of Genesis 1:1, In the beginning.

  • v11 "a bird of prey from the east, the man of My counsel" — Cyrus, named in 44:28 and 45:1. The read form atsati, "My counsel," is followed.

  • vv12–13 "you who are far from righteousness… it is not far off" — rechoqim, lo tirchaq: the people are far from it; the LORD's righteousness is not far from them.

chapters.title: The Fall of the Daughter of Babylon
chapters.html:
Isaiah 47

1Come down and sit in the dust,
virgin daughter of Babylon;
sit on the ground without a throne,
daughter of the Chaldeans!
For you will no longer be called
tender and delicate.

2Take the millstones and grind flour;
remove your veil;
strip off your skirt, uncover your legs,
wade through the rivers.

3Your nakedness will be uncovered,
and your shame will be seen.
I will take vengeance,
and I will spare no one.

4Our Redeemer — the LORD of hosts is His name —
is the Holy One of Israel.

5Sit in silence, and go into darkness,
daughter of the Chaldeans;
for you will no longer be called
the mistress of kingdoms.

6I was angry with My people;
I profaned My inheritance,
and I gave them into your hand.
You showed them no mercy;
on the aged you made your yoke very heavy.

7You said, "I will be mistress forever,"
so that you did not lay these things to heart
or remember how it would end.

8So now hear this, you lover of pleasures,
who sits secure,
who says in her heart,
"I am, and there is none besides me;
I will not sit as a widow
or know the loss of children."

9These two things will come to you
in a moment, in one day:
the loss of children and widowhood.
They will come on you in full measure,
in spite of your many sorceries
and the great power of your spells.

10You felt secure in your wickedness;
you said, "No one sees me."
Your wisdom and your knowledge led you astray,
and you said in your heart,
"I am, and there is none besides me."

11But disaster will come on you,
which you will not know how to charm away;
calamity will fall on you,
which you will not be able to ward off;
ruin will come on you suddenly,
which you do not know.

12Stand fast in your spells
and your many sorceries,
with which you have labored from your youth;
perhaps you will be able to profit,
perhaps you will strike terror.

13You are wearied with your many counsels;
let them stand up and save you,
the astrologers of the heavens,
who gaze at the stars,
who make known at the new moons
what will come on you.

14They have become like stubble;
the fire burns them;
they cannot deliver themselves
from the power of the flame.
It is no coal to warm oneself by,
no fire to sit before!

15So they have become to you,
those with whom you have labored,
who have traded with you from your youth;
they wander off, each his own way;
there is no one to save you.

Notes

  • v1 "virgin daughter of Babylon" — betulat bat Bavel, the city spoken of as a young woman, as virgin daughter of Zion in 37:22. Babylon is brought down from the throne to the dust and the millstones, the work of a slave woman (the slave girl who is behind the millstones, Exodus 11:5).

  • v3 "I will spare no one" — lo efga adam, "I will not meet a man." Paga is to meet someone, with a plea or with a blow; in 53:12 and 59:16 the same verb is to intercede. The line can mean that the LORD lets no one plead for Babylon, or that He meets no one with mercy. The Greek has I will no longer hand you over to men.

  • vv5, 7 "the mistress of kingdoms… I will be mistress forever" — gevéret, the word for the mistress of a slave girl (Sarai over Hagar, Genesis 16:4, 8). The one who was mistress is now the one who grinds.

  • v6 "on the aged you made your yoke very heavy" — Babylon was the LORD's instrument, as Assyria was the rod of My anger (10:5); the guilt is in how it used the power. Old age is the age the LORD promises to carry Israel to (46:4).

  • vv8, 10 "I am, and there is none besides me" — ani ve-afsi od: Babylon speaks the LORD's own words. Efes, "none besides," and od, "no other," are the words of 45:6, there is none besides Me; I am the LORD, and there is no other, and of 46:9.

  • vv8–9 "widow… the loss of children" — almanah, shekhol: the two griefs she says she will never know arrive together, in a moment, in one day. "In full measure" — ke-tummam, "as their completeness."

  • v11 "which you will not know how to charm away" — lo tede'i shachrah. The letters are those of shachar, "dawn," and of the verb of 26:9, seeks You at dawn. Read as "dawn," the line is you will not know where it dawns from; read as the verb, you will not know how to seek it away, that is, avert it by the sorceries of v9, as the next line has kapperah, "cover it, ransom it off." "Ruin" — sho'ah, as in 10:3, the ruin that will come from far away.

  • v13 "the astrologers of the heavens" — hoverei shamayim, the read form; the written form spells it as a verb. The verb havar is found nowhere else, and what it does is not known; the Greek has the astrologers of heaven, which is what the next two lines describe: they gaze at the stars and announce at each new moon (mod'im le-chodashim) what is coming.

  • v14 "It is no coal to warm oneself by" — lachmam, the verb of 44:15–16, where the idol maker warms himself at the half of the log he does not worship. The fire that burns the stargazers warms no one.

chapters.title: Refined in the Furnace of Affliction
chapters.html:
Isaiah 48

1Hear this, house of Jacob,
who are called by the name of Israel,
and who came from the waters of Judah,
who swear by the name of the LORD
and call on the God of Israel,
but not in truth or in righteousness.

2For they call themselves after the holy city
and lean on the God of Israel;
the LORD of hosts is His name.

3The former things I declared long ago;
they went out from My mouth, and I announced them;
suddenly I did them, and they came to pass.

4Because I knew that you are stubborn,
and your neck is an iron sinew
and your forehead bronze,

5I declared them to you long ago;
before they came to pass I announced them to you,
so that you would not say, "My idol did them;
my carved image and my cast image commanded them."

6You have heard; see it all.
Will you not declare it?
From now on I announce new things to you,
hidden things that you have not known.

7They are created now, not long ago;
before today you never heard of them,
so that you would not say, "I knew them already."

8You have not heard, you have not known;
from long ago your ear has not been opened.
For I knew that you would deal treacherously,
and that you were called a rebel from the womb.

9For My name's sake I defer My anger;
for the sake of My praise I hold it back for you,
so as not to cut you off.

10I have refined you, but not as silver;
I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.

11For My own sake, for My own sake, I do it;
for how should it be profaned?
My glory I give to no other.

12Listen to Me, Jacob,
and Israel, whom I called:
I am He; I am the first,
and I am also the last.

13My own hand laid the foundation of the earth,
and My right hand spread out the heavens;
when I call to them,
they stand up together.

14Assemble, all of you, and listen!
Who among them has declared these things?
The LORD loves him;
he will carry out His purpose on Babylon,
and His arm will be against the Chaldeans.

15I, I have spoken; I have called him;
I have brought him, and he will prosper in his way.

16Draw near to Me, hear this:
from the beginning I have not spoken in secret;
from the time it came to be, I have been there.
And now the Lord GOD has sent me, and His Spirit.

17Thus says the LORD,
your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel:
"I am the LORD your God,
who teaches you what is for your good,
who leads you in the way you should go.

18If only you had paid attention to My commandments!
Then your peace would have been like a river,
and your righteousness like the waves of the sea;

19your seed would have been like the sand,
and the offspring of your body like its grains;
its name would never be cut off
or destroyed from before Me."

20Go out from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans!
Declare this with a shout of joy, proclaim it,
send it out to the end of the earth;
say, "The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!"

21They did not thirst
when He led them through the deserts;
He made water flow for them from the rock;
He split the rock, and water gushed out.

22"There is no peace," says the LORD, "for the wicked."

Notes

  • v1 "who came from the waters of Judah" — u-mimmei Yehudah, the people pictured as a stream flowing from its spring, as Psalm 68:26 calls them you who come from the fountain of Israel. The Greek has only who came out of Judah.

  • v4 "you are stubborn, and your neck is an iron sinew" — qasheh, "hard," the word of Exodus 32:9, a stiff-necked people (qesheh oref). Isaiah spells the old phrase out: the neck has a sinew of iron and the forehead is bronze.

  • v8 "a rebel from the womb" — poshea mi-beten. Israel was formed from the womb (44:2, 24) and carried from the womb (46:3); it has also been rebelling from the womb. The LORD knew both.

  • v10 "I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction" — bechartikha, from bachar, "choose," the verb of Israel whom I have chosen (41:8; 44:1, 2). Beside I have refined you the reader may expect "tested," but that is bachan (28:16, a tested stone), one letter different, and the Hebrew has bachar. The Greek has I have rescued you from the furnace of poverty. Kur, "furnace," is the word of Egypt, the iron furnace (Deuteronomy 4:20).

  • v11 "for how should it be profaned?" — the Hebrew has no subject; the thing that would be profaned is the name of v9. The Greek supplies it, My name is profaned. "My glory I give to no other" — the words of 42:8.

  • vv14–15 "The LORD loves him; he will carry out His purpose on Babylon" — Cyrus, called and brought by the LORD (41:2, 25; 45:1–4). Cheftso, "His purpose," is the word of 44:28, where Cyrus shall carry out all My purpose. The Greek reads it as God speaking to Israel: Loving you, I have done your will on Babylon.

  • v16 "And now the Lord GOD has sent me, and His Spirit" — a new voice speaks, me, sent by the Lord GOD; it is not said whose. The Hebrew order allows two readings: the Lord GOD and His Spirit have sent me, or the Lord GOD has sent me and His Spirit with me. The English keeps the Hebrew order and both readings.

  • vv18–19 "your seed would have been like the sand" — the promise to Abraham, your seed… as the sand that is on the lip of the sea (Genesis 22:17), as it would have been kept had Israel listened. "Its grains" — ke-me'otav, a word found only here.

  • v21 "He split the rock, and water gushed out" — va-yivqa tsur va-yazuvu mayim, the exodus told in the Psalms' words: He opened the rock, and water gushed out (Psalm 105:41; also 78:20). The way out of Babylon is a second exodus.

  • v22 "There is no peace… for the wicked" — the line comes again at 57:21, there with says my God.

speech.text: Isaiah 48

Hear this, house of Jacob, who are called by the name of Israel, and who came from the waters of Judah, who swear by the name of the LORD and call on the God of Israel, but not in truth or in righteousness.
For they call themselves after the holy city and lean on the God of Israel; the LORD of hosts is His name.
The former things I declared long ago; they went out from My mouth, and I announced them; suddenly I did them, and they came to pass.
Because I knew that you are stubborn, and your neck is an iron sinew and your forehead bronze,
I declared them to you long ago; before they came to pass I announced them to you, so that you would not say, "My idol did them; my carved image and my cast image commanded them."
You have heard; see it all. Will you not declare it? From now on I announce new things to you, hidden things that you have not known.
They are created now, not long ago; before today you never heard of them, so that you would not say, "I knew them already."
You have not heard, you have not known; from long ago your ear has not been opened. For I knew that you would deal treacherously, and that you were called a rebel from the womb.
For My name's sake I defer My anger; for the sake of My praise I hold it back for you, so as not to cut you off.
I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
For My own sake, for My own sake, I do it; for how should it be profaned? My glory I give to no other.
Listen to Me, Jacob, and Israel, whom I called: I am He; I am the first, and I am also the last.
My own hand laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens; when I call to them, they stand up together.
Assemble, all of you, and listen! Who among them has declared these things? The LORD loves him; he will carry out His purpose on Babylon, and His arm will be against the Chaldeans.
I, I have spoken; I have called him; I have brought him, and he will prosper in his way.
Draw near to Me, hear this: from the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time it came to be, I have been there. And now the Lord GOD has sent me, and His Spirit.
Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: "I am the LORD your God, who teaches you what is for your good, who leads you in the way you should go.
If only you had paid attention to My commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea;
your seed would have been like the sand, and the offspring of your body like its grains; its name would never be cut off or destroyed from before Me."
Go out from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans! Declare this with a shout of joy, proclaim it, send it out to the end of the earth; say, "The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!"
They did not thirst when He led them through the deserts; He made water flow for them from the rock; He split the rock, and water gushed out.
"There is no peace," says the LORD, "for the wicked."

chapters.title: A Light for the Nations
chapters.html:
Isaiah 49

1Listen to me, you coastlands;
pay attention, you peoples from afar.
The LORD called me from the womb;
from my mother's body He named my name.

2He made my mouth like a sharp sword;
in the shadow of His hand He hid me;
He made me a polished arrow;
in His quiver He hid me away.

3He said to me, "You are My servant,
Israel, in whom I will be glorified."

4But I said, "I have labored in vain;
I have spent my strength for emptiness and vapor;
yet surely my right is with the LORD,
and my reward with my God."

5But now the LORD says,
who formed me from the womb to be His servant,
to bring Jacob back to Him,
and that Israel might be gathered to Him —
for I am honored in the eyes of the LORD,
and my God has become my strength —

6He says:
"It is too small a thing that you should be My servant
to raise up the tribes of Jacob
and to bring back the preserved of Israel;
I will give you as a light for the nations,
that My deliverance may reach to the end of the earth."

7Thus says the LORD,
the Redeemer of Israel, his Holy One,
to one deeply despised, abhorred by the nation,
the servant of rulers:
"Kings will see and rise up;
princes, and they will bow down,
because of the LORD, who is faithful,
the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you."

8Thus says the LORD:
"In a time of favor I have answered you,
and in a day of deliverance I have helped you;
I will keep you and give you
as a covenant for the people,
to restore the land,
to give out the desolate inheritances,

9saying to the prisoners, 'Go out,'
to those who are in darkness, 'Show yourselves.'
They will feed along the roads,
and on all the bare heights will be their pasture.

10They will not hunger or thirst,
and neither burning heat nor sun will strike them,
for He who has compassion on them will lead them,
and by springs of water He will guide them.

11I will make all My mountains a road,
and My highways will be raised up.

12These will come from afar,
and these from the north and from the west,
and these from the land of Sinim."

13Sing for joy, you heavens, and rejoice, earth;
break out into singing, you mountains!
For the LORD has comforted His people
and will have compassion on His afflicted.

14But Zion said, "The LORD has forsaken me;
the Lord has forgotten me."

15"Can a woman forget her nursing child,
or have no compassion on the son of her womb?
Even these may forget,
yet I will not forget you.

16I have engraved you on the palms of My hands;
your walls are continually before Me.

17Your sons hurry back;
those who tore you down and laid you waste
go out from you.

18Lift up your eyes all around and see:
they all gather together, they come to you.
As I live," declares the LORD,
"you will put them all on like ornaments;
you will bind them on as a bride does.

19Surely your waste and desolate places
and your ruined land —
surely now you will be too narrow for those who live in you,
and those who swallowed you up will be far away.

20The children born in your bereavement
will yet say in your hearing,
'The place is too narrow for me;
make room for me to live.'

21Then you will say in your heart,
'Who bore me these?
I was bereaved and barren,
exiled and turned away;
who brought these up?
I was left alone;
where have these come from?'"

22Thus says the Lord GOD:
"I am about to lift up My hand to the nations
and raise My signal to the peoples;
they will bring your sons in their arms,
and your daughters will be carried on their shoulders.

23Kings will be your foster fathers,
and their queens your nursing mothers;
with their faces to the ground they will bow down to you
and lick the dust of your feet.
Then you will know that I am the LORD;
those who wait for Me will not be put to shame."

24Can the prey be taken from the mighty,
or the captives of the righteous be rescued?

25For thus says the LORD:
"Even the captives of the mighty will be taken,
and the prey of the tyrant will be rescued;
I will contend with those who contend with you,
and I will save your children.

26I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh,
and they will be drunk on their own blood as with sweet wine.
Then all flesh will know
that I am the LORD your Savior,
and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob."

Notes

  • vv1–3 "The LORD called me from the womb… You are My servant, Israel" — the servant of 42:1 now speaks for himself. He is given the name Israel (v3), and in v5 he is sent to bring Jacob back: the servant bears the people's name and is sent to the people. "In whom I will be glorified" — etpa'ar, the verb of 44:23, the LORD… will be glorified in Israel.

  • v4 "my right is with the LORD, and my reward with my God" — mishpati, the word of Jacob's complaint in 40:27, my right is passed over by my God. The servant says the same of himself and answers it: his right is with God. Pe'ullati, "my reward," is the word of 40:10, His reward is with Him. "Emptiness and vapor" — tohu va-hevel: tohu as in 44:9, hevel the word that is Abel's name (Genesis 4:2).

  • v5 "and that Israel might be gathered to Him" — the read form lo, "to Him," is followed. The written form is lo with another letter, "not": and Israel is not gathered. The Greek has to gather Jacob to Him, and Israel, with no not.

  • v6 "a light for the nations, that My deliverance may reach to the end of the earth" — or goyim, as in 42:6. Paul and Barnabas take it as a command to themselves in Antioch of Pisidia: I have set you as a light for the nations, that you may be for salvation to the end of the earth (Acts 13:47).

  • v8 "In a time of favor I have answered you" — Paul quotes the line in the Greek and adds, Now is the favorable time; now is the day of salvation (2 Corinthians 6:2). "A covenant for the people" — as in 42:6.

  • v12 "the land of Sinim" — a land named only here, set against the north and the west (yam, the sea); which land is meant is not known. The Greek has the land of the Persians.

  • vv10, 13, 15 "He who has compassion… will have compassion… have no compassion on the son of her womb" — merachamam, yerachem, merachem, from the letters of rechem, "womb." God's compassion is set against a mother's for the child of her body, and it outlasts hers.

  • v17 "Your sons hurry back" — banayikh, "your sons," as the vowels read it; the sons return in vv20–22. The same letters read bonayikh, "your builders," which stands against those who tore you down in the next line, and the Greek has you will quickly be built by those who tore you down.

  • vv20–21 "the children born in your bereavement… I was bereaved and barren" — shikkulayikh, shekhulah, the word Babylon said she would never know (I will not… know the loss of children, 47:8). Babylon loses her children in one day; Zion, who thought herself bereaved, finds herself with more than the place can hold.

  • v24 "the captives of the righteous" — shevi tsaddiq. The next verse answers with the captives of the mighty… the prey of the tyrant, so the captor of v24 is a strong man; the Hebrew calls him tsaddiq, which can mean one who is in the right, a captor who holds his captives lawfully. The Greek has if one takes captive unjustly, will it be saved?

chapters.title: I Did Not Hide My Face
chapters.html:
Isaiah 50

1Thus says the LORD:
"Where is your mother's certificate of divorce,
with which I sent her away?
Or which of My creditors is it
to whom I sold you?
It was for your iniquities that you were sold,
and for your transgressions your mother was sent away.

2Why, when I came, was there no one?
When I called, was there no one to answer?
Is My hand too short to redeem,
or have I no power to deliver?
By My rebuke I dry up the sea;
I make the rivers a desert;
their fish stink for lack of water
and die of thirst.

3I clothe the heavens with blackness
and make sackcloth their covering."

The Lord GOD Has Opened My Ear

4The Lord GOD has given me
the tongue of disciples,
to know how to sustain the weary with a word.
Morning by morning He wakens,
He wakens my ear
to hear as disciples hear.

5The Lord GOD has opened my ear,
and I was not rebellious;
I did not turn back.

6I gave my back to those who strike,
and my cheeks to those who pull out the beard;
I did not hide my face
from insults and spitting.

7But the Lord GOD helps me;
therefore I have not been disgraced;
therefore I have set my face like flint,
and I know that I will not be put to shame.

8He who declares me in the right is near.
Who will contend with me?
Let us stand up together.
Who has a case against me?
Let him come near to me.

9The Lord GOD helps me;
who will declare me guilty?
All of them will wear out like a garment;
the moth will eat them up.

10Who among you fears the LORD
and obeys the voice of His servant?
Let him who walks in darkness
and has no light
trust in the name of the LORD
and rely on his God.

11But all of you who kindle a fire,
who arm yourselves with firebrands:
walk by the light of your fire,
and by the firebrands you have lit!
This you will have from My hand:
you will lie down in torment.

Notes

  • v1 "Where is your mother's certificate of divorce… which of My creditors" — sefer keritut, the document of Deuteronomy 24:1, he writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand and sends her out of his house. A man in debt might sell his children to a creditor (the creditor has come to take my two children, 2 Kings 4:1). The LORD has no certificate to show and no creditor to pay: the mother was sent away, and the children sold, for their own sins.

  • v2 "Is My hand too short to redeem?" — ha-qatsor qatsrah yadi, the LORD's question to Moses in the wilderness, Is the LORD's hand too short? (Numbers 11:23). Isaiah returns to it in 59:1. "By My rebuke I dry up the sea" — ge'arah and charav, the words of Psalm 106:9, He rebuked the Sea of Reeds, and it dried up.

  • v4 "the tongue of disciples… to hear as disciples hear" — limmudim, "those who are taught," the word of 8:16, seal the instruction among my disciples. The servant speaks as one taught before he teaches. "To sustain" — la'ut, a verb found only here; its sense is taken from what follows, the weary and a word. The Greek has to know when to speak a word.

  • v6 "I gave my back to those who strike… I did not hide my face from insults and spitting" — the Greek has my cheeks to slaps (rhapismata) and the shame of spitting (emptysmata). The Gospel tells the night before the crucifixion in the same words: they spat in His face… and some slapped Him (Matthew 26:67, eneptysan, erapisan).

  • v7 "I have set my face like flint" — challamish, the flint rock the LORD brought water out of in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 8:15). The servant does not turn back (v5) and does not flinch.

  • vv8–9 "He who declares me in the right is near… who will declare me guilty?" — matsdiqi, yarshi'eni, the words of a court: one who acquits, one who condemns. Paul uses the scene for the believer: Who will bring a charge against God's elect? God is the one who justifies; who is the one who condemns? (Romans 8:33–34).

  • v9 "the moth will eat them up" — ash yokhlem, said again in 51:8, the moth will eat them up like a garment.

  • v10 "Let him who walks in darkness and has no light" — nogah, "brightness," the word of 9:2, light has shone on them (nagah), there given to the people who walked in darkness.

  • vv10–11 "trust in the name of the LORD… walk by the light of your fire" — two ways through the dark. One trusts the LORD with no light of his own; the others make their own light and walk by it, and lie down in torment (ma'atsevah, from the root of etsev, the pain of Genesis 3:16).

chapters.title: Awake, Awake
chapters.html:
Isaiah 51

1Listen to Me, you who pursue righteousness,
you who seek the LORD:
look to the rock from which you were hewn,
and to the quarry from which you were dug.

2Look to Abraham your father,
and to Sarah who bore you;
for he was one when I called him,
and I blessed him and made him many.

3For the LORD comforts Zion;
He comforts all her waste places;
He makes her wilderness like Eden,
and her desert like the garden of the LORD;
joy and gladness will be found in her,
thanksgiving and the sound of song.

4Pay attention to Me, My people;
give ear to Me, My nation;
for instruction will go out from Me,
and I will set My justice as a light for the peoples.

5My righteousness is near;
My deliverance has gone out,
and My arms will judge the peoples;
the coastlands wait for Me,
and for My arm they hope.

6Lift up your eyes to the heavens,
and look at the earth beneath;
for the heavens will vanish like smoke,
the earth will wear out like a garment,
and its inhabitants will die in the same way;
but My deliverance will be forever,
and My righteousness will not be broken.

7Listen to Me, you who know righteousness,
the people with My instruction in their heart:
do not fear the reproach of men,
and do not be dismayed at their revilings.

8For the moth will eat them up like a garment,
and the worm will eat them like wool;
but My righteousness will be forever,
and My deliverance to all generations.

9Awake, awake, put on strength,
arm of the LORD!
Awake, as in the days of old,
the generations of long ago.
Was it not You who cut Rahab in pieces,
who pierced the dragon?

10Was it not You who dried up the sea,
the waters of the great deep,
who made the depths of the sea a way
for the redeemed to cross over?

11The ransomed of the LORD will return
and come to Zion with singing;
everlasting joy will be on their heads;
they will obtain gladness and joy,
and sorrow and sighing will flee away.

12I, I am He who comforts you;
who are you that you are afraid of man, who dies,
of the son of man, who is made like grass,

13and have forgotten the LORD your Maker,
who stretched out the heavens
and laid the foundations of the earth,
and you live in dread continually, all day long,
because of the fury of the oppressor
when he sets himself to destroy?
Where is the fury of the oppressor?

14The one bowed down will soon be set free;
he will not die and go down to the pit,
nor will his bread be lacking.

15For I am the LORD your God,
who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar —
the LORD of hosts is His name.

16I have put My words in your mouth
and covered you in the shadow of My hand,
to plant the heavens
and lay the foundations of the earth,
and to say to Zion, "You are My people."

The Cup of Staggering

17Rouse yourself, rouse yourself,
stand up, Jerusalem,
you who have drunk from the hand of the LORD
the cup of His wrath,
who have drunk the bowl, the cup of reeling,
and drained it.

18There is none to guide her
among all the sons she has borne;
there is none to take her by the hand
among all the sons she has brought up.

19These two things have come on you —
who will grieve with you? —
devastation and destruction, famine and sword;
by whom shall I comfort you?

20Your sons have fainted;
they lie at the head of every street
like an antelope in a net;
they are full of the wrath of the LORD,
the rebuke of your God.

21So hear this, you who are afflicted,
who are drunk, but not with wine:

22Thus says your Lord, the LORD,
your God who pleads the cause of His people:
"I have taken from your hand the cup of reeling;
the bowl, the cup of My wrath,
you will drink no more.

23I will put it into the hand of your tormentors,
who said to you, 'Bow down, that we may pass over,'
and you made your back like the ground,
like the street for those who pass over."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "the rock from which you were hewn… Abraham your father" — the quarry is named in the next line: the people were cut from Abraham and Sarah. He was one when I called him — the LORD's promise to the one man, I will bless you, and I will make your name great (Genesis 12:2). Va-arbehu, "and made him many": one man became a people.

  • v3 "her desert like the garden of the LORD" — the words of Genesis 13:10, where the plain of the Jordan was like the garden of the LORD before it was ruined. Here the ruin is turned back.

  • v4 "instruction will go out from Me" — torah… tetse, as in 2:3, out of Zion shall go forth instruction; there from Zion, here from the LORD Himself, and a light for the peoples, as the servant is a light for the nations (42:6; 49:6).

  • vv6, 8 "My deliverance will be forever" — the heavens vanish like smoke and the earth wears out like a garment, the picture of 50:9; the LORD's deliverance and righteousness outlast them both. The two verses say it twice, in reverse order.

  • v9 "Awake, awake… who cut Rahab in pieces, who pierced the dragon" — Rahab is the sea monster, a name also given to Egypt (30:7); tannin is the dragon that is in the sea of 27:1. "Pierced" — mecholelet, the verb of 53:5, he was pierced for our transgressions.

  • v10 "who dried up the sea… a way for the redeemed to cross over" — the Sea of Reeds, told with tehom rabbah, the great deep whose fountains split open at the flood (Genesis 7:11). The arm that dried the sea once is called to wake and do it again.

  • v11 "The ransomed of the LORD will return" — the same verse as 35:10, almost word for word, set here at the end of the cry Awake.

  • vv9, 17; 52:1 "Awake, awake… Rouse yourself, rouse yourself… Awake, awake" — three doubled calls. The first is to the LORD's arm; the second and third turn the call back to Jerusalem, who must stand up from the cup and put on her own strength.

  • vv17, 22 "the cup of His wrath… the cup of reeling" — kos ha-tar'elah, the cup that makes one stagger, as wine to drink that makes us reel (Psalm 60:3, tar'elah). Psalm 75:8 puts the cup in the LORD's hand, for the wicked of the earth to drain; here Jerusalem has drained it, and the LORD takes it from her hand to give to her tormentors.

  • v19 "by whom shall I comfort you?" — mi anachamekh, "who — I will comfort you," the LORD's own question: there is no one in Jerusalem to comfort her (v18), and He names none. The Greek has who will comfort you?

speech.text: Isaiah 51
Listen to Me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the LORD: look to the rock from which you were hewn, and to the quarry from which you were dug.
Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you; for he was one when I called him, and I blessed him and made him many.

For the LORD comforts Zion; He comforts all her waste places; He makes her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the sound of song.
Pay attention to Me, My people; give ear to Me, My nation; for instruction will go out from Me, and I will set My justice as a light for the peoples.
My righteousness is near; My deliverance has gone out, and My arms will judge the peoples; the coastlands wait for Me, and for My arm they hope.

Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look at the earth beneath; for the heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants will die in the same way; but My deliverance will be forever, and My righteousness will not be broken.
Listen to Me, you who know righteousness, the people with My instruction in their heart: do not fear the reproach of men, and do not be dismayed at their revilings.
For the moth will eat them up like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool; but My righteousness will be forever, and My deliverance to all generations.
Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of the LORD! Awake, as in the days of old, the generations of long ago. Was it not You who cut Rahab in pieces, who pierced the dragon?
Was it not You who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed to cross over?
The ransomed of the LORD will return and come to Zion with singing; everlasting joy will be on their heads; they will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
I, I am He who comforts you; who are you that you are afraid of man, who dies, of the son of man, who is made like grass,

and have forgotten the LORD your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth, and you live in dread continually, all day long, because of the fury of the oppressor when he sets himself to destroy? Where is the fury of the oppressor?
The one bowed down will soon be set free; he will not die and go down to the pit, nor will his bread be lacking.
For I am the LORD your God, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar — the LORD of hosts is His name.
I have put My words in your mouth and covered you in the shadow of My hand, to plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth, and to say to Zion, "You are My people."
The Cup of Staggering
Rouse yourself, rouse yourself, stand up, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of His wrath, who have drunk the bowl, the cup of reeling, and drained it.
There is none to guide her among all the sons she has borne; there is none to take her by the hand among all the sons she has brought up.
These two things have come on you — who will grieve with you? — devastation and destruction, famine and sword; by whom shall I comfort you?
Your sons have fainted; they lie at the head of every street like an antelope in a net; they are full of the wrath of the LORD, the rebuke of your God.
So hear this, you who are afflicted, who are drunk, but not with wine:
Thus says your Lord, the LORD, your God who pleads the cause of His people: "I have taken from your hand the cup of reeling; the bowl, the cup of My wrath, you will drink no more.
I will put it into the hand of your tormentors, who said to you, 'Bow down, that we may pass over,' and you made your back like the ground, like the street for those who pass over."

chapters.title: How Beautiful on the Mountains
chapters.html:
Isaiah 52

1Awake, awake,
put on your strength, Zion;
put on your beautiful garments,
Jerusalem, the holy city;
for the uncircumcised and the unclean
will no longer enter you.

2Shake yourself from the dust,
rise up, sit enthroned, Jerusalem;
loose the bonds from your neck,
captive daughter of Zion.

3For thus says the LORD: "You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed without money."

4For thus says the Lord GOD: "My people went down at first into Egypt to live there as guests, and Assyria oppressed them for nothing.

5So now, what do I have here," declares the LORD, "seeing that My people are taken away for nothing? Their rulers howl," declares the LORD, "and continually, all day long, My name is despised.

6Therefore My people will know My name; therefore in that day they will know that I am He who speaks: here I am."

7How beautiful on the mountains
are the feet of him who brings good news,
who proclaims peace,
who brings good news of good things,
who proclaims deliverance,
who says to Zion, "Your God reigns!"

8The voice of your watchmen!
They lift up their voice;
together they sing for joy;
for eye to eye they see
the LORD return to Zion.

9Break out together into singing,
you waste places of Jerusalem;
for the LORD has comforted His people;
He has redeemed Jerusalem.

10The LORD has bared His holy arm
before the eyes of all the nations,
and all the ends of the earth will see
the deliverance of our God.

11Depart, depart, go out from there;
touch nothing unclean;
go out from the middle of her;
purify yourselves,
you who carry the vessels of the LORD.

12For you will not go out in haste,
nor will you go in flight;
for the LORD will go before you,
and the God of Israel will be your rear guard.

My Servant

13My servant will act wisely;
he will rise high and be lifted up,
and be very exalted.

14As many were appalled at you —
so marred was his appearance, beyond that of a man,
and his form beyond the sons of men —

15so many nations will marvel at him;
kings will shut their mouths because of him;
for what they had not been told they will see,
and what they had not heard they will understand.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Shake yourself from the dust, rise up, sit enthroned… captive daughter of Zion" — the reverse of Babylon's sentence, Come down and sit in the dust… sit on the ground without a throne (47:1). Zion rises from the dust to the seat Babylon lost. Shevi, "sit," and sheviyah, "captive," sound alike: the captive is told to sit enthroned.

  • v3 "You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed without money" — chinnam, "for nothing," as in 50:1: no creditor was paid when they were sold, and no money will be paid to buy them back. Cyrus sets the exiles free not for price or reward (45:13).

  • v4 "to live there as guests" — la-gur, the word of Jacob's sons before Pharaoh, We have come to live in the land as guests (Genesis 47:4). Israel went down to Egypt by choice and was oppressed; Assyria took them for nothing, be-efes, with no cause.

  • v5 "what do I have here" — the read form mah li, "what is it to Me"; the written form is mi li, "who do I have here." "My name is despised" — the Greek has because of you My name is blasphemed among the nations, and Paul quotes that form against those who teach the law and break it: the name of God is blasphemed among the nations because of you (Romans 2:24).

  • v7 "the feet of him who brings good news" — mevasser, the word of 40:9, Zion, herald of good news; there Zion carries the news, here a runner brings it to her. Paul quotes the line for those sent to preach: How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news! (Romans 10:15). "Your God reigns" — malakh Elohayikh.

  • v8 "eye to eye they see the LORD return to Zion" — ayin be-ayin, the watchmen on the walls see His return face to face.

  • v11 "touch nothing unclean… you who carry the vessels of the LORD" — the vessels of the house of the LORD that Cyrus brought out of the house of Babylon's gods (Ezra 1:7). Paul joins the line to other verses: Come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord, and touch nothing unclean (2 Corinthians 6:17).

  • v12 "you will not go out in haste" — be-chippazon, the word of the first Passover, You shall eat it in haste (Exodus 12:11). This exodus is not a flight; the LORD goes before them and behind them, as at the sea the pillar of cloud moved from before them and stood behind them (Exodus 14:19).

  • v13 "he will rise high and be lifted up" — yarum ve-nissa, the words of 6:1, the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and of 33:10, now I will rise high; now I will be lifted up. Words used of the LORD are said of His servant.

  • v15 "so many nations will marvel at him" — the reading of the Greek, which answers as many were appalled in v14 and the kings who shut their mouths. The Hebrew is yazzeh, the verb of the priest who sprinkles the blood before the LORD (Leviticus 4:6; 16:14): so he will sprinkle many nations. Paul quotes the end of the verse from the Greek: those who were not told about him will see (Romans 15:21).

chapters.title: He Carried Our Sicknesses
chapters.html:
Isaiah 53

1Who has believed what we have heard,
and to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?

2He grew up before Him like a young plant,
and like a root out of dry ground;
he had no form or majesty that we should look at him,
and no appearance that we should desire him.

3He was despised and forsaken by men,
a man of pains, and acquainted with sickness;
and like one from whom people hide their faces
he was despised, and we did not esteem him.

4Surely he carried our sicknesses
and bore our pains;
yet we considered him stricken,
struck down by God, and afflicted.

5But he was pierced for our transgressions;
he was crushed for our iniquities;
the chastisement that brought us peace was on him,
and by his wounds we are healed.

6All we like sheep have gone astray;
we have turned, each one, to his own way;
and the LORD has laid on him
the iniquity of us all.

7He was oppressed, and he was afflicted,
yet he did not open his mouth;
like a lamb that is led to the slaughter,
and like a sheep that is silent before its shearers,
he did not open his mouth.

8By oppression and judgment he was taken away;
and as for his generation, who considered
that he was cut off from the land of the living,
stricken for the transgression of my people?

9His grave was made with the wicked,
and with a rich man in his death,
although he had done no violence,
and there was no deceit in his mouth.

10Yet the LORD was pleased to crush him;
He made him sick.
When his soul makes a guilt offering,
he will see offspring; he will prolong his days,
and the purpose of the LORD will prosper in his hand.

11Out of the anguish of his soul he will see and be satisfied;
by his knowledge the righteous one, My servant,
will make the many righteous,
and he will bear their iniquities.

12Therefore I will give him a portion among the many,
and he will divide the spoil with the strong,
because he poured out his soul to death
and was counted with the transgressors;
yet he carried the sin of many,
and intercedes for the transgressors.

Notes

  • v1 "Who has believed what we have heard?" — shemu'atenu, "our report," the thing heard. John gives the verse as the reason many did not believe in Jesus though they saw His signs (John 12:38), and Paul for those who did not obey the good news (Romans 10:16); both quote the Greek, which begins Lord, who has believed…

  • v2 "He grew up before Him like a young plant, and like a root" — yoneq, a sucker, a shoot from the base of a plant; shoresh, "root," is the word of 11:1 and 11:10, a branch from his roots, the root of Jesse. Lefanav, "before him," does not say whose sight; the capital reads it as the LORD's, whose arm is named in v1.

  • vv3–4 "a man of pains, and acquainted with sickness… Surely he carried our sicknesses and bore our pains" — makh'ovot and choli in v3 are the same two words in v4: the pains and sickness he knew were ours. Nasa, "carry," and saval, "bear," are the verbs of 46:4, where the LORD carries and bears His people. Matthew gives the verse as fulfilled when Jesus healed the sick: He took our weaknesses and carried our diseases (Matthew 8:17).

  • v5 "pierced… crushed" — mecholal, the verb of 51:9, where the arm of the LORD pierced the dragon; medukka, from dakka, the verb of v10, the LORD was pleased to crush him. "By his wounds" — ba-chavurato, "by his wound" (singular, a welt or stripe). Peter: by whose wound you were healed (1 Peter 2:24).

  • vv6, 12 "the LORD has laid on him… and intercedes for the transgressors" — hifgia and yafgia, the same verb (paga, to meet, to fall on, to plead). The LORD made the iniquity of all fall on him; he in turn pleads for those whose iniquity it was. The Gospel gives he was counted with the transgressors as fulfilled in Jesus: And He was counted with the lawless (Luke 22:37).

  • v7 "like a lamb that is led to the slaughter" — the passage the Ethiopian, a eunuch and treasurer of the queen of the Ethiopians, was reading in his chariot on the road home from Jerusalem. He asked Philip, About whom does the prophet say this, about himself or about someone else?, and Philip, beginning from this scripture, told him the good news of Jesus (Acts 8:27–35).

  • vv8, 11 "cut off from the land of the living… he will bear their iniquities" — nigzar, and avonotam yisbol: the day of atonement's goat shall carry on itself all their guilt to a land cut off (Leviticus 16:22, avonotam, gezerah). "Stricken for the transgression of my people" — nega lamo, "a blow to them"; lamo is usually plural, and as a poetic form it can be singular, to him. The Greek has he was led to death.

  • v9 "His grave was made with the wicked, and with a rich man in his death" — va-yitten, "he gave," with no subject named; be-motav, "in his deaths," plural. Peter: who committed no sin, nor was deceit found in His mouth (1 Peter 2:22).

  • v10 "When his soul makes a guilt offering" — im tasim asham nafsho. Tasim can be "she makes," with nafsho, "his soul," as subject, or "you make," when you make his soul a guilt offering. Asham is the guilt offering of Leviticus 5:6. "The LORD was pleased… the purpose of the LORD" — chafets and chefets, the verb and its noun, the purpose of 44:28.

  • v11 "he will see and be satisfied" — the Hebrew has no object for see; the Greek has to show him light. "Will make the many righteous" — yatsdiq, the verb of 50:8, He who declares me in the right: the one declared in the right there declares many in the right here.

speech.text: Isaiah 53
Who has believed what we have heard, and to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?
He grew up before Him like a young plant, and like a root out of dry ground; he had no form or majesty that we should look at him, and no appearance that we should desire him.
He was despised and forsaken by men, a man of pains, and acquainted with sickness; and like one from whom people hide their faces he was despised, and we did not esteem him.
Surely he carried our sicknesses and bore our pains; yet we considered him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
But he was pierced for our transgressions; he was crushed for our iniquities; the chastisement that brought us peace was on him, and by his wounds we are healed.
All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned, each one, to his own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that is silent before its shearers, he did not open his mouth.
By oppression and judgment he was taken away; and as for his generation, who considered that he was cut off from the land of the living, stricken for the transgression of my people?
His grave was made with the wicked, and with a rich man in his death, although he had done no violence, and there was no deceit in his mouth.

Therefore I will give him a portion among the many, and he will divide the spoil with the strong, because he poured out his soul to death and was counted with the transgressors; yet he carried the sin of many, and intercedes for the transgressors.

chapters.title: Sing, Barren One
chapters.html:
Isaiah 54

1"Sing, barren one, who did not bear;
break out into singing and shout,
you who were not in labor!
For the children of the desolate one will be more
than the children of the married one," says the LORD.

2"Enlarge the place of your tent,
and let the curtains of your dwellings be stretched out;
do not hold back;
lengthen your cords
and strengthen your stakes.

3For you will burst out to the right and to the left,
and your seed will possess the nations
and will people the desolate cities.

4Do not fear, for you will not be put to shame;
do not be disgraced, for you will not be humiliated;
for you will forget the shame of your youth,
and the reproach of your widowhood you will remember no more.

5For your Maker is your husband —
the LORD of hosts is His name —
and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel;
He is called the God of all the earth.

6For the LORD has called you
like a wife forsaken and grieved in spirit,
like a wife of one's youth when she is rejected,"
says your God.

7"For a brief moment I forsook you,
but with great compassion I will gather you.

8In a flood of anger
I hid My face from you for a moment,
but with everlasting loyal love
I will have compassion on you,"
says the LORD, your Redeemer.

9"For this is like the waters of Noah to Me:
as I swore that the waters of Noah
would never again pass over the earth,
so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you
or rebuke you.

10For the mountains may depart
and the hills be shaken,
but My loyal love will not depart from you,
and My covenant of peace will not be shaken,"
says the LORD, who has compassion on you.

11"Afflicted one, storm-tossed, not comforted,
I am about to set your stones in antimony
and lay your foundations with sapphires.

12I will make your battlements of rubies,
your gates of sparkling stones,
and all your wall of precious stones.

13All your sons will be disciples of the LORD,
and great will be the peace of your sons.

14In righteousness you will be established;
you will be far from oppression, for you will not fear,
and from terror, for it will not come near you.

15If anyone stirs up strife, it is not from Me;
whoever stirs up strife with you will fall because of you.

16I have created the smith
who blows the fire of coals
and brings out a weapon for its work;
I have also created the ravager to destroy.

17No weapon that is formed against you will succeed,
and every tongue that rises against you in judgment
you will condemn.
This is the inheritance of the servants of the LORD,
and their righteousness is from Me,"
declares the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 "Sing, barren one, who did not bear" — aqarah, the word of Sarah, Sarai was barren (Genesis 11:30), whom 51:2 has just named as the mother who bore you. Zion is the barren mother whose children outnumber those of the woman with a husband. Paul quotes the verse in the Greek of the Jerusalem above… which is our mother (Galatians 4:26–27).

  • vv2–3 "Enlarge the place of your tent… you will burst out to the right and to the left" — tifrotsi, the verb of the promise to Jacob, you shall burst out to the west and to the east (Genesis 28:14). "Your seed" — zar'ekh, as in 44:3 and 48:19.

  • vv5–6 "your Maker is your husband… like a wife forsaken" — bo'alayikh, from ba'al, "husband, owner." To the question of 50:1, Where is your mother's certificate of divorce?, the answer is that the LORD calls her back as a wife. Bo'alayikh and osayikh, "your husband" and "your Maker," are plural in form, as the names of God can be (Ecclesiastes 12:1, your Creator, is the same).

  • vv7–8 "For a brief moment… with great compassion… with everlasting loyal love" — the moment set against everlasting, the anger against loyal love (chesed olam). "In a flood of anger" — be-shetsef qetsef, two words that rhyme; shetsef is found only here.

  • v9 "like the waters of Noah" — the oath after the flood, never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood (Genesis 9:11). The LORD swears to Zion the way He swore to the earth.

  • v10 "My covenant of peace" — berit shelomi, the words the LORD gave Phinehas, I give him My covenant of peace (Numbers 25:12). "Depart… be shaken" — yamushu and temutenah, each said twice: the mountains move, the love and the covenant do not.

  • vv11–12 "your stones in antimony… sapphires… rubies… sparkling stones" — pukh, the black eye-paint of 2 Kings 9:30 (She painted her eyes), here the setting for the stones. The gems are sappirim, kadkod and eqdach. Kadkod is found only here and in Ezekiel 27:16, eqdach only here, and which stones they were is not known; eqdach is from qadach, "kindle." The Greek has carbuncle… sapphire… jasper… crystal.

  • v13 "All your sons will be disciples of the LORD" — limmudei YHWH, the word of 8:16 and 50:4: Zion's children are taught as the servant was taught. Jesus quotes the Greek, They will all be taught by God (John 6:45).

  • v15 "If anyone stirs up strife" — gor yagur, spelled as gur, "live as a guest" (52:4). The line goes on to will fall because of you, which fits the other verb gur, "stir up strife, attack," as in Psalm 59:3, fierce men stir up strife against me (yaguru). The Greek reads it as guests: proselytes will come to you through Me and live beside you.

  • v17 "the servants of the LORD" — avdei YHWH: after the one servant of 52:13–53:12, who will see offspring (53:10), the LORD's servants are many. "Their righteousness is from Me" — tsidqatam me-itti.

For you will burst out to the right and to the left, and your seed will possess the nations and will people the desolate cities.

I will make your battlements of rubies, your gates of sparkling stones, and all your wall of precious stones.
All your sons will be disciples of the LORD, and great will be the peace of your sons.
In righteousness you will be established; you will be far from oppression, for you will not fear, and from terror, for it will not come near you.
