No weapon that is formed against you will succeed, and every tongue that rises against you in judgment you will condemn. This is the inheritance of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness is from Me," declares the LORD.

chapters.title: Come to the Waters
chapters.html:
Isaiah 55

1Come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters;
and you who have no money,
come, buy grain and eat!
Come, buy wine and milk
without money and without price.

2Why do you weigh out money for what is not bread,
and your labor for what does not satisfy?
Listen carefully to Me, and eat what is good,
and let your soul delight itself in rich food.

3Incline your ear, and come to Me;
hear, that your soul may live;
and I will make with you an everlasting covenant,
the sure loyal love shown to David.

4I made him a witness to the peoples,
a leader and commander for the peoples.

5You will call a nation you do not know,
and a nation that did not know you will run to you,
because of the LORD your God,
the Holy One of Israel,
for He has glorified you.

6Seek the LORD while He may be found;
call on Him while He is near.

7Let the wicked forsake his way,
and the man of iniquity his thoughts;
let him return to the LORD, that He may have compassion on him,
and to our God, for He will abundantly pardon.

8For My thoughts are not your thoughts,
nor are your ways My ways, declares the LORD.

9For as the heavens are higher than the earth,
so are My ways higher than your ways
and My thoughts than your thoughts.

10For as the rain and the snow come down from the heavens
and do not return there
without watering the earth,
making it bring forth and sprout,
giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater,

11so shall My word be that goes out from My mouth:
it will not return to Me empty,
but it will accomplish what I purpose,
and succeed in what I sent it for.

12For you will go out with joy,
and be led out in peace;
the mountains and the hills will break out into singing before you,
and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.

13Instead of the thornbush the cypress will come up;
instead of the brier the myrtle will come up;
and it will be to the LORD for a name,
for an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.

Notes

  • v1 "Come… buy grain and eat" — hoy, the word that elsewhere in Isaiah opens a woe (Woe to him who strives, 45:9), here a street-seller's call. Shivru, "buy grain," is the verb of Jacob sending his sons to Egypt, Go down there and buy grain for us (Genesis 42:2): grain is bought here without money.

  • v3 "the sure loyal love shown to David" — chasdei David ha-ne'emanim, the words of Solomon's prayer, Remember the loyal love shown to David Your servant (2 Chronicles 6:42). The promise made to David's house (your house and your kingdom shall be made sure, ne'man, 2 Samuel 7:16) is made now to all who come. Paul quotes the Greek of the line, I will give you the holy and sure things of David, of the risen Jesus (Acts 13:34).

  • v4 "a leader and commander" — nagid, the title Samuel gives the man after God's heart, the LORD has appointed him leader over His people (1 Samuel 13:14).

  • v5 "for He has glorified you" — pe'arakh, the verb of 49:3, in whom I will be glorified. What was said to the servant is said here to the people.

  • vv8–9 "My thoughts are not your thoughts" — the thoughts (machshevot) of v7 that the wicked must forsake. The heavens above the earth measure the distance between them.

  • vv10–11 "giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater… so shall My word be" — the word is sent out like the rain and does not come back empty. Paul uses the Greek of v10 for the giver of a gift: He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food (2 Corinthians 9:10). "What I purpose" — chafatsti, the verb of 53:10, the LORD was pleased, and of its noun, the purpose of the LORD will prosper in his hand.

  • v12 "you will go out with joy… the trees of the field will clap their hands" — the exodus from Babylon, told again (48:20; 52:11–12), with the hills breaking out into singing as at 44:23 and 49:13.

  • v13 "an everlasting sign that will not be cut off" — ot olam… lo yikkaret; in 56:5 the eunuch is given an everlasting name that will not be cut off, the same words.

speech.text: Isaiah 55
Come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you who have no money, come, buy grain and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
Why do you weigh out money for what is not bread, and your labor for what does not satisfy? Listen carefully to Me, and eat what is good, and let your soul delight itself in rich food.
Incline your ear, and come to Me; hear, that your soul may live; and I will make with you an everlasting covenant, the sure loyal love shown to David.
I made him a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander for the peoples.
You will call a nation you do not know, and a nation that did not know you will run to you, because of the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, for He has glorified you.
Seek the LORD while He may be found; call on Him while He is near.
Let the wicked forsake his way, and the man of iniquity his thoughts; let him return to the LORD, that He may have compassion on him, and to our God, for He will abundantly pardon.
For My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways My ways, declares the LORD.
For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are My ways higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts.
For as the rain and the snow come down from the heavens and do not return there without watering the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater,
so shall My word be that goes out from My mouth: it will not return to Me empty, but it will accomplish what I purpose, and succeed in what I sent it for.
For you will go out with joy, and be led out in peace; the mountains and the hills will break out into singing before you, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
Instead of the thornbush the cypress will come up; instead of the brier the myrtle will come up; and it will be to the LORD for a name, for an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.

chapters.title: A House of Prayer for All the Peoples
chapters.html:
Isaiah 56

1Thus says the LORD:
"Keep justice and do righteousness,
for My deliverance is near to come,
and My righteousness to be revealed.

2Blessed is the man who does this,
and the son of man who holds it fast,
who keeps the sabbath, not profaning it,
and keeps his hand from doing any evil."

3Let not the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say,
"The LORD will separate me from His people";
and let not the eunuch say,
"I am a dry tree."

4For thus says the LORD:
"To the eunuchs who keep My sabbaths,
who choose what pleases Me
and hold fast My covenant,

5I will give, in My house and within My walls,
a monument and a name
better than sons and daughters;
to each I will give an everlasting name
that will not be cut off.

6The foreigners who join themselves to the LORD,
to minister to Him, to love the name of the LORD,
and to be His servants,
everyone who keeps the sabbath, not profaning it,
and holds fast My covenant —

7these I will bring to My holy mountain
and make them joyful in My house of prayer;
their burnt offerings and their sacrifices
will be accepted on My altar;
for My house will be called a house of prayer
for all the peoples."

8The Lord GOD declares,
who gathers the banished of Israel:
"I will gather yet others to him
besides those already gathered."

Blind Watchmen

9All you beasts of the field, come to devour,
all you beasts in the forest!

10His watchmen are blind;
they are all without knowledge;
they are all mute dogs;
they cannot bark;
dreaming, lying down,
loving to slumber.

11The dogs have a greedy appetite;
they never know when they have had enough.
They are shepherds who cannot understand;
they have all turned to their own way,
each to his own gain, every last one.

12"Come," they say, "let me get wine,
and let us drink our fill of strong drink;
and tomorrow will be like this day,
great beyond measure."

Notes

  • vv3–5 "the foreigner… the eunuch… a monument and a name" — the law kept the eunuch out of the assembly of the LORD (Deuteronomy 23:1), and certain foreigners with him (23:3). Here the foreigner and the eunuch are named first and given a place in My house and within My walls. "A monument and a name" — yad va-shem, "a hand and a name": a standing stone, as Absalom raised a pillar because I have no son to keep my name in remembrance, and it was called Absalom's Monument (yad Avshalom, 2 Samuel 18:18). The eunuch has no son; the LORD gives him what sons would have given, and better.

  • v3 "I am a dry tree" — no branch will grow from him. The Ethiopian whom Philip met on the road was such a man: a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch, who had come to worship in Jerusalem and was reading Isaiah (Acts 8:27–28).

  • vv2, 4, 6 "who keeps the sabbath, not profaning it… hold fast My covenant" — the sabbath is a sign between Me and you (Exodus 31:13); keeping it is the mark of belonging, and it is open to the foreigner and the eunuch as to Israel.

  • v5 "an everlasting name that will not be cut off" — shem olam… asher lo yikkaret, the words of 55:13, an everlasting sign that will not be cut off. "To each" — the Hebrew turns from them to him, I will give him.

  • v7 "a house of prayer for all the peoples" — Jesus quotes the line when He drives the sellers out of the temple: My house shall be called a house of prayer (Matthew 21:13). Mark gives the whole of it, for all the nations (Mark 11:17).

  • v8 "who gathers the banished of Israel" — nidchei Yisra'el, as in 11:12, gather the banished of Israel. Beyond Israel's own exiles the LORD gathers yet others.

  • vv10–11 "His watchmen are blind… mute dogs… shepherds who cannot understand" — the leaders who should warn the people (watchmen, the word of 52:8, the voice of your watchmen) sleep, and the guard dogs do not bark. "Dreaming" — hozim, a word found only here. "They have all turned to their own way, each to his own gain" — the words of 53:6, we have turned, each one, to his own way, now said of the shepherds.

  • v11 "The dogs have a greedy appetite" — azzei nefesh, "strong of soul": their nefesh, their appetite, is fierce and never satisfied, the soul of 55:2 that is told to delight itself in rich food.

chapters.title: The High and Lifted Up One Dwells with the Crushed
chapters.html:
Isaiah 57

1The righteous man perishes,
and no one lays it to heart;
men of loyal love are taken away,
and no one understands
that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.

2He enters into peace;
they rest in their beds,
each who walks in uprightness.

3But you, come here,
sons of a sorceress,
offspring of the adulterer and the prostitute.

4Whom are you mocking?
Against whom do you open wide your mouth
and stick out your tongue?
Are you not children of transgression,
offspring of deceit,

5you who burn with lust among the oaks,
under every green tree,
who slaughter the children in the valleys,
under the clefts of the rocks?

6Among the smooth stones of the valley is your portion;
they, they are your lot;
to them you have poured out a drink offering,
you have brought a grain offering.
Shall I relent over these things?

7On a high and lifted up mountain
you have set your bed;
there too you went up
to offer sacrifice.

8Behind the door and the doorpost
you have set your memorial;
for, turning from Me, you uncovered your bed and went up;
you made it wide;
you made a covenant for yourself with them;
you loved their bed;
you gazed on a hand.

9You journeyed to Molech with oil
and multiplied your perfumes;
you sent your envoys far off,
and sent them down even to Sheol.

10You were wearied with the length of your way,
but you did not say, "It is hopeless";
you found new life for your strength,
so you did not grow faint.

11Whom did you dread and fear,
that you lied,
and did not remember Me,
did not lay it to heart?
Have I not been silent, and for a long time,
so that you do not fear Me?

12I will declare your righteousness and your deeds,
but they will not profit you.

13When you cry out,
let your collection of idols deliver you!
The wind will carry them all off;
a breath will take them away.
But whoever takes refuge in Me will possess the land
and inherit My holy mountain.

14One will say,
"Build up, build up, prepare the way;
remove every obstacle from My people's way."

15For thus says the One who is high and lifted up,
who dwells forever, whose name is Holy:
"I dwell in the high and holy place,
and with the one who is crushed and lowly in spirit,
to revive the spirit of the lowly
and to revive the heart of the crushed.

16For I will not contend forever,
nor will I always be angry;
for the spirit would grow faint before Me,
and the breath of those I made.

17Because of the iniquity of his gain I was angry,
and I struck him;
I hid My face and was angry;
but he went on turning away
in the way of his own heart.

18I have seen his ways, but I will heal him;
I will lead him and restore comfort to him
and to his mourners,

19creating the fruit of the lips.
Peace, peace, to the far and to the near,"
says the LORD,
"and I will heal him."

20But the wicked are like the tossing sea,
for it cannot be still,
and its waters toss up mire and mud.

21"There is no peace," says my God, "for the wicked."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "The righteous man perishes… He enters into peace" — no one sees why the righteous die; the answer is that they are taken away from the evil to come (ne'esaf, "gathered," the verb of Abraham's death, he was gathered to his people, Genesis 25:8) and rest. "Men of loyal love" — anshei chesed.

  • v5 "you who burn with lust among the oaks" — ba-elim, the oaks of 1:29, the oaks that you desired; the same letters are elim, "gods," and the Greek has who call on idols under leafy trees. "Who slaughter the children in the valleys" — the sacrifice of children that the law forbids, You shall not give any of your children to pass over to Molech (Leviticus 18:21).

  • v6 "Among the smooth stones of the valley is your portion" — be-chalqei nachal chelqekh, "in the smooth things of the valley is your smooth share": chelek, "portion," and chalaq, "smooth," sound alike.

  • vv7, 15 "On a high and lifted up mountain you have set your bed… the One who is high and lifted up" — gavoah ve-nissa and ram ve-nissa. She climbs a high and lifted up mountain to her lovers; the LORD who is high and lifted up (6:1; 52:13) comes down to the crushed.

  • v8 "Behind the door and the doorpost you have set your memorial" — mezuzah, the doorpost on which Israel was told, Write them on the doorposts of your house (Deuteronomy 6:9). Behind it she set up a reminder of her own. "You gazed on a hand" — yad chazit: yad, "hand," is also a monument (56:5, a monument and a name); what she gazed on is not said more plainly.

  • v9 "You journeyed to Molech with oil" — the letters are mlk. The Hebrew vowels read them la-melekh, "to the king"; the same letters spell Molekh, the god of child sacrifice (You shall not give any of your children to pass over to Molech, Leviticus 18:21), and the text reads them so: the children slaughtered in v5, and the envoys sent down even to Sheol in the next line. The Greek has no king or god here.

  • v13 "let your collection of idols deliver you!… a breath will take them away" — qibbutsayikh, "your gatherings." Hevel, "breath," is the vapor of 49:4.

  • v14 "Build up, build up, prepare the way" — pannu derekh, the words of 40:3, In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD; there the way is for the LORD, here for His people.

  • v15 "with the one who is crushed and lowly in spirit… the heart of the crushed" — dakka, nidka'im, the verb of 53:5 and 53:10, he was crushed for our iniquities. The LORD who dwells on high dwells also with the crushed.

  • vv19, 21 "Peace, peace, to the far and to the near… There is no peace… for the wicked" — Paul says Christ came and proclaimed peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near (Ephesians 2:17). The chapter ends with the line of 48:22, here says my God.

chapters.title: The Fast That I Choose
chapters.html:
Isaiah 58

1Cry aloud, do not hold back;
lift up your voice like a ram's horn;
declare to My people their transgression,
and to the house of Jacob their sins.

2Yet they seek Me day after day
and delight to know My ways,
as if they were a nation that did righteousness
and did not forsake the justice of its God;
they ask Me for just judgments;
they delight to draw near to God.

3"Why have we fasted, and You do not see?
Why have we afflicted our souls, and You take no notice?"
But on the day of your fast you seek your own pleasure,
and drive hard all your workers.

4You fast only to quarrel and fight
and to strike with a wicked fist.
Fasting as you do today
will not make your voice heard on high.

5Is such the fast that I choose,
a day for a man to afflict his soul?
Is it to bow down his head like a reed,
and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him?
Will you call this a fast,
and a day of favor to the LORD?

6Is not this the fast that I choose:
to loose the bonds of wickedness,
to undo the straps of the yoke,
to let the oppressed go free,
and to break every yoke?

7Is it not to share your bread with the hungry
and bring the homeless poor into your house;
when you see the naked, to cover him,
and not to hide yourself from your own flesh?

8Then your light will break out like the dawn,
and your healing will spring up quickly;
your righteousness will go before you;
the glory of the LORD will be your rear guard.

9Then you will call, and the LORD will answer;
you will cry for help, and He will say, "Here I am."
If you take away from among you the yoke,
the pointing of the finger, and speaking wickedness,

10if you give your soul to the hungry
and satisfy the soul of the afflicted,
then your light will rise in the darkness,
and your gloom will be like noon.

11The LORD will guide you continually
and satisfy your desire in scorched places
and strengthen your bones;
you will be like a watered garden,
like a spring of water
whose waters do not fail.

12Those from among you will rebuild the ancient ruins;
you will raise up the foundations of many generations;
you will be called the repairer of the breach,
the restorer of streets to live in.

13If you turn back your foot from the sabbath,
from doing your own pleasure on My holy day,
and call the sabbath a delight,
the holy day of the LORD honorable;
if you honor it, not going your own ways,
nor seeking your own pleasure,
nor talking idly,

14then you will delight yourself in the LORD,
and I will make you ride on the heights of the earth;
I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father,
for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.

Notes

  • vv3, 5 "Why have we afflicted our souls?… a day for a man to afflict his soul" — innu nafshenu, the words of the day of atonement, you shall afflict yourselves (Leviticus 16:29). The people keep the form of that fast and ask why God does not notice.

  • vv3, 13 "you seek your own pleasure" — chefets, three times (v3; twice in v13), the word for the LORD's own purpose in 44:28, 53:10 and 55:11. On the fast day and on the sabbath the people pursue their own chefets and not His.

  • v5 "a day of favor to the LORD" — yom ratson, as a time of favor in 49:8.

  • v6 "to let the oppressed go free" — ratsutsim, "the crushed," the word of the crushed reed of 42:3. In the synagogue at Nazareth Jesus reads from Isaiah 61:1–2 and joins to it the Greek of this line, to send away the crushed in release (Luke 4:18).

  • v8 "the glory of the LORD will be your rear guard" — ya'asfekha, the word of 52:12, the God of Israel will be your rear guard: the LORD goes before and behind those who set the oppressed free, as He went before and behind those who came out of Babylon.

  • v9 "He will say, 'Here I am'" — hinneni, the answer of a servant to his master (Abraham's Here I am, Genesis 22:1). Here God gives that answer to the one who calls.

  • v10 "if you give your soul to the hungry and satisfy the soul of the afflicted" — ve-tafeq la-ra'ev nafshekha ve-nefesh na'anah tasbia, nefesh twice: the giver's own appetite is handed over to fill the appetite of the afflicted. In v7 the bread is shared; here the giver gives himself. The Greek has give your bread to the hungry from your soul.

  • v12 "the repairer of the breach" — goder perets, one who builds up a gap in a wall.

  • vv13–14 "call the sabbath a delight… then you will delight yourself in the LORD" — oneg and titanag, one root. The delight given up for His day comes back as delight in Him. "I will make you ride on the heights of the earth" — the words of the Song of Moses, He made him ride on the heights of the earth (Deuteronomy 32:13).

chapters.title: The Redeemer Will Come to Zion
chapters.html:
Isaiah 59

1The LORD's hand is not too short to save,
nor His ear too heavy to hear;

2but your iniquities have made a separation
between you and your God,
and your sins have hidden His face from you,
so that He does not hear.

3For your hands are defiled with blood,
and your fingers with iniquity;
your lips have spoken lies;
your tongue mutters wickedness.

4No one calls for justice,
and no one goes to law honestly;
they trust in emptiness and speak falsehood;
they conceive trouble and give birth to iniquity.

5They hatch adders' eggs
and weave the spider's web;
whoever eats their eggs dies,
and from one that is crushed a viper breaks out.

6Their webs will not become clothing;
they will not cover themselves with what they make;
their works are works of iniquity,
and deeds of violence are in their hands.

7Their feet run to evil,
and they hurry to shed innocent blood;
their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity;
devastation and destruction are in their highways.

8The way of peace they do not know,
and there is no justice in their paths;
they have made their roads crooked;
no one who walks in them knows peace.

9Therefore justice is far from us,
and righteousness does not overtake us;
we hope for light, and there is darkness;
for brightness, and we walk in gloom.

10We grope for the wall like the blind;
we grope like those who have no eyes;
we stumble at noon as in the twilight;
among the strong we are like the dead.

11We all growl like bears;
we moan and moan like doves;
we hope for justice, and there is none;
for deliverance, and it is far from us.

12For our transgressions are many before You,
and our sins testify against us;
for our transgressions are with us,
and we know our iniquities:

13transgressing, and denying the LORD,
and turning back from following our God,
speaking oppression and revolt,
conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood.

14Justice is turned back,
and righteousness stands far off;
for truth has stumbled in the public square,
and uprightness cannot enter.

15Truth is lacking,
and whoever turns from evil makes himself a prey.
The LORD saw it, and it was evil in His eyes
that there was no justice.

16He saw that there was no man,
and was appalled that there was no one to intercede;
then His own arm brought Him deliverance,
and His righteousness upheld Him.

17He put on righteousness as a breastplate,
and a helmet of deliverance on His head;
He put on garments of vengeance for clothing,
and wrapped Himself in zeal as a cloak.

18According to their deeds, so will He repay:
wrath to His adversaries, recompense to His enemies;
to the coastlands He will repay recompense.

19So they will fear the name of the LORD from the west,
and His glory from the rising of the sun;
for He will come like a rushing stream
that the Spirit of the LORD drives on.

20"A Redeemer will come to Zion,
to those in Jacob who turn from transgression,"
declares the LORD.

21"As for Me, this is My covenant with them," says the LORD: "My Spirit that is on you, and My words that I have put in your mouth, will not depart from your mouth, or from the mouth of your offspring, or from the mouth of your offspring's offspring," says the LORD, "from now on and forever."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "The LORD's hand is not too short to save… your iniquities have made a separation" — the answer to the question of 50:2, Is My hand too short to redeem?: the hand is not short, and the ear is not heavy; what stands between is mavdilim, "making a separation," the verb of God who made a division between the light and the darkness (Genesis 1:4) and separated Israel from the peoples (Leviticus 20:26).

  • vv7–8 "Their feet run to evil… The way of peace they do not know" — Paul builds a chain of verses on human sin and takes these lines from the Greek: their feet are swift to shed blood; ruin and misery are in their paths, and the way of peace they have not known (Romans 3:15–17).

  • vv9–11 "we hope for light, and there is darkness" — the people speak for themselves and confess (vv12–13). The light they wait for is the light of 58:8, 10, promised to those who loose the bonds of others.

  • v10 "among the strong we are like the dead" — ba-ashmannim, a word found only here, and its sense is not certain; "the stout, the strong" sets it against the dead.

  • v16 "no one to intercede" — mafgia, the verb of 53:12, he… intercedes for the transgressors. There was no one to stand between, so the LORD's own arm acts. 63:5 says it again in His own voice: I was appalled that there was no one to uphold; My own arm brought Me deliverance.

  • v17 "righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of deliverance" — the LORD arms Himself. Paul gives the armor to believers: having put on the breastplate of righteousness… take the helmet of salvation (Ephesians 6:14, 17; also 1 Thessalonians 5:8).

  • v19 "like a rushing stream that the Spirit of the LORD drives on" — ki yavo kha-nahar tsar, ruach YHWH nosesah vo. Tsar can be "narrow, rushing," said of the stream, or "an adversary": when the adversary comes like a river, the Spirit of the LORD will lift a banner against him, reading nosesah from nes, "banner." The Greek has the wrath of the Lord will come like a violent river.

  • v20 "A Redeemer will come to Zion" — go'el, the kinsman who buys back (41:14). Paul quotes the Greek of vv20–21, The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will turn away ungodliness from Jacob (Romans 11:26–27).

  • v21 "My Spirit that is on you, and My words that I have put in your mouth" — the words said to the servant, I have put My words in your mouth (51:16), and the Spirit put on him (42:1), now promised to the people and to their children's children.

speech.text: Isaiah 59
The LORD's hand is not too short to save, nor His ear too heavy to hear;
but your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God, and your sins have hidden His face from you, so that He does not hear.
For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken lies; your tongue mutters wickedness.
No one calls for justice, and no one goes to law honestly; they trust in emptiness and speak falsehood; they conceive trouble and give birth to iniquity.
They hatch adders' eggs and weave the spider's web; whoever eats their eggs dies, and from one that is crushed a viper breaks out.
Their webs will not become clothing; they will not cover themselves with what they make; their works are works of iniquity, and deeds of violence are in their hands.
Their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood; their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; devastation and destruction are in their highways.
The way of peace they do not know, and there is no justice in their paths; they have made their roads crooked; no one who walks in them knows peace.
Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness does not overtake us; we hope for light, and there is darkness; for brightness, and we walk in gloom.
We grope for the wall like the blind; we grope like those who have no eyes; we stumble at noon as in the twilight; among the strong we are like the dead.
We all growl like bears; we moan and moan like doves; we hope for justice, and there is none; for deliverance, and it is far from us.
For our transgressions are many before You, and our sins testify against us; for our transgressions are with us, and we know our iniquities:
transgressing, and denying the LORD, and turning back from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood.
Justice is turned back, and righteousness stands far off; for truth has stumbled in the public square, and uprightness cannot enter.
Truth is lacking, and whoever turns from evil makes himself a prey. The LORD saw it, and it was evil in His eyes that there was no justice.
He saw that there was no man, and was appalled that there was no one to intercede; then His own arm brought Him deliverance, and His righteousness upheld Him.
He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of deliverance on His head; He put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and wrapped Himself in zeal as a cloak.
According to their deeds, so will He repay: wrath to His adversaries, recompense to His enemies; to the coastlands He will repay recompense.
So they will fear the name of the LORD from the west, and His glory from the rising of the sun; for He will come like a rushing stream that the Spirit of the LORD drives on.
"A Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression," declares the LORD.

"As for Me, this is My covenant with them," says the LORD: "My Spirit that is on you, and My words that I have put in your mouth, will not depart from your mouth, or from the mouth of your offspring, or from the mouth of your offspring's offspring," says the LORD, "from now on and forever."

chapters.title: Arise, Shine
chapters.html:
Isaiah 60

1Arise, shine, for your light has come,
and the glory of the LORD has risen on you.

2For darkness covers the earth,
and thick darkness the peoples;
but the LORD will rise on you,
and His glory will be seen on you.

3Nations will come to your light,
and kings to the brightness of your rising.

4Lift up your eyes all around and see:
they all gather together, they come to you;
your sons will come from afar,
and your daughters will be carried on the hip.

5Then you will see and be radiant;
your heart will tremble and swell,
because the abundance of the sea will be turned to you;
the wealth of the nations will come to you.

6A multitude of camels will cover you,
the young camels of Midian and Ephah;
all those from Sheba will come;
they will bring gold and frankincense,
and proclaim the praises of the LORD.

7All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you;
the rams of Nebaioth will minister to you;
they will come up with favor on My altar,
and I will beautify My beautiful house.

8Who are these that fly like a cloud,
and like doves to their windows?

9For the coastlands wait for Me,
and the ships of Tarshish first,
to bring your sons from afar,
their silver and gold with them,
for the name of the LORD your God,
and for the Holy One of Israel,
because He has glorified you.

10Foreigners will build up your walls,
and their kings will minister to you;
for in My wrath I struck you,
but in My favor I have had compassion on you.

11Your gates will be open continually;
day and night they will not be shut,
so that people may bring to you the wealth of the nations,
with their kings led in procession.

12For the nation and the kingdom that will not serve you will perish;
those nations will be utterly laid waste.

13The glory of Lebanon will come to you,
the cypress, the plane and the pine together,
to beautify the place of My sanctuary,
and I will make the place of My feet glorious.

14The sons of those who afflicted you
will come bending low to you,
and all who despised you
will bow down at the soles of your feet;
they will call you the City of the LORD,
the Zion of the Holy One of Israel.

15Instead of being forsaken and hated,
with no one passing through,
I will make you majestic forever,
a joy from generation to generation.

16You will drink the milk of nations;
you will nurse at the breast of kings;
and you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior,
and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

17Instead of bronze I will bring gold,
and instead of iron I will bring silver,
instead of wood, bronze,
instead of stones, iron.
I will make peace your overseers
and righteousness your slave drivers.

18Violence will no longer be heard in your land,
devastation or destruction within your borders;
you will call your walls Deliverance,
and your gates Praise.

19The sun will no longer be your light by day,
nor will the brightness of the moon give you light;
but the LORD will be your everlasting light,
and your God your beauty.

20Your sun will no longer go down,
nor your moon withdraw;
for the LORD will be your everlasting light,
and the days of your mourning will be ended.

21Your people will all be righteous;
they will possess the land forever,
the branch of My planting,
the work of My hands, that I may be glorified.

22The least one will become a thousand,
and the smallest a mighty nation.
I am the LORD; in its time I will hasten it.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "Arise, shine… the brightness of your rising" — zarach, the verb of the sun rising, three times (vv1, 2, 3): the LORD rises on Zion like the sun, and the nations walk to her light. The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light (9:2); here the darkness covers the peoples, and Zion is where the light is.

  • v6 "gold and frankincense" — camels from Midian, Ephah and Sheba bring gifts and praise. The magi from the east bring gold, frankincense and myrrh to the child (Matthew 2:11).

  • v7 "Kedar… Nebaioth" — the sons of Ishmael, Nebaioth; and Kedar (Genesis 25:13): the tribes of the desert bring their flocks to the altar.

  • vv7, 9, 13, 21 "I will beautify… He has glorified you… to beautify… that I may be glorified" — pa'ar, the verb of 49:3 and 55:5, four times in the chapter: the LORD makes His house and His city beautiful, and is glorified in His people.

  • v10 "in My wrath I struck you, but in My favor I have had compassion" — as 54:7–8, For a brief moment I forsook you, but with great compassion I will gather you.

  • v17 "righteousness your slave drivers" — nogesayikh, the word for Egypt's slave drivers (Exodus 3:7) and for those Israel will one day rule over (14:2). Those who drove Zion will be replaced by peace and righteousness.

  • vv19–20 "the LORD will be your everlasting light" — sun and moon give way to the LORD Himself. The city John sees has no need of the sun or of the moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gave it light (Revelation 21:23).

  • v21 "the branch of My planting" — netser, the branch that comes from the roots of Jesse (11:1), here said of the whole people. "My planting" is the read form matta'ai; the written form is matta'o, "His planting."

  • v22 "The least one will become a thousand" — as Abraham was one when I called him and was made many (51:2). "In its time I will hasten it" — be-ittah achishennah: the LORD sets the time, and when it comes He does not delay.

chapters.title: The Year of the LORD's Favor
chapters.html:
Isaiah 61

1The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on me,
because the LORD has anointed me
to bring good news to the poor;
He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted,
to proclaim liberty to the captives,
and the opening of the prison to those who are bound;

2to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor,
and the day of vengeance of our God;
to comfort all who mourn;

3to grant to those who mourn in Zion,
to give them a garland instead of ashes,
the oil of gladness instead of mourning,
the garment of praise instead of a faint spirit;
and they will be called oaks of righteousness,
the planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified.

4They will build up the ancient ruins;
they will raise up the former desolations;
they will renew the ruined cities,
the desolations of many generations.

5Strangers will stand and shepherd your flocks;
foreigners will be your plowmen and vinedressers.

6But you will be called priests of the LORD;
they will speak of you as ministers of our God;
you will eat the wealth of the nations,
and in their glory you will boast.

7Instead of your shame there will be a double portion;
instead of disgrace they will rejoice in their portion;
therefore in their land they will possess a double portion;
everlasting joy will be theirs.

8For I, the LORD, love justice;
I hate robbery and wrongdoing;
I will faithfully give them their reward,
and make an everlasting covenant with them.

9Their offspring will be known among the nations,
and their descendants among the peoples;
all who see them will acknowledge
that they are the offspring the LORD has blessed.

10I will greatly rejoice in the LORD;
my soul will exult in my God;
for He has clothed me with garments of deliverance;
He has wrapped me in a robe of righteousness,
as a bridegroom wears a garland like a priest,
and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.

11For as the earth brings forth its sprouts,
and as a garden makes what is sown in it spring up,
so the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise
spring up before all the nations.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on me, because the LORD has anointed me" — mashach, "anointed," the verb behind mashiach, the title given to Cyrus in 45:1. In the synagogue at Nazareth Jesus reads these lines from the Greek, stops at to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor, rolls up the scroll and says, Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing (Luke 4:16–21). He stops before the day of vengeance.

  • v1 "to proclaim liberty to the captives" — deror, the liberty of the jubilee, proclaim liberty in the land to all who live in it (Leviticus 25:10). "The opening of the prison" — peqach-qoach, "opening, opening," of eyes or of doors; the Greek reads it of the eyes, recovery of sight to the blind, and Luke 4:18 follows the Greek.

  • vv2–3 "the year of the LORD's favor… to comfort all who mourn" — ratson, as a time of favor (49:8) and a day of favor (58:5); to comfort, the word of 40:1, Comfort, comfort My people.

  • v3 "a garland instead of ashes" — pe'er tachat efer, two words with the same letters in another order: the mourner's ashes on the head are exchanged for a festal headdress. "Oaks of righteousness" — elei ha-tsedeq, the oaks of 1:29 and 57:5, where idols were worshipped, now a name for the people. "The planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified" — the words of 60:21.

  • v6 "you will be called priests of the LORD" — what Israel was called to be at Sinai, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation (Exodus 19:6). Peter gives the name to the church, a royal priesthood, a holy nation (1 Peter 2:9).

  • v7 "a double portion" — mishneh, "a second, a double share." The verse moves from your shame to they will rejoice, you and they in the same line, as the Hebrew has it.

  • v8 "I hate robbery and wrongdoing" — gazel be-avlah, following the Greek, robbery from injustice: the LORD who loves justice hates what was done to His people, and so repays them (I will faithfully give them their reward). The Hebrew vowels read the same letters be-olah, "with a burnt offering": I hate robbery with a burnt offering, a sacrifice brought from stolen goods.

  • v10 "as a bridegroom wears a garland like a priest" — yekhahen pe'er, "acts the priest with a garland": the verb is kohen, "priest," and the pe'er is the garland of v3. The LORD put on righteousness and deliverance Himself in 59:17; here He clothes the one who speaks with garments of deliverance and a robe of righteousness.

chapters.title: A New Name
chapters.html:
Isaiah 62

1For Zion's sake I will not keep silent,
and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest,
until her righteousness goes out like brightness,
and her deliverance like a burning torch.

2The nations will see your righteousness,
and all kings your glory;
and you will be called by a new name
that the mouth of the LORD will give.

3You will be a crown of beauty in the hand of the LORD,
and a royal diadem in the palm of your God.

4You will no longer be called Forsaken,
and your land will no longer be called Desolate;
but you will be called My Delight Is in Her,
and your land Married;
for the LORD delights in you,
and your land will be married.

5For as a young man marries a virgin,
so your sons will marry you;
and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride,
so your God will rejoice over you.

6On your walls, Jerusalem,
I have set watchmen;
all day and all night
they will never be silent.
You who remind the LORD,
take no rest,

7and give Him no rest
until He establishes Jerusalem
and makes it a praise in the earth.

8The LORD has sworn by His right hand
and by His mighty arm:
"I will no longer give your grain
as food to your enemies,
and foreigners will not drink your new wine
for which you have labored;

9but those who gather it will eat it
and praise the LORD,
and those who collect it will drink it
in the courts of My sanctuary."

10Go through, go through the gates;
prepare the way for the people;
build up, build up the highway;
clear it of stones;
lift up a signal over the peoples.

11The LORD has proclaimed
to the end of the earth:
Say to the daughter of Zion,
"Your deliverance is coming;
His reward is with Him,
and His recompense before Him."

12They will be called The Holy People,
The Redeemed of the LORD;
and you will be called Sought Out,
A City Not Forsaken.

Notes

  • v1 "like brightness… like a burning torch" — nogah, the brightness of 60:3, kings to the brightness of your rising. Zion's deliverance is seen from far off, like a torch at night.

  • vv2, 4, 12 "a new name… My Delight Is in Her… Married… Sought Out" — the names Zion is given answer the names she had: Azuvah, "Forsaken," becomes Cheftsi-vah, "My delight is in her," and Shemamah, "Desolate," becomes Be'ulah, "Married" (the married one of 54:1). Written as names they are Hephzibah and Beulah; Hephzibah was the name of the mother of Manasseh (2 Kings 21:1). The chapter ends with two more: Derushah, "Sought Out," and A City Not Forsaken.

  • v4 "for the LORD delights in you" — chafets, the verb of the name Cheftsi-vah; the LORD whose purpose (chefets) the servant carried out (53:10) now delights in Zion.

  • v5 "so your sons will marry you" — yiv'alukh banayikh. Read as the Hebrew vowels have it, the sons of the city take her as a bride: the people settle the land and possess it, as your land will be married in v4. The same letters read bonayikh, "your Builder" (plural in form, as your Maker and your husband in 54:5), which would make the LORD the one who marries her, as the next line says, so your God will rejoice over you; the Greek has so your sons will live with you.

  • v6 "You who remind the LORD" — ha-mazkirim, the title of Joah son of Asaph, the recorder (36:3). The watchmen keep the LORD's promise before Him, day and night.

  • vv8–9 "foreigners will not drink your new wine for which you have labored" — the oath undoes the curse of Deuteronomy 28:33, A people you have not known will eat the fruit of your ground and all your labor.

  • v10 "prepare the way… build up, build up the highway" — pannu derekh, the words of 40:3, and sollu sollu, the words of 57:14. "Lift up a signal" — nes, as in 11:12 and 49:22.

  • v11 "Your deliverance is coming; His reward is with Him, and His recompense before Him" — the last line is 40:10 word for word, said there of the Lord GOD. Here deliverance (yesha) is spoken of as a person; the Greek has Your Savior has come. Matthew's account of the entry into Jerusalem begins with this verse's words, Say to the daughter of Zion (Matthew 21:5).

speech.text: Isaiah 62
For Zion's sake I will not keep silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until her righteousness goes out like brightness, and her deliverance like a burning torch.
The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory; and you will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give.
You will be a crown of beauty in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the palm of your God.

You will no longer be called Forsaken, and your land will no longer be called Desolate; but you will be called My Delight Is in Her, and your land Married; for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
For as a young man marries a virgin, so your sons will marry you; and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
On your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen; all day and all night they will never be silent. You who remind the LORD, take no rest,
and give Him no rest until He establishes Jerusalem and makes it a praise in the earth.
The LORD has sworn by His right hand and by His mighty arm: "I will no longer give your grain as food to your enemies, and foreigners will not drink your new wine for which you have labored;
but those who gather it will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who collect it will drink it in the courts of My sanctuary."

They will be called The Holy People, The Redeemed of the LORD; and you will be called Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken.

chapters.title: The One Who Comes from Edom
chapters.html:
Isaiah 63

1Who is this coming from Edom,
in crimsoned garments from Bozrah,
this one splendid in His clothing,
striding in the greatness of His strength?
"It is I, speaking in righteousness,
mighty to save."

2Why is Your clothing red,
and Your garments like one who treads in the winepress?

3"I have trodden the winepress alone,
and from the peoples no one was with Me.
I trod them in My anger
and trampled them in My wrath;
their lifeblood spattered on My garments,
and I have stained all My clothing.

4For the day of vengeance was in My heart,
and the year of My redemption had come.

5I looked, and there was no one to help;
I was appalled that there was no one to uphold;
My own arm brought Me deliverance,
and My wrath upheld Me.

6I trampled down the peoples in My anger,
made them drunk in My wrath,
and poured out their lifeblood on the earth."

Remembering the Days of Old

7I will recount the LORD's acts of loyal love,
the praises of the LORD,
according to all that the LORD has done for us,
and His great goodness to the house of Israel,
which He has shown them according to His compassion,
according to the abundance of His loyal love.

8For He said, "Surely they are My people,
sons who will not deal falsely";
and He became their Savior

9in all their distress.
It was no envoy or messenger,
but His own presence that saved them;
in His love and in His pity He redeemed them;
He lifted them up and carried them
all the days of old.

10But they rebelled
and grieved His Holy Spirit;
so He turned to be their enemy,
and He Himself fought against them.

11Then His people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses:
Where is He who brought them up out of the sea
with the shepherds of His flock?
Where is He who put His Holy Spirit among them,

12who made His glorious arm go at the right hand of Moses,
who split the waters before them
to make for Himself an everlasting name,

13who led them through the depths?
Like a horse in the wilderness,
they did not stumble.

14Like livestock going down into the valley,
the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest.
So You led Your people,
to make for Yourself a glorious name.

15Look down from heaven and see,
from Your holy and glorious dwelling.
Where are Your zeal and Your might?
The yearning of Your heart and Your compassion
are restrained toward me.

16For You are our Father,
though Abraham does not know us
and Israel does not acknowledge us;
You, LORD, are our Father;
our Redeemer from of old is Your name.

17Why, LORD, do You make us wander from Your ways,
and harden our heart so that we do not fear You?
Return for the sake of Your servants,
the tribes of Your inheritance.

18Your holy people possessed it for a little while;
our adversaries have trampled down Your sanctuary.

19We have long been like those You never ruled,
like those not called by Your name.

Notes

  • v1 "Who is this coming from Edom… from Bozrah" — Edom sounds like adom, "red," the word of v2, Why is Your clothing red?; Esau was named Edom for that red, that red there (Genesis 25:30). Bozrah, Edom's city, has the root letters of batsir, the grape harvest, b-ts-r. Both names point to the winepress before it is named. Edom has already been the place of the LORD's judgment: the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom (34:6).

  • vv3–4 "I have stained all My clothing… the year of My redemption" — eg'alti, "I have stained," and ge'ulai, "My redemption," are spelled with the same three letters, g-'-l: one root means "to defile," the other "to buy back," the root of the Redeemer of 59:20. The garments are stained in the work of redeeming. "The day of vengeance… the year" — the pair of 61:2, the year of the LORD's favor, and the day of vengeance of our God, in the reverse order.

  • v3 "I have trodden the winepress alone" — John sees the rider called the Word of God clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and He treads the winepress of the wine of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty (Revelation 19:13, 15).

  • v5 "I was appalled that there was no one to uphold; My own arm brought Me deliverance" — the words of 59:16, told there of the LORD, He saw that there was no man, and was appalled that there was no one to intercede; then His own arm brought Him deliverance, and here spoken by Him. There He put on garments of vengeance (59:17); here they are stained.

  • vv8–9 "He became their Savior in all their distress. It was no envoy or messenger, but His own presence that saved them" — this follows the written Hebrew and the Greek. The written form is lo, "not," and tsar, read tsir, "envoy," the word for the envoys of 57:9; the Greek has He became their salvation out of all their distress. Not an envoy, nor a messenger, but He Himself saved them. Panav, "His face," His presence, is the LORD Himself, as in Deuteronomy 4:37, where be-fanav, "by His face," is He Himself brought you out of Egypt. The read form is lo, "to Him," which gives In all their distress He was distressed, and the messenger of His presence saved them.

  • vv9, 14 "His own presence… gave them rest" — both halves of the LORD's promise to Moses, My face will go, and I will give you rest (Exodus 33:14): panav, "His face," and tenichennu, "gave them rest," the same verb. After the golden calf the LORD said He would send a messenger and I will not go up among you (Exodus 33:2–3), and Moses answered, If Your face is not going, do not take us up from here (33:15).

  • vv10–11 "His Holy Spirit" — ruach qodsho, found only here and in David's prayer, do not take Your Holy Spirit from me (Psalm 51:11). Paul's do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God (Ephesians 4:30) turns v10 into a warning.

  • v11 "Then His people remembered… the shepherds of His flock" — the Hebrew is he remembered the days of old, Moses, His people: the one who remembers is not named, and the question that follows, Where is He…?, is the people's. The shepherds are Moses and Aaron: You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron (Psalm 77:20). The Greek has the singular, the shepherd of the sheep, and Hebrews takes those words for Jesus: the God of peace, who brought up from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep (Hebrews 13:20).

  • v16 "You are our Father, though Abraham does not know us" — the people were told, Look to Abraham your father (51:2). In their prayer they say Abraham would not know them, and they call the LORD their Father, twice in this verse and again in 64:8.

speech.text: Isaiah 63
Who is this coming from Edom, in crimsoned garments from Bozrah, this one splendid in His clothing, striding in the greatness of His strength? "It is I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to save."
Why is Your clothing red, and Your garments like one who treads in the winepress?

"I have trodden the winepress alone, and from the peoples no one was with Me. I trod them in My anger and trampled them in My wrath; their lifeblood spattered on My garments, and I have stained all My clothing.
For the day of vengeance was in My heart, and the year of My redemption had come.
I looked, and there was no one to help; I was appalled that there was no one to uphold; My own arm brought Me deliverance, and My wrath upheld Me.
I trampled down the peoples in My anger, made them drunk in My wrath, and poured out their lifeblood on the earth."
Remembering the Days of Old

I will recount the LORD's acts of loyal love, the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD has done for us, and His great goodness to the house of Israel, which He has shown them according to His compassion, according to the abundance of His loyal love.
For He said, "Surely they are My people, sons who will not deal falsely"; and He became their Savior
in all their distress. It was no envoy or messenger, but His own presence that saved them; in His love and in His pity He redeemed them; He lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
But they rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit; so He turned to be their enemy, and He Himself fought against them.
Then His people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses: Where is He who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of His flock? Where is He who put His Holy Spirit among them,
who made His glorious arm go at the right hand of Moses, who split the waters before them to make for Himself an everlasting name,
who led them through the depths? Like a horse in the wilderness, they did not stumble.
Like livestock going down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest. So You led Your people, to make for Yourself a glorious name.
Look down from heaven and see, from Your holy and glorious dwelling. Where are Your zeal and Your might? The yearning of Your heart and Your compassion are restrained toward me.
For You are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us; You, LORD, are our Father; our Redeemer from of old is Your name.
Why, LORD, do You make us wander from Your ways, and harden our heart so that we do not fear You? Return for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your inheritance.
Your holy people possessed it for a little while; our adversaries have trampled down Your sanctuary.
We have long been like those You never ruled, like those not called by Your name.

chapters.title: Tear Open the Heavens
chapters.html:
Isaiah 64

1Oh, that You would tear open the heavens and come down,
that the mountains would quake at Your presence,

2as when fire kindles brushwood,
and fire makes water boil,
to make Your name known to Your adversaries,
so that the nations might tremble at Your presence!

3When You did awesome things that we did not look for,
You came down; the mountains quaked at Your presence.

4From of old no one has heard,
no ear has perceived,
no eye has seen a God besides You,
who acts for the one who waits for Him.

5You meet the one who gladly does righteousness,
those who remember You in Your ways.
You were angry, and we sinned;
we have been in our sins a long time,
and will we be saved?

6We have all become like one who is unclean,
and all our righteous deeds are like a menstrual cloth.
We all wither like a leaf,
and our iniquities, like the wind, carry us away.

7There is no one who calls on Your name,
who rouses himself to take hold of You;
for You have hidden Your face from us
and made us melt away in the power of our iniquities.

8But now, LORD, You are our Father;
we are the clay, and You are our potter;
we are all the work of Your hand.

9Do not be angry beyond measure, LORD,
and do not remember iniquity forever.
Look on us, please: we are all Your people.

10Your holy cities have become a wilderness;
Zion has become a wilderness,
Jerusalem a desolation.

11Our holy and beautiful house,
where our fathers praised You,
has been burned with fire,
and all our precious things have become ruins.

12Will You restrain Yourself at these things, LORD?
Will You keep silent and afflict us beyond measure?

Notes

  • v1 "Oh, that You would tear open the heavens and come down" — in the Hebrew these words end 63:19, and the Hebrew numbers the rest of this chapter one lower (64:2 is Hebrew 64:1); the English numbering is followed. Qara, "tear," is the word for tearing a garment. At Jesus' baptism Mark says He saw the heavens being torn open (Mark 1:10), where the Greek of Isaiah has if You open the heaven.

  • v4 "no eye has seen a God besides You, who acts for the one who waits for Him" — Paul writes, as it is written: What no eye has seen and no ear has heard, and what has not entered the heart of man, what God has prepared for those who love Him (1 Corinthians 2:9). His words are close to this verse, though not those of the Greek of Isaiah, which has we have not heard, nor have our eyes seen a God besides You, and Your works which You will do for those who wait for mercy.

  • v5 "we have been in our sins a long time, and will we be saved?" — bahem olam ve-nivvashea, "in them, long; and we will be saved." Read as a question, them are the sins of we sinned, and the people ask whether there is any hope left. Read as a statement, them are Your ways two lines above: in them we will be forever, and we will be saved. The Hebrew has no mark of a question. The Greek reads the line another way: You were angry, and we sinned; therefore we went astray.

  • v6 "like one who is unclean… like a menstrual cloth" — tame, "unclean," the cry the blighted man must call out, Unclean! Unclean! (Leviticus 13:45); beged iddim, "a garment of monthly flow," the uncleanness of a woman in her monthly separation, which passed to anyone who touched her and to everything she lay or sat on (Leviticus 15:19–20). The Greek has the rag of a woman sitting apart. The people say their righteous deeds themselves carry the uncleanness.

  • v8 "we are the clay, and You are our potter" — yotsrenu, "the one who forms us," the potter of 29:16 and the One who formed him of 45:9. There the clay talks back to the potter; here it asks Him to remember that it is His work.

  • v11 "Our holy and beautiful house… has been burned with fire" — the burning is told in 2 Kings 25:9, He burned the house of the LORD. Beautiful is tif'arteinu, from pa'ar, the word of the LORD's promise in 60:7, I will beautify My beautiful house.

  • v12 "Will You restrain Yourself… Will You keep silent" — tit'appaq… techesheh, the two verbs of 42:14, For a long time I have held My peace; I have kept still and restrained Myself, where the LORD said the silence would end; restrained is also the word of 63:15. The answer comes in the next chapter: I will not keep silent, but I will repay (65:6).

chapters.title: New Heavens and a New Earth
chapters.html:
Isaiah 65

1I let Myself be sought by those who did not ask;
I let Myself be found by those who did not seek Me.
I said, "Here I am, here I am,"
to a nation not called by My name.

2I have spread out My hands all day long
to a rebellious people,
who walk in a way that is not good,
following their own thoughts;

3a people who provoke Me
to My face continually,
sacrificing in the gardens
and burning incense on the bricks;

4who sit among the graves
and spend the night in hidden places;
who eat the flesh of pigs,
with broth of foul meat in their pots;

5who say, "Keep to yourself;
do not come near me, for I am too holy for you."
These are smoke in My nostrils,
a fire that burns all day.

6It stands written before Me:
I will not keep silent, but I will repay;
I will repay into their lap

7your iniquities and your fathers' iniquities together,
says the LORD,
because they burned incense on the mountains
and insulted Me on the hills;
I will measure into their lap
payment for their former deeds.

8Thus says the LORD:
As when new wine is found in the cluster,
and someone says, "Do not destroy it,
for there is a blessing in it,"
so I will do for the sake of My servants,
and not destroy them all.

9I will bring out offspring from Jacob,
and from Judah an heir to My mountains;
My chosen ones will possess it,
and My servants will live there.

10Sharon will become a pasture for flocks,
and the Valley of Achor a resting place for herds,
for My people who have sought Me.

11But you who forsake the LORD,
who forget My holy mountain,
who set a table for Fortune
and fill cups of mixed wine for Destiny,

12I will destine you to the sword,
and all of you will bow down to the slaughter;
because when I called, you did not answer;
when I spoke, you did not listen;
but you did what was evil in My eyes,
and chose what I did not delight in.

13Therefore thus says the Lord GOD:
My servants will eat,
but you will be hungry;
My servants will drink,
but you will be thirsty;
My servants will rejoice,
but you will be put to shame;

14My servants will sing for gladness of heart,
but you will cry out for pain of heart,
and wail for a broken spirit.

15You will leave your name
to My chosen ones for a curse,
and the Lord GOD will put you to death;
but His servants He will call by another name,

16so that whoever blesses himself in the land
will bless himself by the God of truth,
and whoever swears in the land
will swear by the God of truth;
for the former troubles are forgotten
and are hidden from My eyes.

17For I am about to create new heavens
and a new earth;
the former things will not be remembered
or come to mind.

18But be glad and rejoice forever
in what I create;
for I am about to create Jerusalem to be a joy,
and her people to be a gladness.

19I will rejoice in Jerusalem
and be glad in My people;
no more will the sound of weeping be heard in her,
or the sound of crying.

20No more will there be in it
an infant who lives but a few days,
or an old man who does not fill out his days;
for the youth will die a hundred years old,
and the one who falls short of a hundred will be thought accursed.

21They will build houses and live in them;
they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

22They will not build for another to live in;
they will not plant for another to eat;
for like the days of a tree
will be the days of My people,
and My chosen ones will long enjoy
the work of their hands.

23They will not labor in vain,
or bear children for sudden terror;
for they are the offspring of those blessed by the LORD,
and their descendants with them.

24And it shall come to pass, before they call, that I will answer;
while they are still speaking, I will hear.

25The wolf and the lamb shall graze together,
and the lion shall eat straw like the ox,
and dust shall be the serpent's food.
They shall not harm or destroy
in all My holy mountain,
says the LORD.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "I let Myself be sought… to a nation not called by My name" — nidrashti, "I let Myself be sought." A nation not called by My name is what the people said of themselves in 63:19, like those not called by Your name; and Here I am (hinneni) is the servant's answer, given by the LORD as in 58:9. Paul quotes the Greek of these two verses and divides them: v1, I was found by those who did not seek Me, of the nations, and v2, All day long I have held out My hands to a disobedient and contrary people, of Israel (Romans 10:20–21).

  • vv3–4 "sacrificing in the gardens… who eat the flesh of pigs" — the gardens of 1:29 and of 66:17, where the same people again eat the flesh of pigs; the pig is unclean in the law (Leviticus 11:7). "Spend the night in hidden places" — the Greek says they sleep in the caves for dreams. "Broth of foul meat" — piggulim, the word for an offering eaten on the third day, It is foul (Leviticus 7:18). Broth is the read form, u-meraq; the written form is u-feraq, "and pieces."

  • v5 "I am too holy for you" — qedashtikha, "I am holy to you." The warning not to come near rests on the law's rule for the holiest offerings, Whatever touches them becomes holy (Leviticus 6:18). To the LORD such holiness is smoke in My nostrils.

  • v10 "the Valley of Achor" — achor is "trouble": Joshua said to Achan, Why have you brought trouble on us? The LORD will bring trouble on you today, and the place was named for it, the Valley of Achor to this day (Joshua 7:25–26). The valley named for that trouble becomes a place where herds lie down.

  • vv11–12 "for Fortune… for Destiny… I will destine you" — Gad and Meni, gods of luck. Gad is the word Leah said at her son's birth, Fortune has come (Genesis 30:11). Meni is from manah, "to count, to allot," and the LORD answers with the same verb, u-maniti, I will destine you to the sword. The Greek has a table for the demon and mixed wine for Fortune.

  • vv15–16 "another name… the God of truth" — the servants receive a new name, as Zion did (62:2). "The God of truth" is Elohei amen, "the God of Amen," twice: amen is the word that seals an oath, as the woman says Amen, amen in Numbers 5:22. In Revelation Jesus speaks as the Amen, the faithful and true witness (Revelation 3:14). The Greek has the true God.

  • vv17–19 "new heavens and a new earth… no more will the sound of weeping be heard" — bore, "create," three times in two verses, the verb of In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth (Genesis 1:1). John sees a new heaven and a new earth, and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death will be no more; neither mourning nor crying nor pain will be any more (Revelation 21:1, 4). Peter waits for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells (2 Peter 3:13).

  • v20 "the one who falls short of a hundred will be thought accursed" — ha-chote, from chata, whose first sense is "to miss": the left-handed men of Benjamin could sling a stone at a hair and not miss (Judges 20:16). Read so, the line carries on the one before it: life will be so long that to die short of a hundred will be counted a curse (yequllal, "will be cursed"). The same word is the usual word for the sinner, and the Greek reads it that way: the sinner who dies at a hundred years will be accursed.

  • vv21–22 "They will build houses and live in them" — the curse of Deuteronomy 28:30 undone: You will build a house and not live in it. You will plant a vineyard and not use its fruit. "Like the days of a tree" — the Greek has like the days of the tree of life (Genesis 2:9).

  • v25 "The wolf and the lamb… They shall not harm or destroy in all My holy mountain" — the picture of 11:6–9, with two of its lines word for word: the lion shall eat straw like the ox (11:7) and They shall not harm or destroy in all My holy mountain (11:9). One line is new, dust shall be the serpent's food: the serpent's sentence, dust you shall eat all the days of your life (Genesis 3:14), still stands.

chapters.title: Heaven Is My Throne
chapters.html:
Isaiah 66

1Thus says the LORD:
Heaven is My throne,
and the earth is My footstool;
where is the house you would build for Me,
and where is the place of My rest?

2All these things My hand has made,
and so all these things came to be,
declares the LORD.
But this is the one I will look to:
the one who is poor and broken in spirit,
and trembles at My word.

3Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who kills a man;
whoever sacrifices a lamb, like one who breaks a dog's neck;
whoever presents a grain offering, like one who offers pig's blood;
whoever burns frankincense as a memorial, like one who blesses an idol.
They have chosen their own ways,
and their soul delights in their loathsome things;

4so I also will choose harsh treatment for them,
and bring on them what they dread;
because when I called, no one answered;
when I spoke, they did not listen;
but they did what was evil in My eyes,
and chose what I did not delight in.

5Hear the word of the LORD,
you who tremble at His word:
Your brothers who hate you
and cast you out for My name's sake
have said, "Let the LORD be glorified,
so that we may see your joy";
but they will be put to shame.

6A sound of uproar from the city!
A sound from the temple!
The sound of the LORD,
repaying His enemies what they deserve!

7Before she was in labor, she gave birth;
before her pain came upon her,
she delivered a male child.

8Who has heard such a thing?
Who has seen such things?
Can a land be born in one day?
Can a nation be brought forth at once?
Yet as soon as Zion was in labor,
she gave birth to her sons.

9"Shall I bring to the mouth of the womb
and not bring to birth?" says the LORD.
"Shall I, who bring to birth, shut the womb?"
says your God.

10Rejoice with Jerusalem,
and be glad for her, all you who love her;
rejoice with her in joy,
all you who mourn over her,

11so that you may nurse and be satisfied
at her comforting breast,
so that you may drink deeply and delight
in her abundant glory.

12For thus says the LORD:
I am about to extend peace to her like a river,
and the glory of the nations like an overflowing stream;
and you will nurse; you will be carried on the hip
and bounced on the knees.

13As one whom his mother comforts,
so I will comfort you;
you will be comforted in Jerusalem.

14You will see, and your heart will rejoice;
your bones will flourish like the grass;
the hand of the LORD will be known to His servants,
and His indignation to His enemies.

15For the LORD will come in fire,
and His chariots like the whirlwind,
to pay back His anger in fury,
and His rebuke in flames of fire.

16For by fire the LORD will enter into judgment,
and by His sword, with all flesh;
and those slain by the LORD will be many.

17Those who consecrate and purify themselves
to go into the gardens,
following one in the middle,
who eat the flesh of pigs,
loathsome things and mice,
will come to an end together, declares the LORD.

18As for Me, I know their works and their thoughts;
the time is coming to gather all nations and tongues;
and they will come and see My glory.

19I will set a sign among them, and I will send survivors from them to the nations: to Tarshish, Pul and Lud, who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, to the far coastlands that have not heard of My fame or seen My glory; and they will declare My glory among the nations.

20They will bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the LORD, on horses, in chariots, in covered wagons, on mules and on swift camels, to My holy mountain Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the sons of Israel bring their offering in a clean vessel to the house of the LORD.

21I will also take some of them for priests and for Levites, says the LORD.

22For as the new heavens and the new earth
that I am making
will remain before Me, declares the LORD,
so your offspring and your name will remain.

23From new moon to new moon,
and from sabbath to sabbath,
all flesh will come to worship before Me,
says the LORD.

24They will go out and look
on the corpses of the men
who have rebelled against Me;
for their worm will not die,
and their fire will not be quenched,
and they will be an abhorrence to all flesh.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool; where is the house you would build for Me?" — Solomon said it at the dedication of the temple: The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You; how much less this house that I have built! (1 Kings 8:27). Stephen, before the council, says the Most High does not dwell in houses made by hands, and quotes these verses from the Greek (Acts 7:48–50).

  • vv2, 5 "trembles at My word" — chared, "trembling." The same word names the faithful in Ezra's day: everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel (Ezra 9:4; also 10:3). Here those who tremble are cast out by their own brothers (v5).

  • v3 "Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who kills a man" — the Hebrew sets each pair side by side with no word between: slaughtering the ox, striking a man; sacrificing the lamb, breaking a dog's neck. Read with as, which the Greek has, the offering of one who is not poor and broken in spirit (v2) counts as murder and as an unclean sacrifice. Without as, the same people do both, bringing the LORD's offerings and the rites of 65:3–4 together. Breaking the neck is the verb of the law for the firstling donkey that is not redeemed (Exodus 13:13).

  • v4 "because when I called, no one answered" — the charge of 65:12, said there to them, you did not answer, and here said of them.

  • vv7–9 "she delivered a male child… Shall I bring to the mouth of the womb and not bring to birth?" — ashbir, from mashber, the word of Hezekiah's message in the siege, The children have come to the mouth of the womb, and there is no strength to give birth (37:3). The LORD answers with the same picture: what He brings to the point of birth, He delivers. John sees a woman who gave birth to a son, a male child, who is to shepherd all the nations with a rod of iron (Revelation 12:5).

  • vv11–13 "carried on the hip… As one whom his mother comforts" — the daughters carried on the hip (60:4), and the peace like a river that Israel would have had (48:18), now come. The LORD, who said a mother may forget her nursing child, yet I will not forget you (49:15), here is the mother; comfort, three times in v13, is the word of 40:1, Comfort, comfort My people.

  • v17 "following one in the middle… the flesh of pigs, loathsome things and mice" — the read form is achat, "one" (a woman); the written form is achad, "one" (a man): someone leads the rite in the middle of the garden. The pig and the mouse are both unclean in the law (Leviticus 11:7, 29).

  • v18 "As for Me, I know their works and their thoughts" — the Hebrew has no verb: And I — their works and their thoughts — it is coming, to gather all nations. I know is supplied; the Greek has no verb there either.

  • vv19–21 "Tarshish, Pul and Lud… Tubal and Javan… covered wagons… some of them" — the far peoples of Genesis 10, where Javan and Tubal are sons of Japheth (Genesis 10:2); Javan is Greece, and the Greek has Hellas. Where the Hebrew has Pul and who draw the bow, the Greek has Put and Meshech. The covered wagons (tsabbim) are those the chiefs brought for the dwelling (Numbers 7:3). Some of them may be the brothers brought home or the nations who bring them; the Hebrew does not say which.

  • v24 "their worm will not die, and their fire will not be quenched" — Jesus takes these words for the place where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched (Mark 9:48). "An abhorrence" — dera'on, found elsewhere only in Daniel 12:2, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting abhorrence. The book that began with sons who have rebelled against Me (1:2) ends with the men who have rebelled against Me, the same verb.

speech.text: Isaiah 66
Thus says the LORD: Heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool; where is the house you would build for Me, and where is the place of My rest?
All these things My hand has made, and so all these things came to be, declares the LORD. But this is the one I will look to: the one who is poor and broken in spirit, and trembles at My word.

Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who kills a man; whoever sacrifices a lamb, like one who breaks a dog's neck; whoever presents a grain offering, like one who offers pig's blood; whoever burns frankincense as a memorial, like one who blesses an idol. They have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their loathsome things;

so I also will choose harsh treatment for them, and bring on them what they dread; because when I called, no one answered; when I spoke, they did not listen; but they did what was evil in My eyes, and chose what I did not delight in.

Hear the word of the LORD, you who tremble at His word: Your brothers who hate you and cast you out for My name's sake have said, "Let the LORD be glorified, so that we may see your joy"; but they will be put to shame.
A sound of uproar from the city! A sound from the temple! The sound of the LORD, repaying His enemies what they deserve!
Before she was in labor, she gave birth; before her pain came upon her, she delivered a male child.
Who has heard such a thing? Who has seen such things? Can a land be born in one day? Can a nation be brought forth at once? Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her sons.
"Shall I bring to the mouth of the womb and not bring to birth?" says the LORD. "Shall I, who bring to birth, shut the womb?" says your God.
Rejoice with Jerusalem, and be glad for her, all you who love her; rejoice with her in joy, all you who mourn over her,
so that you may nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breast, so that you may drink deeply and delight in her abundant glory.

For thus says the LORD: I am about to extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing stream; and you will nurse; you will be carried on the hip and bounced on the knees.
As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you; you will be comforted in Jerusalem.
You will see, and your heart will rejoice; your bones will flourish like the grass; the hand of the LORD will be known to His servants, and His indignation to His enemies.
For the LORD will come in fire, and His chariots like the whirlwind, to pay back His anger in fury, and His rebuke in flames of fire.
For by fire the LORD will enter into judgment, and by His sword, with all flesh; and those slain by the LORD will be many.
Those who consecrate and purify themselves to go into the gardens, following one in the middle, who eat the flesh of pigs, loathsome things and mice, will come to an end together, declares the LORD.
As for Me, I know their works and their thoughts; the time is coming to gather all nations and tongues; and they will come and see My glory.

I will set a sign among them, and I will send survivors from them to the nations: to Tarshish, Pul and Lud, who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, to the far coastlands that have not heard of My fame or seen My glory; and they will declare My glory among the nations.

They will bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the LORD, on horses, in chariots, in covered wagons, on mules and on swift camels, to My holy mountain Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the sons of Israel bring their offering in a clean vessel to the house of the LORD.
I will also take some of them for priests and for Levites, says the LORD.
For as the new heavens and the new earth that I am making will remain before Me, declares the LORD, so your offspring and your name will remain.
From new moon to new moon, and from sabbath to sabbath, all flesh will come to worship before Me, says the LORD.
They will go out and look on the corpses of the men who have rebelled against Me; for their worm will not die, and their fire will not be quenched, and they will be an abhorrence to all flesh.
